**Jonathan Dwight Jones**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-Jonesfullname-1) (born July 19, 1987)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERDOGSTAT1-2) is an American former professional [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") who competed from 2008 to 2025. During his career with the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC), he was a two-time [Light Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship"), holding the title from 2011 to 2015 and again from 2018 to 2020, and held the [Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship") from 2023 to 2025. He also held the [interim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interim_championship "Interim championship") Light Heavyweight Championship in 2016.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERDOGSTAT1-2) He is regarded as one of the greatest mixed martial artists of all time.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-17)

Jones became the [youngest champion in UFC history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_records#Youngest_champions "List of UFC records") with his light heavyweight title victory over [Maurício Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua") at age 23.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-YOUNGEST1-18) He holds many UFC records in the [light heavyweight division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_heavyweight_(MMA) "Light heavyweight (MMA)"), including the [most title defenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_records#Longest_combined_title_reigns_-_By_division "List of UFC records"), [most wins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_records#Most_wins_-_By_division "List of UFC records"), and longest win streak.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-light-heavyweight-division-205-pound-limit-19) He has also defeated nine different former undisputed UFC champions, the most in history.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:18-20) During much of his championship reign, Jones was widely considered to be the best [pound-for-pound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_for_pound "Pound for pound") fighter in the world and spent a record 1,743 days as the UFC's [#1 pound-for-pound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_records#Men's_longest_combined_pound-for-pound_reign "List of UFC records") fighter.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-light-heavyweight-division-205-pound-limit-19) Never stopped nor outscored during his career, Jones's only professional loss is a controversial disqualification against [Matt Hamill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Hamill "Matt Hamill"); a result disputed by Hamill and UFC president [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-21)

Between 2015 and 2017, Jones was involved in several controversies and lost his light heavyweight title three times as a result of disciplinary action.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-aftermath-22) He was first stripped of his title and removed from the official rankings by the UFC in 2015 after he was arrested on felony [hit-and-run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit-and-run "Hit-and-run") charges.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-aftermath-22) His subsequent returns to the UFC in 2016 and 2017 saw him emerge victorious in title bouts against [Ovince Saint Preux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovince_Saint_Preux "Ovince Saint Preux") and [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier"), but were both cut short by Jones [testing positive for banned substances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_sport "Doping in sport") and receiving further suspensions, with the latter reversed to a [no contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_contest_(combat_sports) "No contest (combat sports)").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-aftermath-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-23) After his 2017 suspension was lifted, Jones reclaimed the championship by defeating [Alexander Gustafsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Gustafsson "Alexander Gustafsson") in 2018, which he held until voluntarily vacating it in 2020.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-cbssports.com-24)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-28) Jones spent three years away from MMA before returning in 2023 to win the heavyweight title against [Ciryl Gane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciryl_Gane "Ciryl Gane") and holding it until his 2025 retirement.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-Raimondi_2023-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-31) He was the eighth UFC fighter to win titles in two different weight classes and the fourth to defend titles in two different divisions.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-32)

## Early life

Jones was born on July 19, 1987, in [Rochester, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York"). At the age of 10, he relocated with his family to the [Binghamton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binghamton,_New_York "Binghamton, New York") area.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-33) His father Arthur is a [pastor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastor "Pastor") at Mount Sinai Church of God in Christ in Binghamton, New York.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:1-34) Growing up, family life revolved around church, and Jones even sang in the church choir.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-35) Arthur discouraged Jon's fighting career, "I wanted him to preach. I tried to discourage him from being a fighter. I told him you don't want to do that. You can do other things. Be a pastor."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:1-34) Jon's mother, Camille, died in 2017 at the age of 55, after a long battle with [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-36)

Jon was one of four children.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SI-37) His older brother [Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Jones_(American_football) "Arthur Jones (American football)") and younger brother [Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandler_Jones "Chandler Jones") both played in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) as [defensive ends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_end "Defensive end").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-38) His older sister, Carmen, died of a [brain tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_tumor "Brain tumor") before her 18th birthday.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SI-37)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-YouTube.com-39)

## Background

### High school

Before beginning his MMA career, Jones was a stand-out high school [wrestler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling "Wrestling") at [Union-Endicott High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union-Endicott_High_School "Union-Endicott High School") in [Endicott, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endicott,_New_York "Endicott, New York").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-jonesnewcomer-40) As a junior in 2004, he won the Northeast Junior Greco‑Roman Regional Championship at 189-pounds and was named Most Outstanding Wrestler at the event.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-41) That year, he also won the STAC Wrestling Championship and placed third at the [NYSPHSAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Public_High_School_Athletic_Association "New York State Public High School Athletic Association") Division I state championships.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:10-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:11-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:12-44) As a senior in 2005, he captured the NYSPHSAA Division I state title at 189-pounds, and was named an NHSCA Senior All‑American.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:13-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:14-46) Over the course of his high school career, he was a two-time Section IV champion.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:15-47) He also played football as a defensive lineman; due to his slight frame, his coach nicknamed him "Bones".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-48)

### College

As a freshman at [Iowa Central Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_Central_Community_College "Iowa Central Community College"), Jones won a [NJCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NJCAA "NJCAA") wrestling national championship, helped secure the overall team championship, and was named an All-American.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-jonesnewcomer-40)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:7-50) After transferring to [Morrisville State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrisville_State_College "Morrisville State College")[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-51) to study Criminal Justice, he dropped out of college to begin his MMA career.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERDOGINT-52)

## Mixed martial arts career

### Early career

Jones made his professional MMA debut in April 2008.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-jonesnewcomer-40) He amassed an undefeated record of 6–0 over a period of three months, finishing all of his opponents. In his last bout before signing with the UFC, Jones defeated Moyses Gabin at BCX 5 for the USKBA Light Heavyweight Championship.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-jonesnewcomer-40) He won the fight via TKO in the second round.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-BATCAGE1-53)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

#### Debut and rise to contender status

Jones made his UFC debut against [André Gusmão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_Gusm%C3%A3o "André Gusmão") at [UFC 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_87 "UFC 87") on August 9, 2008. Jones had accepted the deal on two weeks' notice as a late replacement for [Tomasz Drwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomasz_Drwal "Tomasz Drwal").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-jonesnewcomer-40) Jones won via unanimous decision (30–27, 29–28, and 30–27), using [takedowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takedown_(grappling) "Takedown (grappling)") and unorthodox striking, such as spinning elbows and a spinning back kick.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-sherdogUFC87-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-mmaj3-55)

In his second UFC match, Jones took on veteran [Stephan Bonnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephan_Bonnar "Stephan Bonnar") at [UFC 94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_94 "UFC 94") on January 31, 2009. Jones won the fight by unanimous decision.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-sherdogUFC94-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-mmaj4-57)

Jones's third fight was against [Jake O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_O'Brien_(fighter) "Jake O'Brien (fighter)") at [UFC 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_100 "UFC 100")[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC100-58) on July 11, 2009. Jones won via submission.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-60) In September 2009, Jones was rewarded for his victories by signing a new, four-fight contract with the UFC.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-FIVKNU1-61)

On December 5, 2009, Jones fought fellow [light heavyweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_heavyweight_(MMA) "Light heavyweight (MMA)") prospect [Matt Hamill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Hamill "Matt Hamill") at [The Ultimate Fighter: Heavyweights Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Heavyweights_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: Heavyweights Finale"). Jones used his wrestling to dominate Hamill, but was disqualified for the use of illegal [12–6 elbows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12%E2%80%936_elbow "12–6 elbow").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-YAHOODQ1-62) The [Unified Rules of Mixed Martial Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts_rules#Unified_Rules_of_Mixed_Martial_Arts "Mixed martial arts rules") prohibited downward elbow strikes, and Jones was initially only penalized a point from the round. However, Hamill was unable to continue due to his dislocated shoulder.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-63) Consequently, the replay simulation was reviewed, and showed that Jones's elbows further damaged Hamill's already bloody and lacerated nose. This marked the first time that Nevada had used its recently enacted instant replay rule, in which the referee's decision was supported by the commission, which utilized a slow-motion replay to review the elbows.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-64) UFC president [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") was aggrieved that referee Steve Mazagatti ruled the bout as a [disqualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts_rules "Mixed martial arts rules"), which resulted in a loss for Jones, saying that it should have been a [no contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_contest_(combat_sports) "No contest (combat sports)").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-65) In 2019, White said he was still attempting to have the result overturned to a no contest by the [Nevada State Athletic Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Athletic_Commission "Nevada State Athletic Commission").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-66)

Jones fought [Brandon Vera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Vera "Brandon Vera") on March 21, 2010, at [UFC Live: Vera vs. Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Live:_Vera_vs._Jones "UFC Live: Vera vs. Jones").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-67) Jones won the fight by TKO.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-68) The elbow delivered to stop the fight also broke Vera's face in three places.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-69) Jones also won the "Knockout of the Night" award.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERKOBONUS1-70)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Jon_%22Bones%22_Jones_%26_Glen_%22Big_Baby%22_Davis.jpg/250px-Jon_%22Bones%22_Jones_%26_Glen_%22Big_Baby%22_Davis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jon_%22Bones%22_Jones_&_Glen_%22Big_Baby%22_Davis.jpg)

Jones and basketball player [Glen Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Davis_(basketball) "Glen Davis (basketball)") in 2010

Jones defeated former [IFL Light Heavyweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IFL_champions#Light_Heavyweight_Championship "List of IFL champions") Champion [Vladimir Matyushenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Matyushenko "Vladimir Matyushenko") by TKO with elbows in 1:52 of the first round on August 1, 2010, at [UFC Live: Jones vs. Matyushenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Live:_Jones_vs._Matyushenko "UFC Live: Jones vs. Matyushenko").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-71) Dana White promised Jones a "huge step-up in the competition", if he managed to defeat Matyushenko.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-72) Following the match with Matyushenko, White said, "Vladimir Matyushenko is a guy who I have a lot of respect for and I didn't think it was going to happen that easy. Jones is the real deal and he just catapulted himself tonight into the top eight in the world. Tonight solidified it. ... He's got to keep his head together, stay focused and keep doing all the right things in training. He's smart, good looking and bad-ass. He's going to make a lot of money—this kid is going to do very well."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-73)

After defeating Matyushenko, Jones stated that he wanted a "top-three opponent" for his next fight.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-74) Jones mentioned in an interview with _[Inside MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_MMA "Inside MMA")_ that he would be facing the winner of [Antônio Rogério Nogueira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Rog%C3%A9rio_Nogueira "Antônio Rogério Nogueira") vs. [Ryan Bader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Bader "Ryan Bader").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-MANIAQQ1-75) Reports that Jones had previously been offered a match with Nogueira, but turned it down,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-76) turned out to be false.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-77) In the _Inside MMA_ interview, Jones also stated that he had been informed by Dana White and [Lorenzo Fertitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_Fertitta "Lorenzo Fertitta") that if he finished his next two fights, he would likely receive a title shot.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-MANIAQQ1-75)

White soon confirmed that Jones would face the undefeated _[Ultimate Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Fighter\_8 "The Ultimate Fighter 8")_ winner Ryan Bader, on February 5, 2011, at [UFC 126](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_126 "UFC 126").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-78) Jones handed Bader his first professional loss by defeating him via submission due to a [guillotine choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillotine_choke "Guillotine choke") in the second round after dominating Bader in the first round. Jones was awarded the "Submission of the Night" bonus.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERSUBBONUS1-79)

#### Light Heavyweight Champion

Immediately after the bout with Bader, it was revealed that title contender and Jones's training partner [Rashad Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashad_Evans "Rashad Evans") had sustained a knee injury in training, and would not be able to compete in his scheduled match with UFC light heavyweight champion [Maurício "Shogun" Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua"). Jones was told by [Joe Rogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Rogan "Joe Rogan") in the post-fight interview that he would replace Evans in the fight for the [UFC Light Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-RuaJones-80) On March 19, 2011, at [UFC 128](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_128 "UFC 128"), Jones defeated Rua by TKO at 2:37 of Round 3, becoming the youngest ever UFC champion. After an early flying knee that badly hurt the champion, Shogun was dominated throughout the three rounds. A body shot and knee to the head dropped the champion to his knees, causing the referee to step in and halt the match.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHER128PBP-81)

Jones's first title defense was expected to be on August 6, 2011, at [UFC 133](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_133 "UFC 133") against [Rashad Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashad_Evans "Rashad Evans"),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-82) his former friend and teammate,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-83) but Jones was sidelined with a hand injury.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-84) It was initially announced that the hand injury would require surgery, but Jones opted for rest and rehabilitation without surgery after further consultations with doctors.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-85) Jones's injury was originally thought to keep him out of action until late 2011,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-86) but he instead made his first title defense against [Quinton Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampage_Jackson "Rampage Jackson") on September 24, 2011, at [UFC 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_135 "UFC 135"). Jones defeated Jackson via [rear naked choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_naked_choke "Rear naked choke") submission at 1:14 in the 4th round.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-87) In the process, he became the first UFC fighter to submit Jackson. In 2012, Jones said that this was his favorite fight up to that point.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-88)

Jones vs. Evans was in the works for a second time, and a bout was targeted for December 10, 2011, at [UFC 140](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_140 "UFC 140").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-89) However, a lingering thumb injury cost another title opportunity for Evans, and Jones instead faced [Lyoto Machida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyoto_Machida "Lyoto Machida") at the same event.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-90) Jones successfully defended the light heavyweight title at UFC 140, stopping Machida at 4:26 of the second round via [guillotine choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillotine_choke "Guillotine choke")[technical submission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submission_(combat_sports)#Technical_submission "Submission (combat sports)").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-91) This was the first submission loss in Machida's career.

Jones faced his arch rival and former teammate [Rashad Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashad_Evans "Rashad Evans") on April 21, 2012, at [UFC 145](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_145 "UFC 145"), and won via unanimous decision (49–46, 49–46, and 50–45).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-92) During the UFC 145 post fight press conference, [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") confirmed that Jones's next opponent would be [Dan Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Henderson "Dan Henderson").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-93) The Jones-Henderson fight was expected to take place at [UFC 151](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_151 "UFC 151"), but Henderson pulled out of the bout due to injuries.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-95) Jones then refused a late replacement fight with [Chael Sonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chael_Sonnen "Chael Sonnen") after his coach Greg Jackson told him with three training days left, it would be difficult to prepare.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-96) UFC 151 was then subsequently canceled, the first cancelation in the company's 19-year history.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-97)

Jones's decision to decline the fight against Sonnen was criticized by UFC president Dana White, who said, "This is one of the most selfish, disgusting decisions that doesn't just affect you. This is affecting 16 other lives, their families, kids are going back to school. The list goes on and on of all the things, the money that was spent for fighters to train and the list goes on and on. Like I said, I don't think this is going to make Jon Jones popular with the fans, sponsors, cable distributors, television network executives or other fighters."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-98) However, Jones was defended by MMA analysts, who criticized White for promoting a thin card.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-99) It was later reported that Henderson was injured three weeks prior to the announcement, but kept the injury under wraps as he was still hoping to compete.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-100)

A rematch with [Lyoto Machida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyoto_Machida "Lyoto Machida") was then announced for September 22, 2012, at [UFC 152](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_152 "UFC 152").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-101) Lyoto Machida, who was not contacted prior to the announcement, rejected the fight due to the lack of time to train before the bout.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-102) Jones, instead, defended the championship against [Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") on September 22, 2012, at [UFC 152](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_152 "UFC 152").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-BELFORT-103) Jones opened as a massive favorite (13-to-1) coming into the bout.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-BELFORT-103)

> [I]t was not the finish that's the story of this evening. It's the refusal to be finished.

—Jeff Wagenheim on Jones' submission victory over [Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") at [UFC 152](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_152 "UFC 152")[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-104)

Despite almost being submitted via [armbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armbar "Armbar") in round one, Jones successfully defended the belt against Belfort via [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armlock#Top_shoulder_lock "Armlock") submission in round four,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-106) and equaled [Chuck Liddell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Liddell "Chuck Liddell")'s number of title defenses.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-108) Jones also won a $65,000 _Submission of the Night_ bonus for his finish of Belfort.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-SHERSUBBONUS2-109)

Jones was chosen to coach opposite [Chael Sonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chael_Sonnen "Chael Sonnen") on [Season 17 of the Ultimate Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Team_Jones_vs._Team_Sonnen "The Ultimate Fighter: Team Jones vs. Team Sonnen"). With a bout between the coaches taking place on April 27, 2013, at [UFC 159](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_159 "UFC 159").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-110) Jones displayed a lack of interest in the bout and actively downplayed the contest, making it clear that he did not believe Sonnen was a fit contender. In an interview, Sonnen did his best to garner interest in the bout, but Jones gave him the "[silent treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_treatment "Silent treatment")", and refused to make eye contact.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-111) Jones made quick work of his challenger, finishing Sonnen via TKO in the first round. However, he broke the [phalanx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phalanges_of_the_foot "Phalanges of the foot") (big toe) on his left foot during the fight.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-113)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-115) With the win, Jones tied [Tito Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Ortiz "Tito Ortiz") for having most consecutive title defenses in UFC light heavyweight history.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-116)

Jones faced [Alexander Gustafsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Gustafsson "Alexander Gustafsson") on September 21, 2013, at [UFC 165](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_165 "UFC 165").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC165-117) Jones was badly cut above the eye during the first round,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-118) but he won the back-and-forth fight via unanimous decision (48–47, 48–47, and 49–46). After the match, Jones said Gustafsson gave him the toughest fight of his career, and both were sent to the hospital for their injuries.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-119) Both men suffered lacerations and facial swelling, but were released from the hospital with no broken bones or serious injuries.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-121) The bout earned both fighters the _Fight of the Night_ bonus award.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-122) The match received numerous positive reviews: "an epic battle",[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-124) "instant-classic",[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-125) "Fight of the Year",[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-126) "Greatest light heavyweight title fight of all-time",[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-127) "one of the greatest fights in UFC history".[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-128) On March 8, 2020, it was announced that the fight will be inducted to UFC Hall of Fame's Fight Wing on July 9.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-hoftweet-129)

Jones was expected to take on [Glover Teixeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glover_Teixeira "Glover Teixeira") on February 1, 2014, at [UFC 169](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_169 "UFC 169").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-130) However, on October 7, UFC President Dana White stated that the announcement for this fight on that card was premature and that Jones and Teixeira would face each other on a different card.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-131) On November 13, 2013, it was announced that Jones would fight Teixeira at [UFC 170](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_170 "UFC 170"), scheduled for February 22, 2014;[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-132) however, the next day it was announced that the match had been removed from the card.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-133) On December 4, 2013, it was announced that Jones and Teixeira would face each other at [UFC 171](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_171 "UFC 171") on March 15, 2014, in [Dallas, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas,_Texas "Dallas, Texas");[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-134) however, the fight was moved again. Jones and Teixeira finally fought on April 26, 2014, at [UFC 172](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_172 "UFC 172").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC172-135) Jones won the bout via unanimous decision (50–45, 50–45, and 50–45).[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-136)

On April 27, 2014, UFC President [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") confirmed that Jones would next have a rematch against Gustafsson, and stated the possibility of the match taking place in a stadium in Sweden on pay-per-view.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-138) On May 24, 2014, it was indicated that the rematch would take place in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") on August 30, 2014, at [UFC 177](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_177 "UFC 177").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-139) The statement, and the time and venue, was not official, however, because Gustafsson was the only one who still had agreed to accept the match.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-141) On June 2, the fight was still on hold, and White explained the situation as "Jones doesn't want to fight Gustafsson", and instead expressed his preference for fighting [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier").[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-144)

On June 5, 2014, the UFC confirmed that the Jones vs. Gustafsson rematch would take place on September 27, 2014, at [UFC 178](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_178 "UFC 178").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC178-145) However, Gustafsson had to pull out of the match due to a torn meniscus. Jones was then expected to take on replacement [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier") at [UFC 178](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_178 "UFC 178").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-146) On August 12, 2014, it was announced that Jones had sustained a leg injury in training, causing him to withdraw. The bout was rescheduled, and eventually took place on January 3, 2015, at [UFC 182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_182 "UFC 182").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-147) Jones won the fight by unanimous decision (49–46, 49–46, and 49–46).[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-148) He also became the first person to take Cormier down, scoring three takedowns in total. The win also earned Jones his fourth _Fight of the Night_ bonus award.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-149) It was later revealed that Jones had failed a drug test one month prior to the event, as he tested positive for [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"). (see below in #Controversies)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-Cocaine-150)

#### First suspension and return

Jones was expected to defend his title against [Anthony Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Johnson_(fighter) "Anthony Johnson (fighter)") on May 23, 2015, at [UFC 187](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_187 "UFC 187").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-151) However, on April 28, Jones was stripped of the belt and suspended from the UFC indefinitely in connection with a hit-and-run incident where he crashed into a pregnant woman then fled the scene on foot.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-152) Cormier, who lost against Jones at UFC 182 in January 2015, replaced him and went on to defeat Anthony Johnson to take the vacant UFC Light Heavyweight Championship.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-153)

On October 23, 2015, the UFC announced that Jones had been reinstated to the active roster, nearly six months after his suspension was announced.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-154) A rematch with Cormier was expected to take place on April 23, 2016, at [UFC 197](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_197 "UFC 197").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-155) However, Cormier pulled out of the fight on April 1, citing a foot injury, and was replaced by [Ovince Saint Preux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovince_Saint_Preux "Ovince Saint Preux").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-156)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-157) Jones defeated Saint Preux by unanimous decision (50–44, 50–45, and 50–45).[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-158)

#### Second suspension and return

The rematch with Cormier was rescheduled and expected to take place on July 9, 2016, at [UFC 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_200 "UFC 200").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-ME200-159) However, on July 6, 2016, Jones was removed from the bout by USADA on June 16 after a potential doping violation.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-160) On November 7, 2016, it was announced that Jones had been suspended for one year by USADA, retroactive to July 7.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-161) Two days later, it was announced that Jones had been stripped of his interim title, making him the first fighter in UFC history to be stripped of a title twice.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-162) On December 15, Jones was also suspended by the [Nevada State Athletic Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_Athletic_Commission "Nevada Athletic Commission") (NSAC) for one year.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-163)

While on the sidelines, Jones fought retired MMA veteran [Dan Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Henderson "Dan Henderson") in a grappling match for the Submission Underground 2 tournament on December 10, 2016. After an even start, Jones eventually submitted Henderson with an arm-triangle choke six minutes into the bout. Following the fight, Jones expressed interest in competing against [Chael Sonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chael_Sonnen "Chael Sonnen").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-164)

#### Third suspension and return

The rematch with [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier") took place on July 29, 2017, at [UFC 214](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_214 "UFC 214") at the [Honda Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Center "Honda Center") in [Anaheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). Jones won the fight and re-captured the UFC Light Heavyweight Championship via knockout in the third round.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-165) After the fight, Jones was awarded a _Performance of the Night_ bonus.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-166) After the fight, Jones praised Cormier as a "model champion", while recognizing his own personal failings. He then challenged [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") to a fight.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-167) On August 22, it was announced that Jones had been flagged for a potential doping violation by [USADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USADA "USADA"), stemming from his sample that was collected after weigh-ins July 28. He tested positive for [Turinabol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turinabol "Turinabol"), an [anabolic steroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabolic_steroid "Anabolic steroid"). Jones was placed on a provisional suspension as a result.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-aftermath-22) On September 13, USADA confirmed that both the "A" and "B" sample of Jones's tested positive for Turinabol.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-168) As a result, the California State Athletic Commission (CSAC) officially overturned the result of the fight to a [no contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_contest_(combat_sports) "No contest (combat sports)"). Subsequently, UFC President Dana White made the decision to strip him of the Light Heavyweight championship, and return it to Daniel Cormier.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-169)

In September 2018, it was announced by USADA that Jones would serve a suspension of 15 months. From a potential suspension of 48 months USADA applied a reduction of 30 months for Jones's co-operation in identifying other anti-doping offences, and a further 3 months was applied by arbitrators McLaren in relation to Jones's degree of fault.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-170)

#### Second UFC Light Heavyweight Championship reign

On October 10, 2018, it was announced that Jones would return at [UFC 232](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_232 "UFC 232") on December 29, 2018, in a rematch with [Alexander Gustafsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Gustafsson "Alexander Gustafsson") for the vacant [UFC Light Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-171) Jones defeated Gustafsson by technical knockout in the third round to win the UFC Light Heavyweight Championship.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-172)

In the first defense of his second championship reign, Jones faced [Anthony Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Smith_(fighter) "Anthony Smith (fighter)") on March 2, 2019, in the main event at [UFC 235](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_235 "UFC 235").[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-173) Jones dominated the fight, but was deducted two points in the fourth round after landing an illegal knee to Smith's head. He won the fight via unanimous decision with 48–44 on all three judges' scorecards.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-174)

Jones faced [Thiago Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Santos "Thiago Santos") on July 6, 2019, in the main event at [UFC 239](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_239 "UFC 239").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-twotitles-175) He won the back-and-forth match via split decision (48–47, 47–48, and 48–47), defending his title for the second time.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-cbssports.com-24)

Jones faced [Dominick Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominick_Reyes "Dominick Reyes") on February 8, 2020, in the main event of [UFC 247](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_247 "UFC 247").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-Jonesvs.Reyes-176) Jones won the fight via controversial unanimous decision (48–47, 48–47, and 49–46).[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-177) Of the 21 media scorecards tracked by MMAdecisions.com, 14 scored the contest for Reyes, while seven favored Jones.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-178) With this win, Jones set the new record for most wins in UFC title fight history with 14 wins.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-newrecord-179)

#### Disagreement with the UFC and move to heavyweight

After conflict with UFC President [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") over pay in May 2020, Jones said he had vacated the [UFC Light Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-mmajunkie.usatoday.com-25) Jones was targeting a fight with heavyweight contender [Francis Ngannou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ngannou "Francis Ngannou") and, according to White, wanted "[Deontay Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deontay_Wilder "Deontay Wilder") money", referring to Wilder's reported $25–30 million earnings in his [rematch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deontay_Wilder_vs._Tyson_Fury_II "Deontay Wilder vs. Tyson Fury II") with [Tyson Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Fury "Tyson Fury") held in February 2020.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-ReferenceA-26) On August 15, 2020, Jones announced on social media that he would be relinquishing the Light Heavyweight Championship, as well expressing his desire to move up to heavyweight.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-ReferenceB-27)

#### Heavyweight Champion

After over three years removed from his last bout, Jones faced [Ciryl Gane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciryl_Gane "Ciryl Gane") for the vacant [UFC Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship") on March 4, 2023, at [UFC 285](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_285 "UFC 285").[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-180) He won the bout and earned the title via a [guillotine choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillotine_choke "Guillotine choke") submission in the first round.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-182) After the fight, Jones earned the _Performance of the Night_ bonus award.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC285POTN-183) Jones became the third fighter to win UFC titles at heavyweight and light heavyweight, following Randy Couture and Daniel Cormier.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-184)

Jones was scheduled to defend his title against former two-time heavyweight champion [Stipe Miocic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_Miocic "Stipe Miocic") on November 11, 2023, at [UFC 295](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_295 "UFC 295").[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-185) However, Jones was forced to pull out due to injury after tearing a pectoral tendon.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-186) As a result, a bout for the interim UFC Heavyweight Championship between Sergei Pavlovich and [Tom Aspinall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Aspinall "Tom Aspinall") was scheduled for the event. Aspinall won via first-round knockout to become the interim champion.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-187)

One year after his injury, the bout between Jones and Miocic was rescheduled to November 16, 2024, at [UFC 309](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_309 "UFC 309").[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-188) He won the fight by technical knockout via a spinning back kick followed by punches in the third round.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-189) With this twelfth title defense, Jones broke the record for most title defenses in UFC history.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-title12-190) This fight earned him another _[Performance of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_UFC\_bonus\_award\_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients")_ award.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-UFC309-191)

Following the removal of [Clay Guida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Guida "Clay Guida") from the UFC roster on January 15, 2025,[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-192) Jones became the promotion's longest-tenured fighter.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-193)

### Retirement

Following his title defense against Miocic, Jones expressed disinterest in fighting interim [UFC Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship")[Tom Aspinall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Aspinall "Tom Aspinall"), instead calling out then [UFC Light Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Champion "UFC Light Heavyweight Champion")[Alex Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Pereira "Alex Pereira") for a superfight.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-194) At the post-fight press conference of [UFC on ABC: Hill vs. Rountree Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ABC:_Hill_vs._Rountree_Jr. "UFC on ABC: Hill vs. Rountree Jr.") on June 21, 2025, [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") announced that Jones had retired from mixed martial arts competition and that Aspinall was the new undisputed champion as a result.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-195)

On July 4, 2025, the day after [UFC White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_White_House "UFC White House") was announced, Jones said he re-entered the testing pool and is listed as active on the official UFC website.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-:8-196) On March 9, 2026, after the White House card was announced and Jones was not on it, he requested his release from the UFC.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-197)

## Training

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/John_Jones_kick.gif/250px-John_Jones_kick.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Jones_kick.gif)

Jon Jones kicking a punching bag in training

Jones has trained with Team BombSquad out of [Cortland, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortland,_New_York "Cortland, New York"), then briefly with the Tristar Gym in [Montreal, Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal,_Canada "Montreal, Canada"), and most recently at [Jackson's MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jackson_(MMA_trainer) "Greg Jackson (MMA trainer)") in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico").[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-216) He has also trained in [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") with trainer Patrick O'Connor.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-217)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-218) During his suspension from the UFC, he trained as a [power-lifter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerlifting "Powerlifting").[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-219)

Jones's training emphasizes versatility, strength, and technical mastery, ensuring he remains dominant. His regimen includes a combination of wrestling drills, striking practice, grappling sessions, and high-intensity functional training, all designed to enhance his overall fight game.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-220) To refine his striking and transitions, Jones incorporates pad work, sparring, and clinch drills into his routine. His training also features explosive strength exercises, plyometrics, and agility drills, which boost his speed and power.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-221)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Jake_Mattews_%26_Jon_Jones.jpg/250px-Jake_Mattews_%26_Jon_Jones.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jake_Mattews_&_Jon_Jones.jpg)

Jones and [Jake Matthews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Matthews_(fighter) "Jake Matthews (fighter)") after a training session

During training camps, Jones trains six days a week, balancing intense workouts with active recovery sessions. As the fight nears, he reduces the intensity to give his body time to fully recover. He shifts his focus to honing technical precision and engages in lighter sparring, ensuring he enters the fight in optimal physical and mental condition.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-222)

## Fighting style

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/USMC-101022-M-6664G-732.jpg/250px-USMC-101022-M-6664G-732.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USMC-101022-M-6664G-732.jpg)

Jon Jones posing with Marines at [Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Pendleton "Camp Pendleton") in 2010

Jones has been described as "one of the most dynamic, innovative, and constantly evolving fighters in the history of MMA"[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-223) and "perhaps the greatest martial artist ever to step into an octagon".[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-devel-224) Jones capitalizes on his long range and defensive wrestling to land blows in an unorthodox style.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-eleven-225)

He employs a diverse kicking technique, favoring [front kicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_kick "Front kick") to the body and head, [roundhouse kicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundhouse_kick "Roundhouse kick") to the legs and upper body, and his most known technique, the "oblique kick", a controversial move that targets his opponent's knee.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-eleven-225)[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-kickers-226) The oblique kick was a technique popularized by [Bruce Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Lee "Bruce Lee"),[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-227) whom Jones cited as an inspiration.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-228)

Jones also excels in the [clinch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinch_(grappling) "Clinch (grappling)"), where he is skilled at controlling his opponent's arms and scoring elbow and knee strikes.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-devel-224) He is particularly known for his spinning elbow, which has been clocked at over 900 degrees per second.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-229)[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-230) He uses [Greco-Roman wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Roman_wrestling "Greco-Roman wrestling")[takedowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takedown_(grappling) "Takedown (grappling)") like lateral drops from [overhooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overhook "Overhook"),[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-231) as well as a variety of [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo")[throws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throw_(grappling) "Throw (grappling)"), like [osoto gari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osotogari "Osotogari"), [harai goshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harai_goshi "Harai goshi") and [deashi harai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deashi_harai "Deashi harai"), which he claims he picked up by watching them on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-232) Jones has been praised for his positional control and ability to find openings for punches and elbow strikes on the ground.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-devel-224)

## Controversies

### Eye pokes

Jones has been criticized for repeatedly [poking his opponents in the eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_poke "Eye poke"). In response to the criticism, Jones released a video on Instagram in April 2014 in which he mocked fans by simulating crying and saying "Jones put his finger in his eye. Dirtiest fighter in MMA." After backlash towards the post, Jones deleted it from his account.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-272)

When asked about the controversy, UFC president Dana White stated, "we've got to stop that stuff. The openings of the hands and putting the hands on the face are something bad, but it happens with guys who have reach. They do that a lot."[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-273) White clarified his position in another interview, saying, "It's not just taller fighters. Jones has that range and he can do it, but lots of guys do it because that's how you block punches. So you keep your hands open and you slap punches down. Then guys are rushing in and you're doing whatever, and guys get poked in the eyes." White also noted that in the fight against Glover Teixeira, after Jones was warned about the behavior, he was more careful to avoid any eye pokes throughout the rest of the match, a move he claimed Jones "would not [be] credited for" from detractors.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-274)

Jones later said in an interview, "I realize that I do it. I realize the criticism that I got from it. It's not on purpose. If you watch my fights, it's me extending my arm in a reactionary way. I do put a hand on people's foreheads to maintain distance. That's what you saw [against] Teixeira, but to say I am purposely poking people in the eye, it's just inaccurate."[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-275) In 2017, the Unified Rules were amended to prohibit extension of a fighter's fingers towards the eyes of an opponent.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-276)

### Daniel Cormier altercation

During a promotional event for UFC 178, on August 4, 2014, Jones and [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier") briefly scuffled during an on-stage staredown, initiated by Jones pressing his forehead against Cormier's forehead, prompting Cormier to shove Jones by the throat, to which Jones responded by throwing a punch.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-277) Both fighters were restrained by coaches and event organizers. Later that day during a press conference, Cormier expressed a desire to spit in Jones' face, to which Jones responded by threatening to kill Cormier.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-278) UFC chief legal officer Kirk Hendrick said "there are going to be ramifications". In addition, the Nevada State Athletic Commission requested a video copy of the altercation.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-279) On September 23, 2014, Jones was fined $50,000 and was ordered to undergo 40 hours of community service by the [Nevada Athletic Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Athletic_Commission "Nevada State Athletic Commission").[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-280) During the disciplinary hearing, Jones claimed to have lost a six-figure endorsement deal with Nike, but later admitted to fabricating the statement.[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-LostNike1-281)[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-LostNike2-282)

## Legal issues

### Hit-and-run conviction

On April 27, 2015, [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico"), police stated that Jones was sought in connection with a [hit and run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_and_run "Hit and run") early the previous morning. Jones was alleged to have run a red light and crashed his rental car in a collision involving two other vehicles. Jones allegedly fled the scene of the crash on foot, leaving an injured pregnant woman behind in another vehicle. The incident was witnessed by an off-duty police officer who identified the suspect as an African-American man, wearing a white shirt and dark pants, whom he believed to be Jones.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-283)[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Jones#cite_note-284) According to witnesses, the man described as Jones then returned to the scene to grab cash from the vehicle before fleeing again. Paperwork found in the rental car was under the name of "Jonathan Jones". # UFC in the 2014 Home Stretch

 By Von E. Spencer Kyte • Oct. 11, 2014 

Read on for E. Spencer Kyte’s picks of the top 10 fights remaining in 2014...

![Image 1](https://ufc-video.s3.amazonaws.com/image/181/181-dc-poster.jpg)Coming off a stretch where the UFC rolled out 10 events over eight weeks, capped by [Rory MacDonald](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Rory-MacDonald)’s blistering third-round finish of [Tarec Saffiedine](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Tarec-Saffiedine) last Saturday night in Halifax, the current two-week break is a chance to do two things:  
  
(1)Reflect on some of the outstanding fights that have taken place already this year, and  
(2)Look ahead to the collection of terrific matchups that still remain on the schedule.  
  
While we’re inclined to save our thoughts on the best action of 2014 until the year has come to a close, looking at the upcoming schedule and sharing our thoughts on the most intriguing and exciting contests to hit the Octagon as the autumn colors come out and the New Year draws nearer is something entirely different.  
  
We’re fight fans too and just like everyone else, there are a bunch of fights from the final nine events the year that have us eagerly awaiting their arrival.  
  
Here’s our chronological look at the top fights left on the 2014 fight calendar.  
  
**[JOSE ALDO](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Jose-Aldo) VS. [CHAD MENDES](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Chad-Mendes) – UFC 179 (OCTOBER 25)**  
  
This rematch has all the makings of something special – a true grudge match between a dominant champion and a challenger whose only career loss came in their first encounter in 2012.  
  
Mendes appeared on his way to claiming the first round of that bout until Aldo stopped a takedown by hanging onto the cage, spun free and brought the fight to a close with a precise and vicious knee that dropped the Team Alpha Male member.  
  
The champion has looked sharp in successfully defending the featherweight title thrice since that first meeting, while Mendes has taken his game to the next level, showing improved power to compliment his wrestling in winning five consecutive contests heading into this one.  
  
Once again taking place on Aldo’s home turf, Mendes will be looking to bring the Brazilian’s reign to an end, while the champion has designs on a seventh straight championship defense and another celebration amongst the fans Rio.  
  
**[LUKE ROCKHOLD](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Luke-Rockhold) VS. [MICHAEL BISPING](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Michael-Bisping) – [UFC FIGHT NIGHT:](https://www.ufc.com/event/UFC-Silva-vs-Irvin) ROCKHOLD VS. BISPING (NOVEMBER 8)**  
  
These two have been circling each other since before Rockhold made the transition to the UFC following a championship run under the [](https://www.ufc.com/event/SF-Columbus)[](https://www.ufc.com/event/SF-Rockhold-Jardine)[Strikeforce](https://www.ufc.com/event/SF6)banner, and after months of back-and-forth banter, they’re finally sharing the Octagon in early November.  
  
Rockhold has looked outstanding in his last two appearances, earning first-round stoppage wins over [Costas Philippou](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/constantinos-philippou) and [Tim Boetsch](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Tim-Boetsch), while “The Count” is coming off arguably the most dominant performance of his career – a 16-minute thrashing of [Cung Le](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Cung-Le) at the end of August.  
  
As soon as that bout was completed, this one was put together and as soon as it became official, fight fans everywhere circled November 8 on the calendar because the simmering bad blood and animosity between these two is bound to boil over once they hit the Octagon in Sydney.  
  
**[IAN MCCALL](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Ian-McCall) VS. [JOHN LINEKER](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/John-Lineker) – UFC FIGHT NIGHT: SHOGUN VS. MANUWA (NOVEMBER 8)**  
  
This main card contest on the second half of the November 8 doubleheader carries significant championship ramifications, but even without the potential of producing the next flyweight title challenger, the contrasting styles of these two elite 125-pound competitors is enough to make it a must see matchup.  
  
“Uncle Creepy” turned in his most complete performance to date last time out, picking apart veteran [Brad Pickett](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Brad-Pickett) to pick up his second consecutive victory after failing to register a victory in each of his first three UFC appearances. Showing the quickness and clean striking that made him the top flyweight in the world prior to his arrival in the Octgaon, McCall seems to have put the distractions that limited him in the past behind him and set his sights on a third meeting with flyweight champ [Demetrious Johnson](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Demetrious-Johnson).  
  
Lineker enters off a late third-round stoppage win over [Alptekin Ozkilic](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Alptekin-Ozkilic), but it’s the fact that he’s successfully made weight on consecutive occasions that might be more important, as the hard-hitting 24-year-old Brazilian has always been viewed as legitimate threat with blistering power. Now that he appears to have figure out how to hit the 125-pound limit consistently, “Hands of Stone” could be poised to challenge for the title.  
  
**[JAKE ELLENBERGER](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Jake-Ellenberger) VS. [KELVIN GASTELUM](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Kelvin-Gastelum) – UFC 180 (NOVEMBER 15)**  
  
After establishing himself as one of the top prospects in the organization with his upset win over [Uriah Hall](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Uriah-Hall) to win the middleweight competition on Season 17 of [](https://www.ufc.com/event/Ultimate-Fighter-Team-Serra-vs-Team-Hughes-Finale)[](https://www.ufc.com/event/The-Ultimate-Fighter-Team-US-vs-Team-UK-FINALE)[The Ultimate Fighter,](https://www.ufc.com/event/The-Ultimate-Fighter-Heavyweights-FINALE) Gastelum dropped to welterweight and posted a trio of victories to land at No. 11 in the divisional rankings.  
  
Now he gets a chance to make a push for a place in the Top 5 by taking on the perennial contender Ellenberger in the co-main event of the UFC’s debut fight card in Mexico.  
  
While “The Juggernaut” enters on a two-fight losing streak, the 29-year-old veteran has been a Top 10 fixture since arriving in the UFC five years ago and stands as the biggest test to date for the talented young fighter from Yuma, Arizona. If the Nebraska transplant can revert back to the form that saw him win eight of nine following his debut split decision loss to [Carlos Condit](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Carlos-Condit), he should pair with the recent TUF winner to produce another electric contest in the 170-pound weight class.  
  
**[CAIN VELASQUEZ](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Cain-Velasquez) VS. [FABRICIO WERDUM](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Fabricio-Werdum) – UFC 180**  
  
By the time Velasquez hits the Octagon to defend the UFC heavyweight title against Werdum, it will have been 13 months since he cemented his standing atop the division by doling out a second round of punishment to former champ [Junior dos Santos](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Junior-Dos-Santos) at UFC 166.  
  
With everything that has transpired since then, it’s easy to forget how impressive Velasquez was on that night, but the memories should come rushing back once the American Kickboxing Academy product lands his first big right hand or drives through a double leg.  
  
But Velasquez is facing a challenger that is in the best form of his career and has a history of bucking the odds and rewarding those that rolled the dice on the underdog. From his submission win over Fedor Emelianenko to his playful five-round win over [Travis Browne](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Travis-Browne) in April to cement his shot at the belt, Werdum has consistently risen to the occasion and proven his doubters wrong.  
  
If he can do it again next month in Mexico City, he’ll be the new UFC heavyweight champion.  
  
**[FRANKIE EDGAR](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Frankie-Edgar) VS. [CUB SWANSON](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Cub-Swanson) - UFC FIGHT NIGHT: EDGAR VS. SWANSON (NOVEMBER 22)**  
  
With [Conor McGregor](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Conor-McGregor) having made his case for a title shot with his tour de force showing at UFC 178 and Aldo and Mendes ready to battle for the belt later this month, Edgar and Swanson will collide in Austin, Texas, looking to keep “The Notorious” from cutting in line while earning a championship opportunity for themselves in this one.  
  
“The Answer” completely outworked and overwhelmed B.J. Penn in their trilogy bout earlier this year, pushing his winning streak to two and cementing himself as one of the elite contenders in the featherweight division.  
  
Swanson, meanwhile, has been biding his time and piling up wins since losing his UFC debut to [Ricardo Lamas](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Ricardo-Lamas) a little less than three years ago. “Killer Cub” has racked up six consecutive victories in that span, including four straight against fighters ranked in the Top 15. If he can add Edgar to his running total, the Palms Springs native might have too good a case for contention to overlook.  
  
Either way, this one should be an electric back-and-forth between two supremely talented fighters in what is fast becoming one of the most competitive and entertaining divisions in the UFC.  
  
**[ANTHONY PETTIS](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Anthony-Pettis) VS. [GILBERT MELENDEZ](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Gilbert-Melendez) – UFC 181 (DECEMBER 6)**  
  
The wait to see Pettis defend the lightweight title he won from [Benson Henderson](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Benson-Henderson) is just about over, as his showdown with Melendez is officially less than two months away.  
  
“Showtime” might be the most exciting fighter in the sport today – an inventive striker with tremendous finishing instincts and a flare for the dramatic. While injuries and inactivity have limited him to just four appearances over the last three years, the 27-year-old is a perfect 4-0 in those outings, with the last three all ending in the first round.  
  
If Pettis is glitz and shine, Melendez is his counter-balance - a hard-nosed grinder with good hands, strong wrestling and heart for days.  
  
You won’t see “El Nino” running up the cage wall to deliver any kicks, but the former Strikeforce lightweight champion will battle tooth and nail from bell-to-bell, and after coming out on the wrong side of a split decision in his first attempt to capture UFC gold, you can be sure the man from the Bay Area will do everything in his power to make sure this fight doesn’t go to the judges and unquestionably falls in his favor if it does.  
  
**[JOHNY HENDRICKS](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Johny-Hendricks) VS. [ROBBIE LAWLER](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Robbie-Lawler), PART II – UFC 181**  
  
Already the frontrunner for Fight of the Year, the sequel is set to hit the cage before the year is out, moving up to replace [Chris Weidman](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Chris-Weidman) and [Vitor Belfort](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Vitor-Belfort) atop the UFC 181 fight card in early December.  
  
In addition to being a continuation of one of the best fights of the year, what makes this second showdown between Hendricks and Lawler so compelling is what each has done since their first encounter.  
  
After claiming the victory and the vacant welterweight title in March, Hendricks revealed he’d fought with a torn biceps muscle. He’s since had surgery to repair the injury, and given how well he performed the first time around, how much better is he going to be now that he’s 100 percent?  
  
All Lawler has done since coming up just short in his quest to become welterweight champion is post consecutive victories over Jake Ellenberger and [Matt Brown](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Matt-Brown) two months apart. Many believe “Ruthless” did more damage in the first meeting between these two and with that experience under his belt, it will be interesting to see what adjustments the 13-year veteran makes the second time around.  
  
**UFC WOMEN’S STRAWWEIGHT TITLE FIGHT – THE ULTIMATE FIGHTER 20 FINALE (DECEMBER 12)**  
  
We still don’t know which two competitors will be battling for a place in the history books as the inaugural women’s strawweight champion, but given how competitive and entertaining the first few fights from the current season of The Ultimate Fighter have been, we’re already counting down the days until the final two remaining fighters step into the Octagon with the title on the line.  
  
**JUNIOR DOS SANTOS VS. [STIPE MIOCIC](https://www.ufc.com/fighter/Stipe-Miocic) – UFC ON FOX: DOS SANTOS VS. MIOCIC (DECEMBER 13)**  
  
This might be the most intriguing matchup on this list.  
  
On one side of the cage is Dos Santos, the former heavyweight champion, competing for the first time since his second loss to current titleholder Cain Velasquez. “Cigano” packs thunder in his hands and is unquestionably one of the top heavyweights in the sport today, but after more than a year on the sidelines battling injuries and coming off a his UFC 166, many people are curious to see how the Brazilian responds once he returns to the cage.  
  
On the other side is Miocic, one of the few fresh names in the big boy ranks and a fighter that sought out this pairing with the former champion after their initial meeting was postponed in May. Riding a three-fight winning streak and bringing a well-rounded skill set to the table, the Ohio native could potentially earn himself a shot at the title with a victory over the former champion.  
  
Plus, who doesn’t like watching to heavyweights with knockout power collide in the center of the cage?
