**Anthony Armand Ferguson Padilla**[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-7) (born February 12, 1984) is an American professional [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and [professional boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_boxing "Professional boxing"), and is the current [MFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_Boxing "Misfits Boxing") Middleweight Champion. As a mixed martial artist, he is a former [Interim UFC Lightweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Lightweight_Champion "UFC Lightweight Champion").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-9) A professional since 2008, he was signed to the [UFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC "UFC") from his _[The Ultimate Fighter 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Fighter:\_Team\_Lesnar\_vs.\_Team\_dos\_Santos "The Ultimate Fighter: Team Lesnar vs. Team dos Santos")_ win in 2011 until his departure in 2024. He is regarded as one of the greatest fighters never to have won an undisputed belt.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-11)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Ferguson was born in [Oxnard, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxnard,_California "Oxnard, California"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-13) on February 12, 1984, but grew up mainly in [Muskegon, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muskegon,_Michigan "Muskegon, Michigan"). He is of [Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Americans "Mexican Americans") heritage. His surname of Ferguson comes from his [Scottish American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Americans "Scottish Americans") stepfather.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-UF-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-15)

Ferguson was a three-sport athlete at [Muskegon Catholic Central High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muskegon_Catholic_Central_High_School "Muskegon Catholic Central High School") in American football, baseball, and [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling "Wrestling"). He was a starting defensive back for the 2000 Division 8 state football champions and was a three-time All-State selection in wrestling, winning the 152-lb division in 2002.

After high school, Ferguson enrolled at [Central Michigan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Michigan_University "Central Michigan University") before transferring to [Grand Valley State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Valley_State_University "Grand Valley State University"). He also did a stint at [Muskegon Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muskegon_Community_College "Muskegon Community College"). He did not complete his degree, but had a successful collegiate wrestling career, winning the 2006 [National Collegiate Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Wrestling_Association "National Collegiate Wrestling Association") national wrestling championship in the 165-lb division.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-GVSUwrestling-6)

Following college, Ferguson moved back to California to be closer to his extended family, working in marketing and sales during the day and picking up shifts as a bartender at night. One night, while working a bar shift, a patron noticed Ferguson's [cauliflower ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauliflower_ear "Cauliflower ear") and struck up a conversation about his wrestling background. The patron was a trainer at a local MMA gym and invited him to work with some young [mixed martial artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") on their wrestling. Shortly after this, he decided to pursue a professional mixed martial arts (MMA) career.

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Ferguson began his professional MMA career fighting in small organizations around California in 2007. Notable matches in his early career include a win over kickboxing champion [Joe Schilling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Schilling "Joe Schilling") and a loss to future [World Extreme Cagefighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Extreme_Cagefighting "World Extreme Cagefighting") (WEC) fighter [Karen Darabedyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Darabedyan "Karen Darabedyan").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-16)

### _The Ultimate Fighter_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Ultimate Fighter")]

Ferguson applied to compete in the UFC's reality series _The Ultimate Fighter_ multiple times. In 2010, he was finally accepted to compete in season 13 of the series after amassing a 10–2 professional record and winning the welterweight championship in PureCombat. He competed as a welterweight on _[The Ultimate Fighter: Team Lesnar vs. Team dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Fighter:\_Team\_Lesnar\_vs.\_Team\_dos\_Santos "The Ultimate Fighter: Team Lesnar vs. Team dos Santos")_.

Ferguson was selected as the third pick for Team Lesnar. In his first fight, Ferguson defeated [Justin Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Edwards_(fighter) "Justin Edwards (fighter)") by knockout in the first round. He next faced Ryan McGillivray in the quarterfinals and won by a TKO in the first round. He then faced Chuck O'Neil in the semifinals and won by TKO in the third round to advance to the final.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-17)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship")]

Ferguson officially made his UFC debut at [the Ultimate Fighter 13 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter_13_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter 13 Finale") against [Ramsey Nijem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramsey_Nijem "Ramsey Nijem") to determine the winner of [The Ultimate Fighter 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter_13 "The Ultimate Fighter 13"). Ferguson defeated Nijem by knockout in the first round to win a UFC contract.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-18) He also received a $40,000 _Knockout of the Night_ bonus.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-TUF13-19)

Following his debut, Ferguson returned to lightweight and faced [Aaron Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Riley "Aaron Riley") on September 24, 2011, at [UFC 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_135 "UFC 135"). The fight was stopped after the first round after Riley said he had a broken jaw, resulting in a TKO victory for Ferguson.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-20)

Ferguson then faced MMA veteran [Yves Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Edwards "Yves Edwards") at [the Ultimate Fighter 14 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter_14_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter 14 Finale").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-21) Ferguson won via unanimous decision (30–27, 30–27, and 29–28).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-22)

Ferguson was expected to face [Dennis Hallman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Hallman "Dennis Hallman") on May 5, 2012, at [UFC on Fox: Diaz vs. Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox:_Diaz_vs._Miller "UFC on Fox: Diaz vs. Miller").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-23) Hallman pulled out of the bout with an injury and replaced by [Thiago Tavares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Tavares "Thiago Tavares").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-24) Then, Tavares was forced out of the bout with an injury and replaced by [Michael Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Johnson_(fighter) "Michael Johnson (fighter)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-25) Ferguson lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-26)

#### Win streak

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Win streak")]

After over a year away from competition while healing an arm injury incurred in his last fight, Ferguson returned to face [Mike Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Rio "Mike Rio") on October 19, 2013, at [UFC 166](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_166 "UFC 166") which was the beginning of his twelve fight win streak.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-27) He won by D'Arce choke submission in the first round. The win also earned him his first _Submission of the Night_ award, valued at $60,000.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-UFC166-28)

Ferguson faced [Katsunori Kikuno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsunori_Kikuno "Katsunori Kikuno") on May 24, 2014, at [UFC 173](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_173 "UFC 173").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-29) He won the fight by knockout in the first round.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-30)

Ferguson was expected to face [Danny Castillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Castillo "Danny Castillo") on August 2, 2014, at [UFC 176](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_176 "UFC 176").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-31) After [UFC 176](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_176 "UFC 176") was cancelled, Castillo/Ferguson was rescheduled and took place on August 30, 2014, at [UFC 177](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_177 "UFC 177").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-32) Ferguson won the fight via split decision.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-33)

Ferguson faced [Abel Trujillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Trujillo "Abel Trujillo") on December 6, 2014, at [UFC 181](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_181 "UFC 181").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-34) Ferguson won the bout in the second round by submission.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-35)

Ferguson was expected to face [Yancy Medeiros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yancy_Medeiros "Yancy Medeiros") on February 28, 2015, at [UFC 184](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_184 "UFC 184").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-36) Medeiros pulled out of the bout, citing injury, and was replaced by [Gleison Tibau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gleison_Tibau "Gleison Tibau").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-37) Ferguson won the fight by submission in the first round which also earned him a _Performance of the Night_ bonus.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-UFC184-38)

Ferguson faced [Josh Thomson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Thomson "Josh Thomson") on July 15, 2015, at [UFC Fight Night 71](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_71 "UFC Fight Night 71").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-39) He won the fight via unanimous decision (30–27, 30–27, and 30–26) and earned his second straight _Performance of the Night_ bonus.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-UFCFN71-41)

Ferguson was expected to face [Khabib Nurmagomedov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khabib_Nurmagomedov "Khabib Nurmagomedov") on December 11, 2015, at [the Ultimate Fighter 22 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Team_McGregor_vs._Team_Faber#The_Ultimate_Fighter_22_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: Team McGregor vs. Team Faber").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-42) Nurmagomedov pulled out of the fight in late October, citing injury, and was replaced by [Edson Barboza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edson_Barboza "Edson Barboza").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-43) After a back-and-forth first round that had Ferguson docked one point due to an illegal upkick, Ferguson finished Barboza with a D'Arce choke submission in the second round.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-44) He earned his third consecutive _Performance of the Night_ bonus as well as a _Fight of the Night_ bonus.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-Tristen_Critchfield-45)

A rematch with Michael Johnson was briefly scheduled for March 5, 2016, at [UFC 196](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_196 "UFC 196").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-46) On January 27, it was announced that Johnson withdrew from the bout due to injury. In turn, the bout with Nurmagomedov was rescheduled and expected take place on April 16, 2016, at [UFC on Fox 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_19 "UFC on Fox 19").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-47) On April 5, Ferguson pulled out of the bout due to a [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung "Lung") issue.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-48) He was replaced by promotional newcomer [Darrell Horcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darrell_Horcher "Darrell Horcher").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-49)

Ferguson was expected to face [Michael Chiesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Chiesa "Michael Chiesa") on July 13, 2016, at [UFC Fight Night 91](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_91 "UFC Fight Night 91").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-50) Chiesa pulled out of the fight on June 27, citing injury, and was replaced by promotional newcomer [Lando Vannata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Vannata "Lando Vannata").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-52) Ferguson won his second straight fight via D'Arce choke and was awarded another _Fight of the Night_ bonus.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-Ben_Fowlkes-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-54)

Ferguson fought former champion [Rafael dos Anjos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_dos_Anjos "Rafael dos Anjos") on November 5, 2016, at [the Ultimate Fighter Latin America 3 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Latin_America_3#The_Ultimate_Fighter_Latin_America_3_Finale:_dos_Anjos_vs._Ferguson "The Ultimate Fighter: Latin America 3").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-55) He won the fight by unanimous decision. Both participants were awarded _Fight of the Night_, which gave Ferguson his sixth post-fight bonus in his past five fights.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-Damon_Martin-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-57)

The pairing with Nurmagomedov was scheduled for a third time at [UFC 209](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_209 "UFC 209"), this time for the interim UFC Lightweight Championship.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-58) Prior to the weigh-ins for the event, Nurmagomedov was hospitalized due to the ill effects of his [weight cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weight_cutting "Weight cutting"), and the bout was cancelled yet again.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-59)

Ferguson faced [Kevin Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Lee_(fighter) "Kevin Lee (fighter)") on October 7, 2017, at [UFC 216](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_216 "UFC 216") for the interim UFC Lightweight Championship. He won the bout by triangle choke submission in the third round.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-61) A bout with Nurmagomedov had been scheduled for the fourth time on April 7, 2018, at [UFC 223](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_223 "UFC 223").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-62) On April 1, 2018, Ferguson reportedly tore his [fibular collateral ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibular_collateral_ligament "Fibular collateral ligament") while walking on the set for a pre-fight media obligation and was forced to withdraw from the event.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-64)

Ferguson faced [Anthony Pettis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Pettis "Anthony Pettis") on October 6, 2018, at [UFC 229](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_229 "UFC 229").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-65) He won the bout via corner stoppage after two rounds. Pettis' longtime cornerman and coach, [Duke Roufus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Roufus "Duke Roufus"), informed the referee that he would not continue after suffering a broken hand.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-66) Their performance earned both participants [_Fight of the Night_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_bonus_award_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients") honors.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-MMA_News-67)

Ferguson next faced [Donald Cerrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Cerrone "Donald Cerrone") on June 8, 2019, at [UFC 238](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_238 "UFC 238").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-68) He won the fight via TKO due to a doctor stoppage after Cerrone blew his nose between rounds 2 & 3 which caused his swollen right eye to completely close, rendering him unable to continue.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-69) This fight earned both participants [_Fight of the Night_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_bonus_award_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients") honors.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-mmajunkie.com-70)

#### Losing streak

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Losing streak")]

Ferguson was scheduled to face [Khabib Nurmagomedov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khabib_Nurmagomedov "Khabib Nurmagomedov") for the [UFC Lightweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Lightweight_Championship "UFC Lightweight Championship") on April 18, 2020, at [UFC 249](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_249 "UFC 249"), however the fight was canceled after Nurmagomedov was unable to leave Russia due to restricted air travel as a result of the [coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-71) Ferguson then agreed to compete for the Interim UFC Lightweight Championship against a late replacement in [Justin Gaethje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Gaethje "Justin Gaethje") at the event.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-72) On April 9, UFC president [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") announced that this event was postponed[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-Postpone-73) and the bout eventually took place on May 9, 2020.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-74) He was outstruck by Gaethje for all five rounds, eventually losing the fight via TKO in the fifth round.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-75) This fight earned both participants [_Fight of the Night_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_bonus_award_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients") honors.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-:0-76)

Ferguson faced [Charles Oliveira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Oliveira "Charles Oliveira") on December 12, 2020, at [UFC 256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_256 "UFC 256").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-77) He lost the fight via unanimous decision after being dominated and controlled on the ground for most of the fight.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-78)

Ferguson faced [Beneil Dariush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beneil_Dariush "Beneil Dariush") on May 15, 2021, at [UFC 262](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_262 "UFC 262").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-79) He lost the fight via unanimous decision being once again controlled on the ground for the majority of the fight.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-80)

Ferguson faced former [Bellator Lightweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellator_Lightweight_Champion "Bellator Lightweight Champion")[Michael Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Chandler "Michael Chandler") on May 7, 2022 at [UFC 274](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_274 "UFC 274").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-81) Despite a strong first round, Ferguson lost the fight via knockout early in the second round.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-82)

Ferguson was scheduled to return to the welterweight division to face [Li Jingliang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jingliang "Li Jingliang") on September 10, 2022, in the co-main event of [UFC 279](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_279 "UFC 279").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-83) However, Ferguson instead moved up to the main event to face [Nate Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Diaz "Nate Diaz"), after his original opponent [Khamzat Chimaev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khamzat_Chimaev "Khamzat Chimaev") was pulled from their fight due to missing weight.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-84) Ferguson lost the fight via a guillotine choke submission in the fourth round.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-85)

Ferguson returned to the lightweight division to face [King Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Green "King Green") at [UFC 291](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_291 "UFC 291") on July 29, 2023.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-86) He lost the fight via technical submission due to an arm-triangle choke in the final seconds of the third round.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-87)

Ferguson faced [Paddy Pimblett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddy_Pimblett "Paddy Pimblett") on December 16, 2023, at [UFC 296](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_296 "UFC 296").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-88) He lost the fight via unanimous decision.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-89)

Ferguson faced [Michael Chiesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Chiesa "Michael Chiesa") in a welterweight bout on August 3, 2024 at [UFC on ABC 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ABC_7 "UFC on ABC 7").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-90) He lost the fight via a rear-naked choke submission in the first round.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-91) With this eighth consecutive loss, Ferguson surpassed [B.J. Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.J._Penn "B.J. Penn") and now holds the record for the longest losing streak in UFC history.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-losingstreak-92)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Ferguson has two sons with his wife, Cristina Ferguson.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-111) In March 2019, Cristina filed a temporary restraining order against Tony in Orange County, California, alleging uncharacteristic behavior including severe paranoia, prolonged sleep deprivation, destruction of their home fireplace, and beliefs that a tracking chip had been inserted into his leg during reconstructive knee surgery.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-:1-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-113) According to court filings reported by multiple media outlets, she also stated that Ferguson had taken their son from the family home for several days without her consent, and that police had been called to their residence on multiple occasions over the preceding months.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-114)

She did not allege physical abuse, and later stated that the filing was intended as a precautionary measure to encourage him to seek help for his mental state.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-:1-112) By April 2019, she had withdrawn the request, and the restraining order expired without any criminal charges being filed.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-117) He then began to resume MMA.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-118)

In the early hours of May 7, 2023, Ferguson was arrested in [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") and charged with [driving under the influence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence "Driving under the influence") after allegedly crashing his pickup truck into two other vehicles outside of a nightclub, causing his truck to roll over in the process. He was taken into custody and booked into the LAPD Hollywood police station where his bail was set at $30,000.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-119) He was later released from custody on a [personal recognizance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recognizance "Recognizance") bond.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-120)

## Fighting style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Fighting style")]

Ferguson is known for his well-rounded style which includes unorthodox striking, exceptional cardio, sharp elbows, and proficiency in D'Arce chokes. During his peak, he achieved a 12-fight winning streak, finishing nine of his opponents. His aggressive fighting style, particularly his use of elbows, often left opponents bloodied and contributed to six "Fight of the Night" bonuses.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-121)

## Public appearance and cultural influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tony_Ferguson&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Public appearance and cultural influences")]

Ferguson is known as one of MMA's most eccentric personalities.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-122) He constructed his own custom training apparatus at his house in [Big Bear Lake, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Bear_Lake,_California "Big Bear Lake, California") and regularly posts videos of his unique workouts on his personal [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") page. These include smacking his arms and legs against metal poles to build bone strength, throwing baseballs off a pitcher's mound to build power, and somersault jumps over tall stacks of gym mats.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Ferguson#cite_note-124)

[Tony Ferguson](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2560085/tony-ferguson) waded in with a left knee to the body. [Josh Thomson](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2470332/josh-thomson) saw it the whole way. He wrapped his arms fully around Ferguson and dumped him to the mat for an easy takedown in the first round of their 2015 fight.

Thomson was in control, or so he thought.

Ferguson used the momentum from Thomson's technique and exploded quickly into a front roll. Before Thomson could even process what had just happened, Ferguson was up on his feet, ready to resume his attack.

"I shot a double leg -- probably one of the deepest double legs I've ever hit on anybody," Thomson told ESPN. "Hit him right to a [takedown]. He did a tuck and a roll and came right back up to his feet. I stood back and was like, 'This is crazy.' After that I decided, 'OK, wrestling may not be the way to go.'"

## UFC 249 coverage

[![Image 227](https://a.espncdn.com/i/espn+/ufc-espn-plus.png)](https://plus.espn.com/ufc/ppv?om-navmethod=mma-inline)

UFC 249 is expected to have a card loaded with star power, featuring two title fights. Tony Ferguson and Justin Gaethje, two of the UFC's most exciting fighters, will compete for the interim 155-pound title in the main event, and Henry Cejudo will defend the bantamweight title against former titleholder Dominick Cruz.

[Purchase UFC 249 here](https://plus.espn.com/ppv)

**UFC 249: Ferguson vs. Gaethje**  
 • Saturday, May 9, in Jacksonville, Florida  
 • 6 p.m. ET on ESPN and ESPN PPV

Thomson, the former Strikeforce lightweight champion -- and one of the best 155-pounders of his era -- fought Ferguson at UFC San Diego on July 15, 2015. Ferguson won by unanimous decision for his sixth straight victory. Thomson wasn't just handed a loss, either. In addition to that humbling moment on the takedown attempt, Thomson ended up with about 30 stitches on his head and face, as well as forearm pain that took weeks to heal.

"The sad thing is, [the takedown attempt] was a lot of effort to put out for something he pretty much gave me, so he could roll out, and that pretty much changed the way I approached the fight," Thomson said. "And that was in the first round."

Five years later, Ferguson is still on a winning streak -- 12 straight now. And he's still making opponents shake their heads. On Saturday, Ferguson faces [Justin Gaethje](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/3022345/justin-gaethje) for the UFC interim lightweight title in the main event of [UFC 249](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/29113850/ufc-249-how-watch-tony-ferguson-vs-justin-gaethje-plus-full-analysis) in Jacksonville, Florida. Ferguson (25-3) is known for his unorthodox approach to fighting and sometimes [extreme training tactics](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/28959058/ufc-249-tractor-tires-sledgehammers-tony-ferguson-unique-workouts). But what makes the Californian so different in the Octagon? ESPN asked several of Ferguson's former opponents what it's like to be in the cage with one of the most unique combatants in MMA history.

_Editor's note: Answers have been edited for clarity._

### Josh Thomson (lost to Ferguson via [unanimous decision at UFC San Diego](https://www.ufc.com/video/ufc-209-free-fight-tony-ferguson-vs-josh-thomson) on July 15, 2015)

!Image 228

Josh Thomson, left, says he needed close to 30 stitches after his fight with Tony Ferguson in July 2015.Todd Warshaw/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images

When I first shook his hands at weigh-ins, I didn't realize how big his hands were. When we shook hands, his hand went all the way around my hand. Honestly, he doesn't really hit that hard when I take into consideration guys that I've been hit by. He's not that physically strong, but he has that length and that leverage.

When we got into the fight, he actually grabbed me at the forearm and slid his hand down to where my glove is. There was no way of me getting out. His hand went all the way around my wrist, all the way around my forearm. That all kind of plays into his jiu-jitsu, his control on the ground, all these types of things when he needs to utilize these positions.

There were a lot of things I expected from him. I expected good cardio, I expected a relentless pace. I expected that push kick. I didn't expect it to have as much power as it had behind it. I thought the push kick -- I'll just block it, catch it a couple times, whatever it may be. I did catch it, but when you catch it, he's throwing combinations off of it. My forearm was swollen from blocking that push kick for probably about two weeks. I couldn't put my forearm down. You know when you sit at the dinner table and you rest your forearms on the side of the table? Couldn't do that. It was painful, man.

I had very, very few cuts in my 32-fight career. I want to say by the end [of the night after fighting Ferguson] I probably had close to 30-something stitches on my face. I had 20 on that big cut on the side of my head that actually dropped me. There's a lot that people can prepare for, but that amount of blood and that amount of cuts, that's not something most people can handle.

### [Yves Edwards](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2335706/yves-edwards) (lost to Ferguson via unanimous decision at TUF 14 Finale on Dec. 3, 2011)

!Image 229

Yves Edwards, right, found out about Tony Ferguson's pain tolerance during their fight in 2011. "I think he enjoys it," Edwards says.Josh Hedges/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images

Now that I see him in the cage and I see some of the things he says and does, I'm not surprised by what happened. He's definitely a wild one. There are some things when we fought that were like, how does that make sense? He's orthodox and I'm southpaw. And he's throwing that inside leg kick, hard and viciously. But he isn't trying to kick my thigh. He's literally going down to my shin.

I have a good check. You're throwing that inside kick, you don't pick up the leg and turn it over. You just roll the ankle over and turn it in like you're throwing a hook. He throws that kick and I turn my knee over to check it and we go shin to shin. I'm thinking to myself, "Why the f--- would you do that? That s--- hurts, now we're both f---ed up. But I can't show you this." So I keep fighting. He did that two or three times.

If I do that and it hurts me horribly, I'm not gonna continue to do that same thing. I'm trying to damage you, not myself. He just feels that and keeps moving forward. He's just evolved from there. He's become more and more vicious, more and more calculated. And the cardio that he has -- it's hard to put him down and keep him down. I don't think he has a higher threshold for pain. I think he enjoys it. I don't know if it's one of those things that makes him feel alive or maybe he enjoys the fact that he can out-suffer you.

[Tony Ferguson](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2560085/tony-ferguson) waded in with a left knee to the body. [Josh Thomson](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2470332/josh-thomson) saw it the whole way. He wrapped his arms fully around Ferguson and dumped him to the mat for an easy takedown in the first round of their 2015 fight.

Thomson was in control, or so he thought.

Ferguson used the momentum from Thomson's technique and exploded quickly into a front roll. Before Thomson could even process what had just happened, Ferguson was up on his feet, ready to resume his attack.

"I shot a double leg -- probably one of the deepest double legs I've ever hit on anybody," Thomson told ESPN. "Hit him right to a [takedown]. He did a tuck and a roll and came right back up to his feet. I stood back and was like, 'This is crazy.' After that I decided, 'OK, wrestling may not be the way to go.'"

## UFC 249 coverage

[![Image 227](https://a.espncdn.com/i/espn+/ufc-espn-plus.png)](https://plus.espn.com/ufc/ppv?om-navmethod=mma-inline)

UFC 249 is expected to have a card loaded with star power, featuring two title fights. Tony Ferguson and Justin Gaethje, two of the UFC's most exciting fighters, will compete for the interim 155-pound title in the main event, and Henry Cejudo will defend the bantamweight title against former titleholder Dominick Cruz.

[Purchase UFC 249 here](https://plus.espn.com/ppv)

**UFC 249: Ferguson vs. Gaethje**  
 • Saturday, May 9, in Jacksonville, Florida  
 • 6 p.m. ET on ESPN and ESPN PPV

Thomson, the former Strikeforce lightweight champion -- and one of the best 155-pounders of his era -- fought Ferguson at UFC San Diego on July 15, 2015. Ferguson won by unanimous decision for his sixth straight victory. Thomson wasn't just handed a loss, either. In addition to that humbling moment on the takedown attempt, Thomson ended up with about 30 stitches on his head and face, as well as forearm pain that took weeks to heal.

"The sad thing is, [the takedown attempt] was a lot of effort to put out for something he pretty much gave me, so he could roll out, and that pretty much changed the way I approached the fight," Thomson said. "And that was in the first round."

Five years later, Ferguson is still on a winning streak -- 12 straight now. And he's still making opponents shake their heads. On Saturday, Ferguson faces [Justin Gaethje](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/3022345/justin-gaethje) for the UFC interim lightweight title in the main event of [UFC 249](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/29113850/ufc-249-how-watch-tony-ferguson-vs-justin-gaethje-plus-full-analysis) in Jacksonville, Florida. Ferguson (25-3) is known for his unorthodox approach to fighting and sometimes [extreme training tactics](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/28959058/ufc-249-tractor-tires-sledgehammers-tony-ferguson-unique-workouts). But what makes the Californian so different in the Octagon? ESPN asked several of Ferguson's former opponents what it's like to be in the cage with one of the most unique combatants in MMA history.

_Editor's note: Answers have been edited for clarity._

### Josh Thomson (lost to Ferguson via [unanimous decision at UFC San Diego](https://www.ufc.com/video/ufc-209-free-fight-tony-ferguson-vs-josh-thomson) on July 15, 2015)

!Image 228

Josh Thomson, left, says he needed close to 30 stitches after his fight with Tony Ferguson in July 2015.Todd Warshaw/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images

When I first shook his hands at weigh-ins, I didn't realize how big his hands were. When we shook hands, his hand went all the way around my hand. Honestly, he doesn't really hit that hard when I take into consideration guys that I've been hit by. He's not that physically strong, but he has that length and that leverage.

When we got into the fight, he actually grabbed me at the forearm and slid his hand down to where my glove is. There was no way of me getting out. His hand went all the way around my wrist, all the way around my forearm. That all kind of plays into his jiu-jitsu, his control on the ground, all these types of things when he needs to utilize these positions.

There were a lot of things I expected from him. I expected good cardio, I expected a relentless pace. I expected that push kick. I didn't expect it to have as much power as it had behind it. I thought the push kick -- I'll just block it, catch it a couple times, whatever it may be. I did catch it, but when you catch it, he's throwing combinations off of it. My forearm was swollen from blocking that push kick for probably about two weeks. I couldn't put my forearm down. You know when you sit at the dinner table and you rest your forearms on the side of the table? Couldn't do that. It was painful, man.

I had very, very few cuts in my 32-fight career. I want to say by the end [of the night after fighting Ferguson] I probably had close to 30-something stitches on my face. I had 20 on that big cut on the side of my head that actually dropped me. There's a lot that people can prepare for, but that amount of blood and that amount of cuts, that's not something most people can handle.

### [Yves Edwards](https://www.espn.com/mma/fighter/_/id/2335706/yves-edwards) (lost to Ferguson via unanimous decision at TUF 14 Finale on Dec. 3, 2011)

!Image 229

Yves Edwards, right, found out about Tony Ferguson's pain tolerance during their fight in 2011. "I think he enjoys it," Edwards says.Josh Hedges/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images

Now that I see him in the cage and I see some of the things he says and does, I'm not surprised by what happened. He's definitely a wild one. There are some things when we fought that were like, how does that make sense? He's orthodox and I'm southpaw. And he's throwing that inside leg kick, hard and viciously. But he isn't trying to kick my thigh. He's literally going down to my shin.

I have a good check. You're throwing that inside kick, you don't pick up the leg and turn it over. You just roll the ankle over and turn it in like you're throwing a hook. He throws that kick and I turn my knee over to check it and we go shin to shin. I'm thinking to myself, "Why the f--- would you do that? That s--- hurts, now we're both f---ed up. But I can't show you this." So I keep fighting. He did that two or three times.

If I do that and it hurts me horribly, I'm not gonna continue to do that same thing. I'm trying to damage you, not myself. He just feels that and keeps moving forward. He's just evolved from there. He's become more and more vicious, more and more calculated. And the cardio that he has -- it's hard to put him down and keep him down. I don't think he has a higher threshold for pain. I think he enjoys it. I don't know if it's one of those things that makes him feel alive or maybe he enjoys the fact that he can out-suffer you.
