**Alistair Cees Overeem** (born 17 May 1980) is a Dutch former professional [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and [kickboxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickboxing "Kickboxing"). He is a former [Strikeforce Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Strikeforce champions"), [Dream Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dream_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Dream champions"), [K-1 World Grand Prix Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_K-1_champions#K-1_World_Grand_Prix_Champions "List of K-1 champions"), and was the first fighter to hold world titles in [MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and K-1 kickboxing at the same time. Overeem is also a one-time challenger for the [UFC Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship").

Overeem holds the UFC all-time record for highest significant strike accuracy in the promotion's history (74.3%)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-7).

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Overeem was born in [Hounslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hounslow "Hounslow"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England, to a [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaican_people "Jamaican people") father and a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people") mother, whose maternal great-grandmother was an illegitimate child of King [William III of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_III_of_the_Netherlands "William III of the Netherlands").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-9) When he was six years old, his parents divorced and he moved with his mother and older brother to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), where he grew up in the city of [Amersfoort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amersfoort "Amersfoort").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-10) As a child, Overeem started training martial arts with his older brother [Valentijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentijn_Overeem "Valentijn Overeem") in order to defend himself from [bullying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullying "Bullying"). He decided to pursue a competitive sports career by his brother's example, first in [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") and later [track and field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_Field "Track and Field") and [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11) At the age of 15, he followed Valentijn into [Chris Dolman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Dolman "Chris Dolman")'s [Martial Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_Arts "Martial Arts") gym to become a professional fighter.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Bleach-12) Alistair initially did not like the sport, as he was routinely beaten by more experienced students, but he changed his mind when he met [Bas Rutten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bas_Rutten "Bas Rutten") and [Joop Kasteel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joop_Kasteel "Joop Kasteel"), after which he fully dedicated himself to training.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Bleach-12)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

Overeem had his first MMA professional fight at 19 years old, defeating [Ricardo Fyeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Fyeet "Ricardo Fyeet") by submission on 24 October 1999(1999-10-24) at _[It's Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Showtime\_(kickboxing) "It's Showtime (kickboxing)")_, the first event of the self-titled promotion.

### Early MMA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early MMA career")]

After posting a 10–3 record in [Fighting Network Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting_Network_Rings "Fighting Network Rings"), [M-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-1_Global "M-1 Global"), [It's Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Showtime_(kickboxing) "It's Showtime (kickboxing)"), and 2 Hot 2 Handle, Overeem debuted in the [Pride Fighting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Fighting_Championships "Pride Fighting Championships") on 20 July 2002, defeating Yusuke Imamura by TKO in 44 seconds.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-13)

### Pride FC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pride FC")]

Overeem won two more fights in Pride before entering the 2003 Pride Middleweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_Pride_FC#Pride_Total_Elimination_2003 "2003 in Pride FC") and losing to future [UFC Light heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship")[Chuck Liddell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Liddell "Chuck Liddell") in the quarterfinal match.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-14) Overeem rebounded to defeat [Tomohiko Hashimoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomohiko_Hashimoto "Tomohiko Hashimoto") at the Inoki Bom-Ba-Ye 2003 in 36 seconds.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-15) On 31 October 2004, Overeem fought [Hiromitsu Kanehara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiromitsu_Kanehara "Hiromitsu Kanehara"), defeating him by TKO in the second round at [Pride 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_28 "Pride 28").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-16) Overeem lost his next fight against [Brazilian Top Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Top_Team "Brazilian Top Team") fighter [Antônio Rogério Nogueira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Rog%C3%A9rio_Nogueira "Antônio Rogério Nogueira").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-17)

In 2005, Overeem entered the Pride Middleweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Total_Elimination_2005 "Pride Total Elimination 2005"), in which he defeated [UFC Light heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship")[Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") by submission in the opening round.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-18) Overeem moved on to fight [Igor Vovchanchyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Vovchanchyn "Igor Vovchanchyn") in the quarterfinals at [Pride Critical Countdown 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Critical_Countdown_2005 "Pride Critical Countdown 2005") and won via submission in under two minutes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-19) Overeem lost in the semifinals to the eventual champion [Maurício Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-20)

In February 2006, Overeem fought Russian Top Team favourite [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov"). Overeem won, dislocating Kharitonov's shoulder in the process. With his win over Kharitonov, Overeem secured a spot in the Pride 2006 Openweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination Absolute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Total_Elimination_Absolute "Pride Total Elimination Absolute"). He fought [Brazilian jiu-jitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu") specialist [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"), and lost via [kimura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armlock#Kimura "Armlock") in the second round.

### Debut in Strikeforce

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Debut in Strikeforce")]

On 9 June 2006, Overeem travelled to [San Jose, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California"), to win a rematch with [Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") by decision at [Strikeforce: Revenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Revenge "Strikeforce: Revenge").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-21)

### Return to Pride

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Return to Pride")]

A month later Overeem returned to Pride for a highly anticipated rematch with [Antônio Rogério Nogueira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Rog%C3%A9rio_Nogueira "Antônio Rogério Nogueira"). Overeem entered the fight with a heavily taped neck. After controlling the first round and a half with his striking, Overeem was stumbled from a punch, and Nogueira followed with a flurry of strikes. Worried Overeem would be more severely injured, his corner threw in the towel.

At [Pride Final Conflict Absolute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Final_Conflict_Absolute "Pride Final Conflict Absolute"), Overeem lost to [Ricardo Arona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Arona "Ricardo Arona"). Overeem was on the receiving end of a leg kick that caused a non-serious injury to his nerves, causing him to lose feeling in his foot and leg. Unable to mount much offence or defend against Arona, Overeem tapped out to avoid further injury.

He then suffered another KO loss to [Maurício Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua") at [Pride 33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_33 "Pride 33"), but returned in June 2007 with a submission win over Michael Knaap at [K-1 Grand Prix in Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_GP_2007_in_Amsterdam "K-1 GP 2007 in Amsterdam") (despite [K-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1 "K-1") being a kickboxing promotion, the bout was fought under MMA rules).

On 17 September 2007, at the Hero's 10: Middleweight Tournament Final, Alistair faced [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov") again. Overeem showed solid movement as soon as the first round began, but he suffered a KO loss just before the end of the first round.

### Return to Strikeforce/DREAM/Dynamite

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Return to Strikeforce/DREAM/Dynamite")]

On 16 November 2007, Overeem defeated [Paul Buentello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Buentello "Paul Buentello") for the vacant [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions") by submission due to knee strikes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-22) On 15 June 2008 Overeem won by KO in the first round against Lee Tae-Hyun at DREAM 4. On 21 July 2008, Overeem defeated [K-1 World Grand Prix Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2001 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2001")[Mark Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hunt "Mark Hunt") in the first round by submission at [Dream 5: Lightweight Grand Prix 2008 Final Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_5 "Dream 5").

His next fight was against [Mirko Cro Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirko_Cro_Cop "Mirko Cro Cop") at [Dream 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_6 "Dream 6") on 23 September 2008.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-23) The bout was stopped about halfway through the first round and declared a no-contest, after Overeem landed multiple knees to the groin of Cro Cop.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-24)

Overeem was rumoured to be making his first title defence against [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers") on 6 June at [Strikeforce: Lawler vs. Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Lawler_vs._Shields "Strikeforce: Lawler vs. Shields"). However, a hand injury scuttled plans for the fight.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-25) According to Golden Glory manager Bas Boon, Overeem had suffered a hand infection following a nightclub brawl early May 2009. According to Boon, Alistair and his brother Valentijn, both heavyweights had been involved in an altercation that left five security staff needing hospital treatment and nearly cost Alistair his hand.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Hand,_Pullout-26)

Overeem was scheduled to make his first [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions") defence in a rematch against [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") at [Strikeforce: Carano vs. Cyborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Carano_vs._Cyborg "Strikeforce: Carano vs. Cyborg"), but had to pull out due to a hand injury, most likely caused from his nightclub brawl.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Hand,_Pullout-26)

Alistair defeated Tony Sylvester at Golden Glory's 10-year anniversary celebration with a standing guillotine choke.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-27) He used the same choke only eight days later to submit [James Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Thompson_(fighter) "James Thompson (fighter)") at [Dream 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_12 "Dream 12").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-28)

Overeem was set to face [Andrei Arlovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Arlovski "Andrei Arlovski") at [Dynamite!! 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2009 "Dynamite!! 2009"), but FEG instead opted to have him face [Kazuyuki Fujita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazuyuki_Fujita "Kazuyuki Fujita") to keep with the DREAM vs. Sengoku theme.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-29) Overeem quickly overpowered his opponent and recorded a knockout with a knee to the head.

Overeem next faced [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers") on 15 May 2010 at [Strikeforce: Heavy Artillery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Heavy_Artillery "Strikeforce: Heavy Artillery") to defend his [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-30) He won the fight via TKO in the first round. In his post-fight interview, Overeem declared for another time that he wants to fight [Fedor Emelianenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor_Emelianenko "Fedor Emelianenko"), claiming that Fedor's management can no longer ignore his presence.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-31) The majority of Alistair Overeem's pre-fight training camp took place at the newly opened [Golden Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Glory "Golden Glory") Gym in [Pattaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattaya "Pattaya"), [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand"), where "The Demolition Man" concentrated on the further improvement of his [Muay Thai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muay_Thai "Muay Thai") skills.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-32)

Overeem faced [Todd Duffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Duffee "Todd Duffee") on 31 December 2010 at [Dynamite!! 2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2010 "Dynamite!! 2010").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-33) He defeated Duffee by way of knockout 19 seconds into the first round to win the interim [DREAM Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dream_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Dream champions").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-34)

### Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix")]

In early 2011, Overeem was named as one of eight men that will take part of the Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix, alongside [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"), [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov"), [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers"), [Josh Barnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Barnett "Josh Barnett"), [Andrei Arlovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Arlovski "Andrei Arlovski"), [Antônio Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Silva_(fighter) "Antônio Silva (fighter)") and [Fedor Emelianenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor_Emelianenko "Fedor Emelianenko").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-35)

A rematch with [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") took place on 18 June 2011, at [Strikeforce: Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Dallas "Strikeforce: Dallas") as part of an eight-man heavyweight tournament.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-36) Overeem defeated Werdum by unanimous decision (30–27, 30–27, and 29–28).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-37)

### Removal from GP/Strikeforce

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Removal from GP/Strikeforce")]

On 17 July, it was announced that Overeem was removed from the promotion's 2011 Heavyweight Grand Prix. Overeem went on to state that he felt the September date was too soon for him to return, and that he needed time to rest and heal after his 18 June quarterfinal decision win over [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"). Overeem was swapped out for unbeaten up-and-comer [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-38) Subsequently, on 29 July, it was announced that Overeem had been released from the Strikeforce organization as [Zuffa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuffa "Zuffa") exercised their right to eliminate the one remaining fight on his contract.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-40) It was revealed that the reason behind Overeem's release from Strikeforce was not due to his unwillingness to participate in the Grand Prix semi-finals, but due to Golden Glory's policy requiring that the money fighters made through fights be paid through their management first.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-41)

This disagreement led not only to Overeem's release but also other Golden Glory stars under a Zuffa contract, including former [Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions")[Marloes Coenen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen"), [Norwegian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_people "Norwegian people") UFC Heavyweight [Jon Olav Einemo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Olav_Einemo "Jon Olav Einemo"), and even brother [Valentijn Overeem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentijn_Overeem "Valentijn Overeem"). Team Golden Glory leader Bas Boon stated he has since changed the policy, and that Alistair Overeem could come to the UFC under an exclusive deal if the right terms are offered, which he later received.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-42)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship (2011–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship (2011–2021)")]

After much speculation, on 6 September 2011 it was announced that Overeem had signed a contract with the [UFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"), and that his first fight would be against former [UFC Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship")[Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") on 30 December 2011 at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-44)

The lead up to the fight was rife with controversy. In November 2011, both competitors were required by the [NSAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_Athletic_Commission "Nevada Athletic Commission") to comply with out-of-competition drug testing. Lesnar delivered his sample screen on 21 November, while Overeem delivered his on 23 November. The screen, however, did not meet the standards of the commission. Overeem submitted a second test through his personal physician, which was also deemed unacceptable before flying out of the country. Overeem was ultimately given a conditional license for the fight by the committee during a meeting held on 12 December 2011.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-45)

On 30 December 2011, at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141"), Overeem made his UFC debut in the main event against [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-46) Overeem hurt Lesnar multiple times early on with knees to the body, and went on to finish the fight with a kick to the liver and subsequent punches at 2:26 of the first round. The victory earned him a heavyweight title shot against champion [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-47)

#### Failed drug test

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Failed drug test")]

Overeem was scheduled to fight [UFC Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship")[Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") on 26 May 2012 at [UFC 146](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_146 "UFC 146"). However, on 4 April 2012, Overeem was revealed to have failed his pre-fight drug test by the [Nevada State Athletic Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Athletic_Commission "Nevada State Athletic Commission") (NSAC).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-48) Overeem had a 14-to-1 testosterone-to-epitestosterone (T/E) ratio, over the allowed ratio rate of 6-to-1. On Friday 20 April 2012 UFC President [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") confirmed that Overeem had been removed from his fight with dos Santos and replaced by [Frank Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Mir "Frank Mir").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-50)

One day prior to his meeting with the NSAC, Overeem released a prepared statement to the media in which he claims the positive result of the drug test came as a result of a doctor-prescribed "anti-inflammatory medication that was mixed with testosterone."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-51) Overeem's lawyer filed a continuation request for additional time to gather support for his recent claim, which was voted on by the NSAC on 24 April 2012.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-52) The request was denied and the NSAC voted unanimously to deny Overeem's application status for a period of nine months, dating back to 27 March, the day of his drug test. He was allowed to reapply after this time period in December 2012.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-53)

#### Return

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Return")]

Overeem returned to face [Antônio Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Silva_(fighter) "Antônio Silva (fighter)") on 2 February 2013 at [UFC 156](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_156 "UFC 156").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-54) Leading up to the fight, Overeem was dismissive of Silva's skills, claiming he was better than his opponent in every aspect of MMA.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-55) Despite being a heavy betting favourite and having won rounds one and two, an overconfident Overeem lost to Silva by KO in the third round.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-56)

Overeem was expected to face former UFC Heavyweight Champion [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") on 25 May 2013 at [UFC 160](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_160 "UFC 160").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-HW-57) However, in early March, Overeem pulled out of the bout, citing an injury[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-58) and was replaced by [Mark Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hunt "Mark Hunt").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-HuntIn-59)

For his third fight with the promotion, Overeem faced [Travis Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Browne "Travis Browne") in the co-main event at [UFC Fight Night 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_26 "UFC Fight Night 26") on 17 August 2013.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-60) Overeem was dominant early in the fight, attacking Browne with a flurry of knees and punches. Browne recovered and defeated Overeem via TKO with a front kick.

Overeem was scheduled to face [Frank Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Mir "Frank Mir") on 16 November 2013 at [UFC 167](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_167 "UFC 167").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-61) However, the pairing was moved to 1 February 2014 at [UFC 169](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_169 "UFC 169").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-62) He defeated Mir by unanimous decision and called out [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") in his post-fight interview.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-63)

Overeem injured his elbow and decided to take the time out to have surgery, expecting to return in September 2014.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-64) On 9 July, the UFC announced he would face [Ben Rothwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Rothwell "Ben Rothwell") on 5 September 2014 at [UFC Fight Night 50](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_50 "UFC Fight Night 50").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-65) Rothwell defeated Overeem via TKO in the first round.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-66)

Overeem faced [Stefan Struve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Struve "Stefan Struve") at [UFC on Fox 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_13 "UFC on Fox 13") on 13 December 2014.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-67) He won the fight via KO in the first round.

Overeem next faced [Roy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Nelson_(fighter) "Roy Nelson (fighter)") on 14 March 2015 at [UFC 185](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_185 "UFC 185").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-68) He won the fight by unanimous decision.

A bout with [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") was rescheduled for 19 December 2015 at [UFC on Fox 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_17 "UFC on Fox 17").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-69) He won the fight via TKO in the second round.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-70)

On 15 February 2016, Overeem announced that he had signed a new contract with the UFC.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-71)

Overeem faced [Andrei Arlovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Arlovski "Andrei Arlovski") on 8 May 2016 at [UFC Fight Night 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_87 "UFC Fight Night 87").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-headliner-72) He won the fight via TKO early in the second round.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-73) Subsequently, he earned his first _Performance of the Night_ bonus.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-74)

Overeem faced [Stipe Miocic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_Miocic "Stipe Miocic") for the [UFC Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UFC_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of UFC champions") on 10 September 2016 at [UFC 203](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_203 "UFC 203").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-75) Overeem dropped Miocic with a quick straight left punch before losing the fight via knockout in the first round.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-76) Both participants were awarded _Fight of the Night_ honors.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-77)

Overeem faced [Mark Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hunt "Mark Hunt") in a rematch on 4 March 2017 at [UFC 209](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_209 "UFC 209").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-78) He won the fight via knockout in the third round.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-79)

A third fight with [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") took place on 8 July 2017 at [UFC 213](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_213 "UFC 213").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-80) Overeem won the fight by majority decision.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-81)

Overeem faced [Francis Ngannou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ngannou "Francis Ngannou") on 2 December 2017 at [UFC 218](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_218 "UFC 218").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-82) He lost the fight via knockout in the first round.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-83)

Overeem faced [Curtis Blaydes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Blaydes "Curtis Blaydes") on 9 June 2018 at [UFC 225](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_225 "UFC 225").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-84) He lost the fight via TKO due to elbows in the third round.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-85)

Overeem faced promotional newcomer [Sergei Pavlovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Pavlovich "Sergei Pavlovich") on 24 November 2018 at [UFC Fight Night 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_141 "UFC Fight Night 141").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-86) He won the fight via TKO in the first round.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-87)

Overeem was expected to face [Alexander Volkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Volkov_(fighter) "Alexander Volkov (fighter)") on 20 April 2019 at [UFC Fight Night 149](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN+_7 "UFC on ESPN+ 7").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-88) Volkov was forced to withdraw from the bout, and was replaced by [Alexey Oleynik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexey_Oleynik "Alexey Oleynik").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-89) After a few back-and-forth exchanges, Overeem won the fight via technical knockout in round one.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-90)

Overeem was expected to face [Walt Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Harris_(fighter) "Walt Harris (fighter)") on 7 December 2019 at [UFC on ESPN 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_7 "UFC on ESPN 7").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-DCME-91) However, Harris pulled out on 1 November 2019 due to the ongoing search for his missing step-daughter,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-92) and he was replaced by [Jairzinho Rozenstruik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jairzinho_Rozenstruik "Jairzinho Rozenstruik").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-93) He lost the fight via knockout in the last four seconds of the fifth round after being up on all three judges' scorecards (39–37, 39–37, and 40–36).[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-94)

The bout with [Walt Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Harris_(fighter) "Walt Harris (fighter)") was rescheduled to take place on 11 April 2020 at [UFC Fight Night: Overeem vs. Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night:_Overeem_vs._Harris "UFC Fight Night: Overeem vs. Harris"). Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the event was eventually postponed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-95) The fight was rescheduled to 16 May 2020 at [UFC on ESPN: Overeem vs. Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN:_Overeem_vs._Harris "UFC on ESPN: Overeem vs. Harris").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-96) Overeem was dropped and almost finished early in the first round, but went onto dominate the fight with ground and pound, eventually finishing Harris with a head kick and more ground and pound for a second-round TKO win.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-97)

Overeem faced [Augusto Sakai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusto_Sakai "Augusto Sakai") on 5 September 2020 in the main event of [UFC Fight Night 176](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_176 "UFC Fight Night 176").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-98) He won the fight via technical knockout in the fifth round.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-99)

Overeem faced [Alexander Volkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Volkov_(fighter) "Alexander Volkov (fighter)") on 6 February 2021 at [UFC Fight Night 184](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_184 "UFC Fight Night 184").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-100) He lost the fight via technical knockout in round two.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-101)

On 3 March 2021, it was announced that Overeem had been released from his UFC contract.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-102)

## Kickboxing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Kickboxing career")]

Overeem had his first professional kickboxing fight at the age of 17, in a K-1 rules fight on 15 November 1997(1997-11-15), winning the fight. After that he fought against Paul Hordijk, winning by decision on 14 March 1999(1999-03-14). Overeem then moved on to K-1, having two K-1 fights in six years against Errol Parris and [Glaube Feitosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaube_Feitosa "Glaube Feitosa"). Overeem was knocked out in both bouts and stayed with MMA from then on. He did not fight in K-1 for four more years.

On 31 December 2008, Overeem faced [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari"), one of K-1's top contenders, under K-1 rules at [Dynamite!! 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2008 "Dynamite!! 2008"). He defeated Hari by way of knockout in the first round.

### K-1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: K-1")]

On 28 March 2009 he faced [Remy Bonjasky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remy_Bonjasky "Remy Bonjasky"), the defending K-1 Champion, at the [K-1 World GP 2009 in Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_GP_2009_in_Yokohama "K-1 World GP 2009 in Yokohama"). Overeem had success in the first and second rounds, but was knocked down by a right hook from Bonjasky in the third, who secured a unanimous decision win. All three judges scored the bout 30–28 in favour of Bonjasky.

On 26 September, at the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2009_Final_16 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final 16"), having been selected by fan voting after his impressive performances against [Remy Bonjasky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remy_Bonjasky "Remy Bonjasky") and [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari"), Overeem shocked the kickboxing world by achieving a huge upset. He defeated K-1's longest-serving member, legendary three-time champion [Peter Aerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Aerts "Peter Aerts"), by unanimous decision. At the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2009_Final "K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final"), Overeem knocked out the [Kyokushin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyokushin "Kyokushin") karate champion, [Ewerton Teixeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerton_Teixeira "Ewerton Teixeira"), with a knee strike in the first round, but lost to [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari") via TKO in the semifinals.

At the K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 in Yokohama, Overeem defeated [Dzevad Poturak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dzevad_Poturak "Dzevad Poturak") via KO (right knee) in round one at 2:40.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-103) Overeem defeated [Ben Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Edwards_(kickboxer) "Ben Edwards (kickboxer)") by TKO in the first round on 2 October 2010 at [K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2010_in_Seoul_Final_16 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 in Seoul Final 16"), which qualified him for the 2010 K-1 World Grand Prix.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-104)

On 11 December, at the [Ariake Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariake_Coliseum "Ariake Coliseum"), Overeem won the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2010_Final "K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final"). In the quarterfinals, he beat [Tyrone Spong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrone_Spong "Tyrone Spong") by unanimous decision (29–27, 29–28, and 29–27). In the semi-finals, he defeated [Gokhan Saki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gokhan_Saki "Gokhan Saki") by first-round TKO after breaking Saki's right arm with a left [middle kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundhouse_kick#Semi-circular_kick "Roundhouse kick"). Saki's arm was already injured as a result of his previous fight with Daniel Ghita. In the finals, he fought [Peter Aerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Aerts "Peter Aerts") for a second time. Overeem came out aggressively and finished Aerts in the first round.

### Glory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Glory")]

Over a decade removed from his previous kickboxing bouts, news surfaced on 8 June 2021, that Overeem had signed a multi-fight contract with [Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory_(kickboxing) "Glory (kickboxing)").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-reemglory-105)

Overeem was scheduled to challenge the reigning [Glory Heavyweight champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory_(kickboxing)#Glory_Heavyweight_Championship "Glory (kickboxing)")[Rico Verhoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rico_Verhoeven "Rico Verhoeven") at [Glory: Collision 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_Glory#Glory:_Collision_3 "2021 in Glory") on 23 October 2021.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-106) On 6 October 2021 it was announced that Overeem had to withdraw from the event due to an injury.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-107) He was replaced by former Glory heavyweight title challenger [Jamal Ben Saddik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Ben_Saddik "Jamal Ben Saddik").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-108)

Overeem faced [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari") on 8 October 2022 at [Glory: Collision 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_in_Glory#Glory:_Collision_4 "2022 in Glory").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-109) He won the fight via unanimous decision.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-110) On 21 November 2022, it was revealed that Overeem had tested positive for a banned substance.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-111) After a few months the B- Sample was also tested positive the decision was overturned to a No-Contest due to the use of Performance-enhancing Drugs.

## Fighting style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Fighting style")]

Overeem is considered one of the most well-rounded heavyweights in the sport,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-116) though he is mainly known for his excellence and power in the striking field.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117) A kickboxer of the Dutch school of [Muay Thai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muay_Thai "Muay Thai") decorated in [K-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1 "K-1") world tournaments,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Ency-118) Overeem favours [kicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick "Kick") to the body and legs and [knee strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_strike "Knee strike") from the [clinch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinch_(grappling) "Clinch (grappling)"),[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) which have been described as "devastating."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117) His most famous finishing technique used to be the left knee to the midsection, which he has utilised to end many fights, but he switched to the left body kick instead late in his career.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) He is also proficient with left [overhands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overhand_(boxing) "Overhand (boxing)") and [hooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_(boxing) "Hook (boxing)") once his opponents are worn down.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) On the grappling field, Overeem is universally known for his usage of the [guillotine choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillotine_choke "Guillotine choke"),[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Ency-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) a simple technique he uses to great effect thanks to his strength and height.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) Overeem was labeled as "the best grappler in Europe" after submitting all his opponents in the ADCC 2005 tryouts through this move.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-120)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Overeem's great-great-grandfather was enslaved on the island of Jamaica. He became a free man and bought a large tract of land on which he started a village, which has survived and prospered to this day. His Dutch mother is a descendant of [King William III of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_William_III_of_the_Netherlands "King William III of the Netherlands") through one of his many illegitimate children.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-121)

Overeem has a cameo appearance in the music video for [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s hit single "[Sexy and I Know It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy_and_I_Know_It "Sexy and I Know It")".[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-122)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

In 2009, Alistair and his brother were involved in an altercation at a Dutch [dance club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_club "Dance club"). Alistair started arguing with a bouncer when he found himself without coins to pay the [toilet attendant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay_toilet "Pay toilet") and was asked to leave by five other security workers. Valentijn intervened in his favor and was hit in the face with a [flash light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_light "Flash light"), which incited a brawl. The incident ended with five bouncers having to go urgently to the hospital and Alistair being forced to turn down a title fight due to a hand injury gained in the brawl.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-123)

On 1 January 2012, following his match with [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141"), Overeem shoved a woman in the face, "causing her to stagger back," at the [Wynn Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynn_Las_Vegas "Wynn Las Vegas") at about 3 a.m., according to the [Las Vegas Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Police_Department "Las Vegas Police Department"). Not arrested but summoned to court, Overeem was charged with [misdemeanor battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_(crime) "Battery (crime)") and faced a maximum of six months in the Clark County Detention Center and a fine up to $1,000.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-124) On 28 March 2012, Overeem was given a 90-day county jail sentence that would be suspended depending on the completion of 50 hours of community service and anger management.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-125)

**Alistair Cees Overeem** (born 17 May 1980) is a Dutch former professional [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and [kickboxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickboxing "Kickboxing"). He is a former [Strikeforce Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Strikeforce champions"), [Dream Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dream_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Dream champions"), [K-1 World Grand Prix Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_K-1_champions#K-1_World_Grand_Prix_Champions "List of K-1 champions"), and was the first fighter to hold world titles in [MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and K-1 kickboxing at the same time. Overeem is also a one-time challenger for the [UFC Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship").

Overeem holds the UFC all-time record for highest significant strike accuracy in the promotion's history (74.3%)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-7).

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Overeem was born in [Hounslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hounslow "Hounslow"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England, to a [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaican_people "Jamaican people") father and a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people") mother, whose maternal great-grandmother was an illegitimate child of King [William III of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_III_of_the_Netherlands "William III of the Netherlands").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-9) When he was six years old, his parents divorced and he moved with his mother and older brother to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), where he grew up in the city of [Amersfoort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amersfoort "Amersfoort").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-10) As a child, Overeem started training martial arts with his older brother [Valentijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentijn_Overeem "Valentijn Overeem") in order to defend himself from [bullying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullying "Bullying"). He decided to pursue a competitive sports career by his brother's example, first in [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") and later [track and field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_Field "Track and Field") and [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11) At the age of 15, he followed Valentijn into [Chris Dolman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Dolman "Chris Dolman")'s [Martial Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_Arts "Martial Arts") gym to become a professional fighter.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Bleach-12) Alistair initially did not like the sport, as he was routinely beaten by more experienced students, but he changed his mind when he met [Bas Rutten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bas_Rutten "Bas Rutten") and [Joop Kasteel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joop_Kasteel "Joop Kasteel"), after which he fully dedicated himself to training.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Sto-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Bleach-12)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

Overeem had his first MMA professional fight at 19 years old, defeating [Ricardo Fyeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Fyeet "Ricardo Fyeet") by submission on 24 October 1999(1999-10-24) at _[It's Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Showtime\_(kickboxing) "It's Showtime (kickboxing)")_, the first event of the self-titled promotion.

### Early MMA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early MMA career")]

After posting a 10–3 record in [Fighting Network Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting_Network_Rings "Fighting Network Rings"), [M-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-1_Global "M-1 Global"), [It's Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Showtime_(kickboxing) "It's Showtime (kickboxing)"), and 2 Hot 2 Handle, Overeem debuted in the [Pride Fighting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Fighting_Championships "Pride Fighting Championships") on 20 July 2002, defeating Yusuke Imamura by TKO in 44 seconds.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-13)

### Pride FC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pride FC")]

Overeem won two more fights in Pride before entering the 2003 Pride Middleweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_Pride_FC#Pride_Total_Elimination_2003 "2003 in Pride FC") and losing to future [UFC Light heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship")[Chuck Liddell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Liddell "Chuck Liddell") in the quarterfinal match.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-14) Overeem rebounded to defeat [Tomohiko Hashimoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomohiko_Hashimoto "Tomohiko Hashimoto") at the Inoki Bom-Ba-Ye 2003 in 36 seconds.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-15) On 31 October 2004, Overeem fought [Hiromitsu Kanehara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiromitsu_Kanehara "Hiromitsu Kanehara"), defeating him by TKO in the second round at [Pride 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_28 "Pride 28").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-16) Overeem lost his next fight against [Brazilian Top Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Top_Team "Brazilian Top Team") fighter [Antônio Rogério Nogueira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Rog%C3%A9rio_Nogueira "Antônio Rogério Nogueira").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-17)

In 2005, Overeem entered the Pride Middleweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Total_Elimination_2005 "Pride Total Elimination 2005"), in which he defeated [UFC Light heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Light_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Light Heavyweight Championship")[Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") by submission in the opening round.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-18) Overeem moved on to fight [Igor Vovchanchyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Vovchanchyn "Igor Vovchanchyn") in the quarterfinals at [Pride Critical Countdown 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Critical_Countdown_2005 "Pride Critical Countdown 2005") and won via submission in under two minutes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-19) Overeem lost in the semifinals to the eventual champion [Maurício Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-20)

In February 2006, Overeem fought Russian Top Team favourite [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov"). Overeem won, dislocating Kharitonov's shoulder in the process. With his win over Kharitonov, Overeem secured a spot in the Pride 2006 Openweight Grand Prix at [Pride Total Elimination Absolute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Total_Elimination_Absolute "Pride Total Elimination Absolute"). He fought [Brazilian jiu-jitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu") specialist [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"), and lost via [kimura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armlock#Kimura "Armlock") in the second round.

### Debut in Strikeforce

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Debut in Strikeforce")]

On 9 June 2006, Overeem travelled to [San Jose, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California"), to win a rematch with [Vitor Belfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitor_Belfort "Vitor Belfort") by decision at [Strikeforce: Revenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Revenge "Strikeforce: Revenge").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-21)

### Return to Pride

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Return to Pride")]

A month later Overeem returned to Pride for a highly anticipated rematch with [Antônio Rogério Nogueira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Rog%C3%A9rio_Nogueira "Antônio Rogério Nogueira"). Overeem entered the fight with a heavily taped neck. After controlling the first round and a half with his striking, Overeem was stumbled from a punch, and Nogueira followed with a flurry of strikes. Worried Overeem would be more severely injured, his corner threw in the towel.

At [Pride Final Conflict Absolute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Final_Conflict_Absolute "Pride Final Conflict Absolute"), Overeem lost to [Ricardo Arona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Arona "Ricardo Arona"). Overeem was on the receiving end of a leg kick that caused a non-serious injury to his nerves, causing him to lose feeling in his foot and leg. Unable to mount much offence or defend against Arona, Overeem tapped out to avoid further injury.

He then suffered another KO loss to [Maurício Rua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_Rua "Maurício Rua") at [Pride 33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_33 "Pride 33"), but returned in June 2007 with a submission win over Michael Knaap at [K-1 Grand Prix in Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_GP_2007_in_Amsterdam "K-1 GP 2007 in Amsterdam") (despite [K-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1 "K-1") being a kickboxing promotion, the bout was fought under MMA rules).

On 17 September 2007, at the Hero's 10: Middleweight Tournament Final, Alistair faced [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov") again. Overeem showed solid movement as soon as the first round began, but he suffered a KO loss just before the end of the first round.

### Return to Strikeforce/DREAM/Dynamite

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Return to Strikeforce/DREAM/Dynamite")]

On 16 November 2007, Overeem defeated [Paul Buentello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Buentello "Paul Buentello") for the vacant [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions") by submission due to knee strikes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-22) On 15 June 2008 Overeem won by KO in the first round against Lee Tae-Hyun at DREAM 4. On 21 July 2008, Overeem defeated [K-1 World Grand Prix Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2001 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2001")[Mark Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hunt "Mark Hunt") in the first round by submission at [Dream 5: Lightweight Grand Prix 2008 Final Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_5 "Dream 5").

His next fight was against [Mirko Cro Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirko_Cro_Cop "Mirko Cro Cop") at [Dream 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_6 "Dream 6") on 23 September 2008.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-23) The bout was stopped about halfway through the first round and declared a no-contest, after Overeem landed multiple knees to the groin of Cro Cop.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-24)

Overeem was rumoured to be making his first title defence against [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers") on 6 June at [Strikeforce: Lawler vs. Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Lawler_vs._Shields "Strikeforce: Lawler vs. Shields"). However, a hand injury scuttled plans for the fight.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-25) According to Golden Glory manager Bas Boon, Overeem had suffered a hand infection following a nightclub brawl early May 2009. According to Boon, Alistair and his brother Valentijn, both heavyweights had been involved in an altercation that left five security staff needing hospital treatment and nearly cost Alistair his hand.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Hand,_Pullout-26)

Overeem was scheduled to make his first [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions") defence in a rematch against [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") at [Strikeforce: Carano vs. Cyborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Carano_vs._Cyborg "Strikeforce: Carano vs. Cyborg"), but had to pull out due to a hand injury, most likely caused from his nightclub brawl.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Hand,_Pullout-26)

Alistair defeated Tony Sylvester at Golden Glory's 10-year anniversary celebration with a standing guillotine choke.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-27) He used the same choke only eight days later to submit [James Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Thompson_(fighter) "James Thompson (fighter)") at [Dream 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_12 "Dream 12").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-28)

Overeem was set to face [Andrei Arlovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Arlovski "Andrei Arlovski") at [Dynamite!! 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2009 "Dynamite!! 2009"), but FEG instead opted to have him face [Kazuyuki Fujita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazuyuki_Fujita "Kazuyuki Fujita") to keep with the DREAM vs. Sengoku theme.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-29) Overeem quickly overpowered his opponent and recorded a knockout with a knee to the head.

Overeem next faced [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers") on 15 May 2010 at [Strikeforce: Heavy Artillery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Heavy_Artillery "Strikeforce: Heavy Artillery") to defend his [Strikeforce Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-30) He won the fight via TKO in the first round. In his post-fight interview, Overeem declared for another time that he wants to fight [Fedor Emelianenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor_Emelianenko "Fedor Emelianenko"), claiming that Fedor's management can no longer ignore his presence.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-31) The majority of Alistair Overeem's pre-fight training camp took place at the newly opened [Golden Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Glory "Golden Glory") Gym in [Pattaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattaya "Pattaya"), [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand"), where "The Demolition Man" concentrated on the further improvement of his [Muay Thai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muay_Thai "Muay Thai") skills.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-32)

Overeem faced [Todd Duffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Duffee "Todd Duffee") on 31 December 2010 at [Dynamite!! 2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2010 "Dynamite!! 2010").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-33) He defeated Duffee by way of knockout 19 seconds into the first round to win the interim [DREAM Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dream_champions#Heavyweight_Championship "List of Dream champions").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-34)

### Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix")]

In early 2011, Overeem was named as one of eight men that will take part of the Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix, alongside [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"), [Sergei Kharitonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Kharitonov "Sergei Kharitonov"), [Brett Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Rogers "Brett Rogers"), [Josh Barnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Barnett "Josh Barnett"), [Andrei Arlovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Arlovski "Andrei Arlovski"), [Antônio Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Silva_(fighter) "Antônio Silva (fighter)") and [Fedor Emelianenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor_Emelianenko "Fedor Emelianenko").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-35)

A rematch with [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") took place on 18 June 2011, at [Strikeforce: Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeforce:_Dallas "Strikeforce: Dallas") as part of an eight-man heavyweight tournament.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-36) Overeem defeated Werdum by unanimous decision (30–27, 30–27, and 29–28).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-37)

### Removal from GP/Strikeforce

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Removal from GP/Strikeforce")]

On 17 July, it was announced that Overeem was removed from the promotion's 2011 Heavyweight Grand Prix. Overeem went on to state that he felt the September date was too soon for him to return, and that he needed time to rest and heal after his 18 June quarterfinal decision win over [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum"). Overeem was swapped out for unbeaten up-and-comer [Daniel Cormier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Cormier "Daniel Cormier").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-38) Subsequently, on 29 July, it was announced that Overeem had been released from the Strikeforce organization as [Zuffa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuffa "Zuffa") exercised their right to eliminate the one remaining fight on his contract.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-40) It was revealed that the reason behind Overeem's release from Strikeforce was not due to his unwillingness to participate in the Grand Prix semi-finals, but due to Golden Glory's policy requiring that the money fighters made through fights be paid through their management first.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-41)

This disagreement led not only to Overeem's release but also other Golden Glory stars under a Zuffa contract, including former [Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Strikeforce_champions "List of Strikeforce champions")[Marloes Coenen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen"), [Norwegian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_people "Norwegian people") UFC Heavyweight [Jon Olav Einemo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Olav_Einemo "Jon Olav Einemo"), and even brother [Valentijn Overeem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentijn_Overeem "Valentijn Overeem"). Team Golden Glory leader Bas Boon stated he has since changed the policy, and that Alistair Overeem could come to the UFC under an exclusive deal if the right terms are offered, which he later received.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-42)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship (2011–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship (2011–2021)")]

After much speculation, on 6 September 2011 it was announced that Overeem had signed a contract with the [UFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"), and that his first fight would be against former [UFC Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship")[Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") on 30 December 2011 at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-44)

The lead up to the fight was rife with controversy. In November 2011, both competitors were required by the [NSAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_Athletic_Commission "Nevada Athletic Commission") to comply with out-of-competition drug testing. Lesnar delivered his sample screen on 21 November, while Overeem delivered his on 23 November. The screen, however, did not meet the standards of the commission. Overeem submitted a second test through his personal physician, which was also deemed unacceptable before flying out of the country. Overeem was ultimately given a conditional license for the fight by the committee during a meeting held on 12 December 2011.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-45)

On 30 December 2011, at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141"), Overeem made his UFC debut in the main event against [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-46) Overeem hurt Lesnar multiple times early on with knees to the body, and went on to finish the fight with a kick to the liver and subsequent punches at 2:26 of the first round. The victory earned him a heavyweight title shot against champion [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-47)

#### Failed drug test

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Failed drug test")]

Overeem was scheduled to fight [UFC Heavyweight Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Heavyweight_Championship "UFC Heavyweight Championship")[Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") on 26 May 2012 at [UFC 146](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_146 "UFC 146"). However, on 4 April 2012, Overeem was revealed to have failed his pre-fight drug test by the [Nevada State Athletic Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Athletic_Commission "Nevada State Athletic Commission") (NSAC).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-48) Overeem had a 14-to-1 testosterone-to-epitestosterone (T/E) ratio, over the allowed ratio rate of 6-to-1. On Friday 20 April 2012 UFC President [Dana White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_White "Dana White") confirmed that Overeem had been removed from his fight with dos Santos and replaced by [Frank Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Mir "Frank Mir").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-50)

One day prior to his meeting with the NSAC, Overeem released a prepared statement to the media in which he claims the positive result of the drug test came as a result of a doctor-prescribed "anti-inflammatory medication that was mixed with testosterone."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-51) Overeem's lawyer filed a continuation request for additional time to gather support for his recent claim, which was voted on by the NSAC on 24 April 2012.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-52) The request was denied and the NSAC voted unanimously to deny Overeem's application status for a period of nine months, dating back to 27 March, the day of his drug test. He was allowed to reapply after this time period in December 2012.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-53)

#### Return

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Return")]

Overeem returned to face [Antônio Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Silva_(fighter) "Antônio Silva (fighter)") on 2 February 2013 at [UFC 156](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_156 "UFC 156").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-54) Leading up to the fight, Overeem was dismissive of Silva's skills, claiming he was better than his opponent in every aspect of MMA.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-55) Despite being a heavy betting favourite and having won rounds one and two, an overconfident Overeem lost to Silva by KO in the third round.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-56)

Overeem was expected to face former UFC Heavyweight Champion [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") on 25 May 2013 at [UFC 160](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_160 "UFC 160").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-HW-57) However, in early March, Overeem pulled out of the bout, citing an injury[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-58) and was replaced by [Mark Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hunt "Mark Hunt").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-HuntIn-59)

For his third fight with the promotion, Overeem faced [Travis Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Browne "Travis Browne") in the co-main event at [UFC Fight Night 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_26 "UFC Fight Night 26") on 17 August 2013.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-60) Overeem was dominant early in the fight, attacking Browne with a flurry of knees and punches. Browne recovered and defeated Overeem via TKO with a front kick.

Overeem was scheduled to face [Frank Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Mir "Frank Mir") on 16 November 2013 at [UFC 167](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_167 "UFC 167").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-61) However, the pairing was moved to 1 February 2014 at [UFC 169](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_169 "UFC 169").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-62) He defeated Mir by unanimous decision and called out [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") in his post-fight interview.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-63)

Overeem injured his elbow and decided to take the time out to have surgery, expecting to return in September 2014.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-64) On 9 July, the UFC announced he would face [Ben Rothwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Rothwell "Ben Rothwell") on 5 September 2014 at [UFC Fight Night 50](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_50 "UFC Fight Night 50").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-65) Rothwell defeated Overeem via TKO in the first round.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-66)

Overeem faced [Stefan Struve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Struve "Stefan Struve") at [UFC on Fox 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_13 "UFC on Fox 13") on 13 December 2014.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-67) He won the fight via KO in the first round.

Overeem next faced [Roy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Nelson_(fighter) "Roy Nelson (fighter)") on 14 March 2015 at [UFC 185](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_185 "UFC 185").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-68) He won the fight by unanimous decision.

A bout with [Junior dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_dos_Santos "Junior dos Santos") was rescheduled for 19 December 2015 at [UFC on Fox 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_17 "UFC on Fox 17").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-69) He won the fight via TKO in the second round.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-70)

On 15 February 2016, Overeem announced that he had signed a new contract with the UFC.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-71)

A third fight with [Fabrício Werdum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabr%C3%ADcio_Werdum "Fabrício Werdum") took place on 8 July 2017 at [UFC 213](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_213 "UFC 213").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-80) Overeem won the fight by majority decision.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-81)

Overeem faced [Francis Ngannou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ngannou "Francis Ngannou") on 2 December 2017 at [UFC 218](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_218 "UFC 218").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-82) He lost the fight via knockout in the first round.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-83)

Overeem faced [Curtis Blaydes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Blaydes "Curtis Blaydes") on 9 June 2018 at [UFC 225](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_225 "UFC 225").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-84) He lost the fight via TKO due to elbows in the third round.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-85)

Overeem faced promotional newcomer [Sergei Pavlovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Pavlovich "Sergei Pavlovich") on 24 November 2018 at [UFC Fight Night 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_141 "UFC Fight Night 141").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-86) He won the fight via TKO in the first round.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-87)
