## Kickboxing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Kickboxing career")]

Overeem had his first professional kickboxing fight at the age of 17, in a K-1 rules fight on 15 November 1997(1997-11-15), winning the fight. After that he fought against Paul Hordijk, winning by decision on 14 March 1999(1999-03-14). Overeem then moved on to K-1, having two K-1 fights in six years against Errol Parris and [Glaube Feitosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaube_Feitosa "Glaube Feitosa"). Overeem was knocked out in both bouts and stayed with MMA from then on. He did not fight in K-1 for four more years.

On 31 December 2008, Overeem faced [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari"), one of K-1's top contenders, under K-1 rules at [Dynamite!! 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite!!_2008 "Dynamite!! 2008"). He defeated Hari by way of knockout in the first round.

### K-1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: K-1")]

On 28 March 2009 he faced [Remy Bonjasky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remy_Bonjasky "Remy Bonjasky"), the defending K-1 Champion, at the [K-1 World GP 2009 in Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_GP_2009_in_Yokohama "K-1 World GP 2009 in Yokohama"). Overeem had success in the first and second rounds, but was knocked down by a right hook from Bonjasky in the third, who secured a unanimous decision win. All three judges scored the bout 30–28 in favour of Bonjasky.

On 26 September, at the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2009_Final_16 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final 16"), having been selected by fan voting after his impressive performances against [Remy Bonjasky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remy_Bonjasky "Remy Bonjasky") and [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari"), Overeem shocked the kickboxing world by achieving a huge upset. He defeated K-1's longest-serving member, legendary three-time champion [Peter Aerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Aerts "Peter Aerts"), by unanimous decision. At the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2009_Final "K-1 World Grand Prix 2009 Final"), Overeem knocked out the [Kyokushin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyokushin "Kyokushin") karate champion, [Ewerton Teixeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerton_Teixeira "Ewerton Teixeira"), with a knee strike in the first round, but lost to [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari") via TKO in the semifinals.

At the K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 in Yokohama, Overeem defeated [Dzevad Poturak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dzevad_Poturak "Dzevad Poturak") via KO (right knee) in round one at 2:40.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-103) Overeem defeated [Ben Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Edwards_(kickboxer) "Ben Edwards (kickboxer)") by TKO in the first round on 2 October 2010 at [K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2010_in_Seoul_Final_16 "K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 in Seoul Final 16"), which qualified him for the 2010 K-1 World Grand Prix.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-104)

On 11 December, at the [Ariake Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariake_Coliseum "Ariake Coliseum"), Overeem won the [K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1_World_Grand_Prix_2010_Final "K-1 World Grand Prix 2010 Final"). In the quarterfinals, he beat [Tyrone Spong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrone_Spong "Tyrone Spong") by unanimous decision (29–27, 29–28, and 29–27). In the semi-finals, he defeated [Gokhan Saki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gokhan_Saki "Gokhan Saki") by first-round TKO after breaking Saki's right arm with a left [middle kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundhouse_kick#Semi-circular_kick "Roundhouse kick"). Saki's arm was already injured as a result of his previous fight with Daniel Ghita. In the finals, he fought [Peter Aerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Aerts "Peter Aerts") for a second time. Overeem came out aggressively and finished Aerts in the first round.

### Glory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Glory")]

Over a decade removed from his previous kickboxing bouts, news surfaced on 8 June 2021, that Overeem had signed a multi-fight contract with [Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory_(kickboxing) "Glory (kickboxing)").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-reemglory-105)

Overeem was scheduled to challenge the reigning [Glory Heavyweight champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory_(kickboxing)#Glory_Heavyweight_Championship "Glory (kickboxing)")[Rico Verhoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rico_Verhoeven "Rico Verhoeven") at [Glory: Collision 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_Glory#Glory:_Collision_3 "2021 in Glory") on 23 October 2021.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-106) On 6 October 2021 it was announced that Overeem had to withdraw from the event due to an injury.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-107) He was replaced by former Glory heavyweight title challenger [Jamal Ben Saddik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Ben_Saddik "Jamal Ben Saddik").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-108)

Overeem faced [Badr Hari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badr_Hari "Badr Hari") on 8 October 2022 at [Glory: Collision 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_in_Glory#Glory:_Collision_4 "2022 in Glory").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-109) He won the fight via unanimous decision.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-110) On 21 November 2022, it was revealed that Overeem had tested positive for a banned substance.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-111) After a few months the B- Sample was also tested positive the decision was overturned to a No-Contest due to the use of Performance-enhancing Drugs.

## Fighting style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Fighting style")]

Overeem is considered one of the most well-rounded heavyweights in the sport,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-116) though he is mainly known for his excellence and power in the striking field.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117) A kickboxer of the Dutch school of [Muay Thai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muay_Thai "Muay Thai") decorated in [K-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-1 "K-1") world tournaments,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Ency-118) Overeem favours [kicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick "Kick") to the body and legs and [knee strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_strike "Knee strike") from the [clinch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinch_(grappling) "Clinch (grappling)"),[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) which have been described as "devastating."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117) His most famous finishing technique used to be the left knee to the midsection, which he has utilised to end many fights, but he switched to the left body kick instead late in his career.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) He is also proficient with left [overhands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overhand_(boxing) "Overhand (boxing)") and [hooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_(boxing) "Hook (boxing)") once his opponents are worn down.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) On the grappling field, Overeem is universally known for his usage of the [guillotine choke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillotine_choke "Guillotine choke"),[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Choke-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-Ency-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) a simple technique he uses to great effect thanks to his strength and height.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-strength-119) Overeem was labeled as "the best grappler in Europe" after submitting all his opponents in the ADCC 2005 tryouts through this move.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-120)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Overeem's great-great-grandfather was enslaved on the island of Jamaica. He became a free man and bought a large tract of land on which he started a village, which has survived and prospered to this day. His Dutch mother is a descendant of [King William III of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_William_III_of_the_Netherlands "King William III of the Netherlands") through one of his many illegitimate children.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-121)

Overeem has a cameo appearance in the music video for [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s hit single "[Sexy and I Know It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy_and_I_Know_It "Sexy and I Know It")".[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-122)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alistair_Overeem&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

In 2009, Alistair and his brother were involved in an altercation at a Dutch [dance club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_club "Dance club"). Alistair started arguing with a bouncer when he found himself without coins to pay the [toilet attendant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay_toilet "Pay toilet") and was asked to leave by five other security workers. Valentijn intervened in his favor and was hit in the face with a [flash light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_light "Flash light"), which incited a brawl. The incident ended with five bouncers having to go urgently to the hospital and Alistair being forced to turn down a title fight due to a hand injury gained in the brawl.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-123)

On 1 January 2012, following his match with [Brock Lesnar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brock_Lesnar "Brock Lesnar") at [UFC 141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_141 "UFC 141"), Overeem shoved a woman in the face, "causing her to stagger back," at the [Wynn Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynn_Las_Vegas "Wynn Las Vegas") at about 3 a.m., according to the [Las Vegas Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Police_Department "Las Vegas Police Department"). Not arrested but summoned to court, Overeem was charged with [misdemeanor battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_(crime) "Battery (crime)") and faced a maximum of six months in the Clark County Detention Center and a fine up to $1,000.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-124) On 28 March 2012, Overeem was given a 90-day county jail sentence that would be suspended depending on the completion of 50 hours of community service and anger management.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Overeem#cite_note-125)

## Background

Penelope López Márquez, popularly known as Arianny Celeste, was born in the United States on November 12, 1985, in Las Vegas, Nevada. She is a ring girl for U.F.C. and a model known for co-hosting the custom car show “Overhaulin’” and has also been featured in “Playboy” magazine several times. She made her U.F.C. debut in 2006 at the Hard Rock Hotel and Casino in Paradise, Nevada. In that same year, she won the title of ‘Ring Girl of the Year’ as dictated by “Fighters Only” magazine.

Celeste has won this title several times throughout her career, showing just how talented she is. She won the title consecutively four times from 2008, at the first World M.M.A. Awards, to 2011, when she beat Brittney Palmer. The year 2012 was the first year that someone other than Celeste had won the title, with her being nominated but beaten by Palmer. Celeste lost to Palmer again in 2013, making it her second consecutive loss. In 2014, Celeste and Palmer were both nominated for the 2014 ‘Ring Girl of the Year’ award at the World M.M.A. Awards. Celeste won, regaining her title and making it her fifth time to have won the award and setting a new record.

Other than being a ring girl and model, Celeste has also been the host and co-host on many shows. This includes a 2010 online exclusive U.F.C. show called “U.F.C. Ultimate Insider” where she and Joe Rogan interviewed various U.F.C. fighters and talked about upcoming matches, P.P.V.s, as well as highlights from previous events. Celeste has also been the co-host of the television series “Overhaulin’” from 2014 to 2015, appearing in seven episodes.

## Why We Love Arianny Celeste

1.   ### She stands up against bullies

In 2015, former U.F.C. bantamweight champion, Ronda Rousey, argued that ring girls were paid too much compared to the fighters. Celeste openly protested this and called Rousey a bully and stated that being a ring girl is harder than it seems. 
2.   ### Her legacy

Celeste has become a household name in the world of M.M.A. and U.F.C. and she has even been honored with appearances as a judge for the 2011 Hooters International Swimsuit Pageant. Not only that, but she also appears in several U.F.C. video games as an octagon girl. 
3.   ### Charity work

Celeste has done a lot of charity work throughout her career. Most notably, she and a friend auctioned off their sports bras on eBay in 2013 to raise money for breast cancer research.

**Cristiane Justino Venâncio** (born July 9, 1985), known as **Cris Cyborg**, is a Brazilian-American professional [mixed martial artist](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and [boxer](https://kids.kiddle.co/Boxing "Boxing"). She competes in the PFL. She is the first and current PFL Super Fights Women's World Featherweight Champion.

Cris Cyborg was also the longest-reigning and last Women’s Featherweight World Champion in Bellator MMA. She has also held titles in the [UFC](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"), Strikeforce, and Invicta FC. She is the only MMA fighter to win world championships in five major MMA organizations. Many people consider Cyborg to be one of the greatest female mixed martial artists ever.

She became famous on August 15, 2009. She won the Strikeforce title by defeating [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano"). This was a big moment as it was the first time women headlined a major fighting event.

## Early Life and Sports

Cris Cyborg was born on July 9, 1985, in [Curitiba](https://kids.kiddle.co/Curitiba "Curitiba"), Brazil. Her parents were Brazilian. She started playing [handball](https://kids.kiddle.co/Handball "Handball") at age twelve. She played at a national level in Brazil.

Because she was so good at handball, she earned many scholarships for college. She chose to study physical education in Curitiba. She planned to become a professional handball player. However, a trainer named Rudimar Fedrigo noticed her. He was impressed by her physical strength. He suggested she try fighting.

Cris Cyborg said about starting her fighting career: "I was playing in a friendly handball tournament. One of the boys, Jorginho, knew Mestre Rafael and Mestre Rudimar. He saw me playing handball and asked if I liked fighting. I said I thought it was cool, but I had never done it. He invited me to a [Muay Thai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Thai_boxing "Thai boxing") class, and I really liked it!"

## Mixed Martial Arts Career

### Starting Her Journey

Cris Justino, before she was known as "Cyborg," had her first professional MMA fight on May 17, 2005. She was 19 years old. She fought Erica Paes, a world champion in [Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu](https://kids.kiddle.co/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu"). Cris lost this first fight. It was her only loss in MMA until 2018.

After her first fight, Cris Cyborg won her next match against Vanessa Porto. She then won three more fights in Brazil. She won these by TKO (technical knockout) in the first round.

She made her debut in the United States on July 26, 2008. She fought Shayna Baszler and won by TKO in the second round. She also defeated Yoko Takahashi by decision on October 4, 2008.

### Strikeforce Success

[![Image 7: Cristiane Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/2/22/Cristiane_Santos.jpg/300px-Cristiane_Santos.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cristiane_Santos.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cristiane_Santos.jpg "Enlarge")

 Cyborg in 2009

Cris Cyborg then signed with Strikeforce. This made a fight with [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano") more likely. In her first Strikeforce fight, she faced Hitomi Akano on April 11, 2009. Cyborg won by TKO in the third round.

On August 15, 2009, she fought [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano") for the Women's Featherweight Championship. Cyborg won by TKO in the first round. This event was historic because it was the first time women were the main event in a major fighting promotion. After the fight, she showed great respect for Carano.

She defended her title against [Marloes Coenen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen") on January 30, 2010. She won by TKO in the third round. She also defended her title against Jan Finney on June 26, 2010, winning by KO in the second round.

#### A Challenge with a Banned Substance

On December 17, 2011, Cyborg fought Hiroko Yamanaka. She won by TKO very quickly. However, on January 6, 2012, it was announced that Cyborg had tested positive for a banned substance. Because of this, the fight result was changed to "no contest." Her license was suspended for one year.

### Invicta Fighting Championships

After Strikeforce closed, Cyborg signed with Invicta Fighting Championships in 2013. She won her first fight back against Fiona Muxlow by TKO in the first round.

Cyborg then fought [Marloes Coenen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen") again for the first-ever Invicta FC Featherweight Championship. This happened on July 13, 2013. Cyborg won by TKO in the fourth round, becoming the first Invicta FC featherweight champion.

She defended her Invicta Featherweight title against Charmaine Tweet in February 2015. She won by TKO in less than a minute. She also defeated Faith Van Duin by TKO in July 2015.

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

In March 2015, Cyborg signed with the [UFC](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"). She made her UFC debut on May 14, 2016, against Leslie Smith. She won by TKO in the first round.

Cyborg fought Lina Länsberg on September 24, 2016, and won by TKO in the second round.

In March 2017, Cyborg gave up her Invicta featherweight title. She was set to fight for the vacant UFC Women's Featherweight Championship at UFC 214. Her opponent changed, and she ended up fighting Tonya Evinger. Cyborg won by TKO in the third round, claiming her first UFC championship.

She defended her UFC title against [Holly Holm](https://kids.kiddle.co/Holly_Holm "Holly Holm") on December 30, 2017. She won by unanimous decision. This fight also earned her a "Fight of the Night" bonus.

Cyborg defended her title again on March 3, 2018, against [Yana Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/Yana_Santos "Yana Santos") at UFC 222. She won by TKO in the first round. After this win, she celebrated by giving out 222 burgers to people experiencing homelessness in Los Angeles.

On December 29, 2018, Cyborg faced [Amanda Nunes](https://kids.kiddle.co/Amanda_Nunes "Amanda Nunes"), who was the UFC Women's Bantamweight champion. Nunes defeated Cyborg by knockout in the first round. This was Cyborg's first knockout loss in her MMA career.

Cyborg's last fight in the UFC was against Felicia Spencer on July 27, 2019. She won by unanimous decision. After this fight, her contract with the UFC ended.

### Bellator MMA

On September 3, 2019, Cris Cyborg signed a deal with Bellator MMA.

She fought [Julia Budd](https://kids.kiddle.co/Julia_Budd "Julia Budd") for the Bellator Women's Featherweight Championship on January 25, 2020. She won by technical knockout in the fourth round. This made her a champion in her fourth major MMA promotion.

Cyborg defended her Bellator title against Arlene Blencowe on October 15, 2020. She won by submission in the second round. This was her first submission win in her MMA career.

She defended her title again against Leslie Smith on May 21, 2021. She won by TKO in the fifth round. Cyborg also defended her title against Sinead Kavanagh on November 12, 2021, winning by knockout in the first round.

On April 23, 2022, Cyborg defended her title in a rematch against Arlene Blencowe. She won by unanimous decision. After this, Cyborg became a free agent.

After being away from MMA for 17 months, Cyborg returned to defend her title against Cat Zingano on October 7, 2023. She won the fight by TKO in the first round.

### Professional Fighters League

On October 19, 2024, Cyborg faced Larissa Pacheco for the PFL Women's Featherweight Superfight Championship. She won the fight by unanimous decision, becoming the first champion in this new division.

## Boxing Career

Cris Cyborg started her professional boxing career on September 25, 2022. She fought Simone Silva and won by unanimous decision.

In her second boxing match on December 11, 2022, she fought Gabrielle Holloway. Cyborg won by unanimous decision. This event set a record for the largest boxing crowd in Nebraska.

On January 19, 2024, Cyborg knocked out Kelsey Wickstrum in the first round. This was her first knockout win in boxing. She then defeated Aria Wild by TKO on June 15, 2024.

After winning her PFL title, Cyborg returned to boxing on March 3, 2025. She defeated Karen Fernandez by knockout in the second round. Just 17 days later, she knocked out Valentina Angarita in the third round. On May 17, 2025, she earned her fifth overall knockout in boxing by stopping Precious Harris-McCray in the second round.

## Personal Life

Cris Cyborg was married to fellow mixed martial artist [Evangelista "Cyborg" Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/Evangelista_Santos "Evangelista Santos"). She adopted his nickname. They separated in December 2011. She became a U.S. citizen in 2016. In 2017, Cyborg announced her engagement to Ray Elbe, who is a trainer and former MMA athlete.

In 2018, Cyborg adopted her teenage niece. This made her the first mother to hold a UFC championship belt.

Cyborg also works with "Fight for the Forgotten." This group helps dig wells to provide clean drinking water for the Batwa people. After her first submission victory in MMA, she earned her Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt.

**Cristiane Justino Venâncio** (born July 9, 1985), known as **Cris Cyborg**, is a Brazilian-American professional [mixed martial artist](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") and [boxer](https://kids.kiddle.co/Boxing "Boxing"). She competes in the PFL. She is the first and current PFL Super Fights Women's World Featherweight Champion.

Cris Cyborg was also the longest-reigning and last Women’s Featherweight World Champion in Bellator MMA. She has also held titles in the [UFC](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"), Strikeforce, and Invicta FC. She is the only MMA fighter to win world championships in five major MMA organizations. Many people consider Cyborg to be one of the greatest female mixed martial artists ever.

She became famous on August 15, 2009. She won the Strikeforce title by defeating [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano"). This was a big moment as it was the first time women headlined a major fighting event.

## Early Life and Sports

Cris Cyborg was born on July 9, 1985, in [Curitiba](https://kids.kiddle.co/Curitiba "Curitiba"), Brazil. Her parents were Brazilian. She started playing [handball](https://kids.kiddle.co/Handball "Handball") at age twelve. She played at a national level in Brazil.

Because she was so good at handball, she earned many scholarships for college. She chose to study physical education in Curitiba. She planned to become a professional handball player. However, a trainer named Rudimar Fedrigo noticed her. He was impressed by her physical strength. He suggested she try fighting.

Cris Cyborg said about starting her fighting career: "I was playing in a friendly handball tournament. One of the boys, Jorginho, knew Mestre Rafael and Mestre Rudimar. He saw me playing handball and asked if I liked fighting. I said I thought it was cool, but I had never done it. He invited me to a [Muay Thai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Thai_boxing "Thai boxing") class, and I really liked it!"

## Mixed Martial Arts Career

### Starting Her Journey

Cris Justino, before she was known as "Cyborg," had her first professional MMA fight on May 17, 2005. She was 19 years old. She fought Erica Paes, a world champion in [Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu](https://kids.kiddle.co/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu"). Cris lost this first fight. It was her only loss in MMA until 2018.

After her first fight, Cris Cyborg won her next match against Vanessa Porto. She then won three more fights in Brazil. She won these by TKO (technical knockout) in the first round.

She made her debut in the United States on July 26, 2008. She fought Shayna Baszler and won by TKO in the second round. She also defeated Yoko Takahashi by decision on October 4, 2008.

### Strikeforce Success

[![Image 7: Cristiane Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/2/22/Cristiane_Santos.jpg/300px-Cristiane_Santos.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cristiane_Santos.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cristiane_Santos.jpg "Enlarge")

 Cyborg in 2009

Cris Cyborg then signed with Strikeforce. This made a fight with [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano") more likely. In her first Strikeforce fight, she faced Hitomi Akano on April 11, 2009. Cyborg won by TKO in the third round.

On August 15, 2009, she fought [Gina Carano](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gina_Carano "Gina Carano") for the Women's Featherweight Championship. Cyborg won by TKO in the first round. This event was historic because it was the first time women were the main event in a major fighting promotion. After the fight, she showed great respect for Carano.

She defended her title against [Marloes Coenen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen") on January 30, 2010. She won by TKO in the third round. She also defended her title against Jan Finney on June 26, 2010, winning by KO in the second round.

#### A Challenge with a Banned Substance

On December 17, 2011, Cyborg fought Hiroko Yamanaka. She won by TKO very quickly. However, on January 6, 2012, it was announced that Cyborg had tested positive for a banned substance. Because of this, the fight result was changed to "no contest." Her license was suspended for one year.

### Invicta Fighting Championships

After Strikeforce closed, Cyborg signed with Invicta Fighting Championships in 2013. She won her first fight back against Fiona Muxlow by TKO in the first round.

Cyborg then fought [Marloes Coenen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marloes_Coenen "Marloes Coenen") again for the first-ever Invicta FC Featherweight Championship. This happened on July 13, 2013. Cyborg won by TKO in the fourth round, becoming the first Invicta FC featherweight champion.

She defended her Invicta Featherweight title against Charmaine Tweet in February 2015. She won by TKO in less than a minute. She also defeated Faith Van Duin by TKO in July 2015.

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

In March 2015, Cyborg signed with the [UFC](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship"). She made her UFC debut on May 14, 2016, against Leslie Smith. She won by TKO in the first round.

Cyborg fought Lina Länsberg on September 24, 2016, and won by TKO in the second round.

In March 2017, Cyborg gave up her Invicta featherweight title. She was set to fight for the vacant UFC Women's Featherweight Championship at UFC 214. Her opponent changed, and she ended up fighting Tonya Evinger. Cyborg won by TKO in the third round, claiming her first UFC championship.

She defended her UFC title against [Holly Holm](https://kids.kiddle.co/Holly_Holm "Holly Holm") on December 30, 2017. She won by unanimous decision. This fight also earned her a "Fight of the Night" bonus.

Cyborg defended her title again on March 3, 2018, against [Yana Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/Yana_Santos "Yana Santos") at UFC 222. She won by TKO in the first round. After this win, she celebrated by giving out 222 burgers to people experiencing homelessness in Los Angeles.

On December 29, 2018, Cyborg faced [Amanda Nunes](https://kids.kiddle.co/Amanda_Nunes "Amanda Nunes"), who was the UFC Women's Bantamweight champion. Nunes defeated Cyborg by knockout in the first round. This was Cyborg's first knockout loss in her MMA career.

Cyborg's last fight in the UFC was against Felicia Spencer on July 27, 2019. She won by unanimous decision. After this fight, her contract with the UFC ended.

### Bellator MMA

On September 3, 2019, Cris Cyborg signed a deal with Bellator MMA.

She fought [Julia Budd](https://kids.kiddle.co/Julia_Budd "Julia Budd") for the Bellator Women's Featherweight Championship on January 25, 2020. She won by technical knockout in the fourth round. This made her a champion in her fourth major MMA promotion.

Cyborg defended her Bellator title against Arlene Blencowe on October 15, 2020. She won by submission in the second round. This was her first submission win in her MMA career.

She defended her title again against Leslie Smith on May 21, 2021. She won by TKO in the fifth round. Cyborg also defended her title against Sinead Kavanagh on November 12, 2021, winning by knockout in the first round.

On April 23, 2022, Cyborg defended her title in a rematch against Arlene Blencowe. She won by unanimous decision. After this, Cyborg became a free agent.

After being away from MMA for 17 months, Cyborg returned to defend her title against Cat Zingano on October 7, 2023. She won the fight by TKO in the first round.

### Professional Fighters League

On October 19, 2024, Cyborg faced Larissa Pacheco for the PFL Women's Featherweight Superfight Championship. She won the fight by unanimous decision, becoming the first champion in this new division.

## Boxing Career

Cris Cyborg started her professional boxing career on September 25, 2022. She fought Simone Silva and won by unanimous decision.

In her second boxing match on December 11, 2022, she fought Gabrielle Holloway. Cyborg won by unanimous decision. This event set a record for the largest boxing crowd in Nebraska.

On January 19, 2024, Cyborg knocked out Kelsey Wickstrum in the first round. This was her first knockout win in boxing. She then defeated Aria Wild by TKO on June 15, 2024.

After winning her PFL title, Cyborg returned to boxing on March 3, 2025. She defeated Karen Fernandez by knockout in the second round. Just 17 days later, she knocked out Valentina Angarita in the third round. On May 17, 2025, she earned her fifth overall knockout in boxing by stopping Precious Harris-McCray in the second round.

## Personal Life

Cris Cyborg was married to fellow mixed martial artist [Evangelista "Cyborg" Santos](https://kids.kiddle.co/Evangelista_Santos "Evangelista Santos"). She adopted his nickname. They separated in December 2011. She became a U.S. citizen in 2016. In 2017, Cyborg announced her engagement to Ray Elbe, who is a trainer and former MMA athlete.

In 2018, Cyborg adopted her teenage niece. This made her the first mother to hold a UFC championship belt.

Cyborg also works with "Fight for the Forgotten." This group helps dig wells to provide clean drinking water for the Batwa people. After her first submission victory in MMA, she earned her Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt.

**Jason Saggo** (born November 23, 1985) is a Canadian [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") who previously fought in the lightweight division of the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC).

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Saggo graduated from [University of Guelph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Guelph "University of Guelph").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-3)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

Saggo made his professional debut in August 2009, winning a fight in Northern Ireland. He amassed a record of 9–1, competing primarily for various regional promotions in Canada before signing with the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") in the spring of 2014.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-4)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship")]

Saggo made his promotional debut against [Josh Shockley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Shockley "Josh Shockley") on June 14, 2014, at [UFC 174](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_174 "UFC 174").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-5) Saggo defeated Shockley via first round TKO.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-6)

Saggo faced promotional newcomer [Paul Felder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Felder "Paul Felder") on October 4, 2014, at [UFC Fight Night 54](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_54 "UFC Fight Night 54").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-7) Saggo lost the fight by split decision.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-8)

Saggo was expected to face [Marcin Bandel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcin_Bandel "Marcin Bandel") on April 11, 2015, at [UFC Fight Night 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_64 "UFC Fight Night 64").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-9) However, Saggo pulled out of the bout due to an injury to his achilles tendon and was replaced by promotional newcomer Stevie Ray.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-10)

Saggo faced [Justin Salas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Salas "Justin Salas") on March 5, 2016, at [UFC 196](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_196 "UFC 196").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-11) He won the fight via TKO in the first round.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-12)

Saggo next faced [Leandro Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leandro_Silva_(MMA) "Leandro Silva (MMA)") on June 18, 2016, at [UFC Fight Night 89](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_89 "UFC Fight Night 89").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-13) He won the fight via split decision.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-14)

Saggo faced [Rustam Khabilov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rustam_Khabilov "Rustam Khabilov") on December 10, 2016, at [UFC 206](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_206 "UFC 206").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-15) He lost the one-sided fight via unanimous decision.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-16)

Saggo faced [Gilbert Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Burns_(fighter) "Gilbert Burns (fighter)") on September 16, 2017, at [UFC Fight Night 116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_116 "UFC Fight Night 116").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-17) He lost the fight via knockout in the second round.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-18) He was subsequently released from the UFC.

### BTC Fight Promotions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: BTC Fight Promotions")]

Following his release from the UFC, Saggo signed a multi-fight deal with BTC Fight Promotions out of Burlington, Ontario. He had his first fight on November 24, 2018, against Adam Assenza at BTC 4 for the BTC Lightweight Championship and won via first round rear-naked choke.

On May 9, Saggo vacated the lightweight title in preparation for a catchweight bout against Deivison Ribeiro on June 1, 2019, at BTC 6.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-19)

**Jason Saggo** (born November 23, 1985) is a Canadian [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") who previously fought in the lightweight division of the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC).

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Saggo graduated from [University of Guelph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Guelph "University of Guelph").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-3)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

Saggo made his professional debut in August 2009, winning a fight in Northern Ireland. He amassed a record of 9–1, competing primarily for various regional promotions in Canada before signing with the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") in the spring of 2014.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-4)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship")]

Saggo made his promotional debut against [Josh Shockley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Shockley "Josh Shockley") on June 14, 2014, at [UFC 174](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_174 "UFC 174").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-5) Saggo defeated Shockley via first round TKO.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-6)

Saggo faced promotional newcomer [Paul Felder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Felder "Paul Felder") on October 4, 2014, at [UFC Fight Night 54](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_54 "UFC Fight Night 54").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-7) Saggo lost the fight by split decision.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-8)

Saggo was expected to face [Marcin Bandel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcin_Bandel "Marcin Bandel") on April 11, 2015, at [UFC Fight Night 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_64 "UFC Fight Night 64").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-9) However, Saggo pulled out of the bout due to an injury to his achilles tendon and was replaced by promotional newcomer Stevie Ray.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-10)

Saggo faced [Justin Salas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Salas "Justin Salas") on March 5, 2016, at [UFC 196](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_196 "UFC 196").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-11) He won the fight via TKO in the first round.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-12)

Saggo next faced [Leandro Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leandro_Silva_(MMA) "Leandro Silva (MMA)") on June 18, 2016, at [UFC Fight Night 89](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_89 "UFC Fight Night 89").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-13) He won the fight via split decision.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-14)

Saggo faced [Rustam Khabilov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rustam_Khabilov "Rustam Khabilov") on December 10, 2016, at [UFC 206](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_206 "UFC 206").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-15) He lost the one-sided fight via unanimous decision.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-16)

Saggo faced [Gilbert Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Burns_(fighter) "Gilbert Burns (fighter)") on September 16, 2017, at [UFC Fight Night 116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_116 "UFC Fight Night 116").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-17) He lost the fight via knockout in the second round.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-18) He was subsequently released from the UFC.

### BTC Fight Promotions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jason_Saggo&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: BTC Fight Promotions")]

Following his release from the UFC, Saggo signed a multi-fight deal with BTC Fight Promotions out of Burlington, Ontario. He had his first fight on November 24, 2018, against Adam Assenza at BTC 4 for the BTC Lightweight Championship and won via first round rear-naked choke.

On May 9, Saggo vacated the lightweight title in preparation for a catchweight bout against Deivison Ribeiro on June 1, 2019, at BTC 6.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Saggo#cite_note-19)

# Marcin Tybura: UFC Record, Stats and Career Profile

Updated 3 August 2026 by [Mark Lawson](https://fightomic.com/author/fightomi/ "View all posts by Mark Lawson")

## The lowdown

Polish. Forty years old. Six foot three and a shade over 250lb on fight night. Born in Uniejów, a small spa town in central Poland, and fighting out of Łódź. A **Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt** who has spent a decade doing the least glamorous job in the sport: standing in the deep end of the UFC Heavyweight division and refusing to drown.

His **MMA record sits at 27-12**, with a **UFC record of 14-11** after the 1 August 2026 loss to [Aleksandar Rakić](https://fightomic.com/aleksandar-rakic-profile/) in Belgrade. Ten knockouts, seven submissions, ten decisions. Four Performance of the Night bonuses. A former M-1 Global Heavyweight champion who arrived in the Octagon already carrying a belt and then lost his first fight in it.

Nickname: Tybur. Nothing clever about it. It is what everyone in Polish MMA has called him since before anyone outside Poland knew his name.

## From Uniejów to a Master’s degree, and only then a cage

Tybura did not grow up shadowboxing in a garage. He found the sport in 2006, when a mate dragged him along, and within weeks he wanted to fight. Then he waited. Five years, in fact. He went to the University of Łódź and came out the other side with a **Master’s degree in Physical Education** before he ever took a professional fight.

That is a strange sequence for a Heavyweight. Most big men in this sport are found by a coach at a wrestling meet or a rugby pitch and rushed into the cage before they can think too hard about it. Tybura studied movement, got the paperwork, and then went to work.

He was 26 by the time he made his debut on 5 November 2011, choking out Robert Marcok with a rear-naked choke on a Polish domestic card. Five more wins followed on the regional circuit, one of them a decision over Adam Wieczorek, who would later make it to the UFC himself. His last regional outing was a third-round TKO of Krystian Kopytowski at Gladiator Arena 4.

Then Russia called.

## Eighty-eight seconds in St Petersburg

M-1 Global signed him in 2013 and dropped him straight into their Heavyweight Grand Prix as an alternate. He beat Denis Komkin, then flattened Chaban Ka in a round to reach the final. Konstantin Gluhov went out by rear-naked choke. Maro Perak got stopped in the third.

The final at M-1 Challenge 50 was the statement. Damian Grabowski, a genuine name in Polish heavyweight MMA at the time, lasted **88 seconds** before Tybura wrapped up a north-south choke and took the **M-1 Global Heavyweight title** along with the 2013 Grand Prix crown. He defended it inside a round against Denis Smoldarev.

Nine fights, nine wins, a belt and a tournament trophy. Then it went sideways in the way heavyweight careers always do eventually.

M-1 booked him in a champion versus champion superfight with Stephan Puetz, the Light Heavyweight titleholder, at Heavyweight and with no belts on the line. Tybura walked in roughly 10kg heavier and won the first two rounds on the cards. In the third he got cut badly enough that the ringside doctor waved it off. First loss of his professional life, and it came in a fight that meant nothing.

His second title defence produced one of the more horrible endings you will see. [Ante Delija](https://fightomic.com/ante-delija-profile/) checked a leg kick two minutes into the fight and broke his own leg doing it. Tybura kept the belt. Nobody celebrated.

## Welcome to the UFC, here is a loss

He signed with the UFC in January 2016 and made his debut that April against Timothy Johnson in Zagreb. He lost a unanimous decision. Champion in one promotion, 0-1 in the next.

The correction came fast. In August 2016 he took Viktor Pešta’s head off with a single kick and MMA Junkie called it a [vicious one-kick knockout](https://mmajunkie.com/2016/08/ufc-fight-night-92-results-marcin-tybura-gets-vicious-one-kick-knockout-of-viktor-pesta), which was fair. That was the first of his four Performance of the Night cheques. He pounded out Luis Henrique at UFC 209 and then outworked Andrei Arlovski over three rounds in Singapore.

Suddenly the Pole was a name. Then came the worst run of his career.

Mark Hunt was pulled from a Sydney main event on medical grounds and Fabrício Werdum stepped in, which meant Tybura’s first UFC headliner was 25 minutes against a former champion on ten days’ notice. He lost. [Derrick Lewis](https://fightomic.com/derrick-lewis-profile/) knocked him out. He beat Stefan Struve, then Shamil Abdurakhimov stopped him and Augusto Sakai flattened him in seconds in Vancouver.

Three finishes in four fights against him. At 33, in the division where nobody gets sentimental, that is usually the end of the conversation.

## The rebuild nobody asked for

It was not the end. Between February 2020 and June 2021 he ripped off five straight wins: [Serghei Spivac](https://fightomic.com/serghei-spivac-profile/), Maxim Grishin, Ben Rothwell, Greg Hardy and Walt Harris. Two of those, the Hardy and Harris finishes, brought bonuses. The Harris fight in particular was a proper survival job. He ate everything the American had early, then dragged him down and finished him with ground-and-pound.

The odd part is that the run happened after his life got harder, not easier. He had been training in Las Vegas with John Wood at Syndicate MMA when the pandemic shut the borders. Stuck in Poland, he had to find somewhere new to work. He landed at **Ankos MMA**, with additional time at Aligatores Fight Club, and it stuck.

“I chose one in Poland and it was perfect for me,” he told UFC.com in a feature on [finding his footing at a new gym](https://www.ufc.com/news/marcin-tybura-small-successes-ufc-fight-night-vegas-88). “It was coincidence, but it was perfect. My coach now and the gym, we’re really good for each other; we match well.” He added the line that has followed him around ever since: “Sometimes, if you don’t give up, there are opportunities that will come; it’s as simple as that.”

His BJJ black belt came in 2017, awarded under Kamil Umiński and Radek Turk on the same day [Jan Błachowicz](https://fightomic.com/jan-blachowicz-profile/) received his. Polish MMA is a small world.

## Volkov, Aspinall and the ugly truth about the top ten

[Alexander Volkov](https://fightomic.com/alexander-volkov-profile/) beat him on points at UFC 267. He got a majority decision over Alexander Romanov at UFC 278 that almost nobody agreed with, and 17 of 18 media scorecards had it a draw. He outpointed Blagoy Ivanov.

Then he headlined UFC London against Tom Aspinall in July 2023 and lasted just over a minute. Tybura had told anyone who asked what the danger was. Fighters storming him inside the first minute. He knew it was coming and it happened anyway.

He was back in a main event eight months later, choking out [Tai Tuivasa](https://fightomic.com/tai-tuivasa-profile/) in the first round in Las Vegas for another bonus. MMA Fighting named him to their [2024 Second Team MMA All-Star](https://www.mmafighting.com/2024/12/24/24326306/2024-mma-all-star-team-who-were-the-most-violent-fighters-in-each-weight-class-this-year) selection that December.

Spivac then armbarred him in a rematch, the first submission loss of his career. He answered by battering Jhonata Diniz into a doctor’s stoppage at UFC 309, and in March 2025 he became **the first man to beat unbeaten Brit Mick Parkin** on a London card.

## Three in a row, and the strangest night of the lot

A decade after the leg break, Delija got his rematch at UFC Paris in September 2025 and knocked him out inside two minutes.

Six months later in Seattle, [Tyrell Fortune](https://fightomic.com/tyrell-fortune-profile/) took a short-notice fight and took a decision. What people remember is what happened afterwards. Bruce Buffer read the scorecards, announced Tybura, and Fortune walked out of the cage toward the tunnel believing he had lost his UFC debut. Officials caught it. ESPN reported that [Fortune was called back into the Octagon](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/48334914/ufc-fortune-called-back-cage-wrong-winner-declared) to be announced the actual winner, with Buffer apologising for the mix-up on the microphone.

Tybura had his hand raised for about ninety seconds. Then he did not.

At UFC Belgrade on 1 August 2026 he met Rakić, who was moving up from Light Heavyweight and riding four straight defeats. Tybura fought from inside the pocket all night while the Serbian picked at his legs and head from range and cut angles. All three judges scored it 30-27. Three losses on the bounce.

## The numbers that outlast the results

Strip away the last two years and look at what he has accumulated. **Second most decision wins in UFC Heavyweight history.** Second most control time. Second most top position time. Second most total strikes landed, behind only Arlovski. Third most total fight time in the division’s history, more than four hours of it. Tied third for most bouts. His 14 UFC wins are level with Stipe Miocic and Curtis Blaydes.

He has been in there with a future undisputed champion, two interim titleholders, a former champion and most of the division’s top end across ten years. He is one of the most-fought men in the history of the weight class and he never got a title shot.

“The small successes are a big thing for me,” he said in that UFC interview. “I’ve learned to live in the present as much as possible.”

At Ankos he now works alongside the next wave of Polish heavyweights, including [Iwo Baraniewski](https://fightomic.com/iwo-baraniewski-profile/), which is the standard arc for a fighter who has been in the division long enough to become the measuring stick rather than the one doing the measuring.

# Marcin Tybura: UFC Record, Stats and Career Profile

Updated 3 August 2026 by [Mark Lawson](https://fightomic.com/author/fightomi/ "View all posts by Mark Lawson")

## The lowdown

Polish. Forty years old. Six foot three and a shade over 250lb on fight night. Born in Uniejów, a small spa town in central Poland, and fighting out of Łódź. A **Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt** who has spent a decade doing the least glamorous job in the sport: standing in the deep end of the UFC Heavyweight division and refusing to drown.

His **MMA record sits at 27-12**, with a **UFC record of 14-11** after the 1 August 2026 loss to [Aleksandar Rakić](https://fightomic.com/aleksandar-rakic-profile/) in Belgrade. Ten knockouts, seven submissions, ten decisions. Four Performance of the Night bonuses. A former M-1 Global Heavyweight champion who arrived in the Octagon already carrying a belt and then lost his first fight in it.

Nickname: Tybur. Nothing clever about it. It is what everyone in Polish MMA has called him since before anyone outside Poland knew his name.

## From Uniejów to a Master’s degree, and only then a cage

Tybura did not grow up shadowboxing in a garage. He found the sport in 2006, when a mate dragged him along, and within weeks he wanted to fight. Then he waited. Five years, in fact. He went to the University of Łódź and came out the other side with a **Master’s degree in Physical Education** before he ever took a professional fight.

That is a strange sequence for a Heavyweight. Most big men in this sport are found by a coach at a wrestling meet or a rugby pitch and rushed into the cage before they can think too hard about it. Tybura studied movement, got the paperwork, and then went to work.

He was 26 by the time he made his debut on 5 November 2011, choking out Robert Marcok with a rear-naked choke on a Polish domestic card. Five more wins followed on the regional circuit, one of them a decision over Adam Wieczorek, who would later make it to the UFC himself. His last regional outing was a third-round TKO of Krystian Kopytowski at Gladiator Arena 4.

Then Russia called.

## Eighty-eight seconds in St Petersburg

M-1 Global signed him in 2013 and dropped him straight into their Heavyweight Grand Prix as an alternate. He beat Denis Komkin, then flattened Chaban Ka in a round to reach the final. Konstantin Gluhov went out by rear-naked choke. Maro Perak got stopped in the third.

The final at M-1 Challenge 50 was the statement. Damian Grabowski, a genuine name in Polish heavyweight MMA at the time, lasted **88 seconds** before Tybura wrapped up a north-south choke and took the **M-1 Global Heavyweight title** along with the 2013 Grand Prix crown. He defended it inside a round against Denis Smoldarev.

Nine fights, nine wins, a belt and a tournament trophy. Then it went sideways in the way heavyweight careers always do eventually.

M-1 booked him in a champion versus champion superfight with Stephan Puetz, the Light Heavyweight titleholder, at Heavyweight and with no belts on the line. Tybura walked in roughly 10kg heavier and won the first two rounds on the cards. In the third he got cut badly enough that the ringside doctor waved it off. First loss of his professional life, and it came in a fight that meant nothing.

His second title defence produced one of the more horrible endings you will see. [Ante Delija](https://fightomic.com/ante-delija-profile/) checked a leg kick two minutes into the fight and broke his own leg doing it. Tybura kept the belt. Nobody celebrated.

## Welcome to the UFC, here is a loss

He signed with the UFC in January 2016 and made his debut that April against Timothy Johnson in Zagreb. He lost a unanimous decision. Champion in one promotion, 0-1 in the next.

The correction came fast. In August 2016 he took Viktor Pešta’s head off with a single kick and MMA Junkie called it a [vicious one-kick knockout](https://mmajunkie.com/2016/08/ufc-fight-night-92-results-marcin-tybura-gets-vicious-one-kick-knockout-of-viktor-pesta), which was fair. That was the first of his four Performance of the Night cheques. He pounded out Luis Henrique at UFC 209 and then outworked Andrei Arlovski over three rounds in Singapore.

Suddenly the Pole was a name. Then came the worst run of his career.

Mark Hunt was pulled from a Sydney main event on medical grounds and Fabrício Werdum stepped in, which meant Tybura’s first UFC headliner was 25 minutes against a former champion on ten days’ notice. He lost. [Derrick Lewis](https://fightomic.com/derrick-lewis-profile/) knocked him out. He beat Stefan Struve, then Shamil Abdurakhimov stopped him and Augusto Sakai flattened him in seconds in Vancouver.

Three finishes in four fights against him. At 33, in the division where nobody gets sentimental, that is usually the end of the conversation.

## The rebuild nobody asked for

It was not the end. Between February 2020 and June 2021 he ripped off five straight wins: [Serghei Spivac](https://fightomic.com/serghei-spivac-profile/), Maxim Grishin, Ben Rothwell, Greg Hardy and Walt Harris. Two of those, the Hardy and Harris finishes, brought bonuses. The Harris fight in particular was a proper survival job. He ate everything the American had early, then dragged him down and finished him with ground-and-pound.

The odd part is that the run happened after his life got harder, not easier. He had been training in Las Vegas with John Wood at Syndicate MMA when the pandemic shut the borders. Stuck in Poland, he had to find somewhere new to work. He landed at **Ankos MMA**, with additional time at Aligatores Fight Club, and it stuck.

“I chose one in Poland and it was perfect for me,” he told UFC.com in a feature on [finding his footing at a new gym](https://www.ufc.com/news/marcin-tybura-small-successes-ufc-fight-night-vegas-88). “It was coincidence, but it was perfect. My coach now and the gym, we’re really good for each other; we match well.” He added the line that has followed him around ever since: “Sometimes, if you don’t give up, there are opportunities that will come; it’s as simple as that.”

His BJJ black belt came in 2017, awarded under Kamil Umiński and Radek Turk on the same day [Jan Błachowicz](https://fightomic.com/jan-blachowicz-profile/) received his. Polish MMA is a small world.

## Volkov, Aspinall and the ugly truth about the top ten

[Alexander Volkov](https://fightomic.com/alexander-volkov-profile/) beat him on points at UFC 267. He got a majority decision over Alexander Romanov at UFC 278 that almost nobody agreed with, and 17 of 18 media scorecards had it a draw. He outpointed Blagoy Ivanov.

Then he headlined UFC London against Tom Aspinall in July 2023 and lasted just over a minute. Tybura had told anyone who asked what the danger was. Fighters storming him inside the first minute. He knew it was coming and it happened anyway.

He was back in a main event eight months later, choking out [Tai Tuivasa](https://fightomic.com/tai-tuivasa-profile/) in the first round in Las Vegas for another bonus. MMA Fighting named him to their [2024 Second Team MMA All-Star](https://www.mmafighting.com/2024/12/24/24326306/2024-mma-all-star-team-who-were-the-most-violent-fighters-in-each-weight-class-this-year) selection that December.

Spivac then armbarred him in a rematch, the first submission loss of his career. He answered by battering Jhonata Diniz into a doctor’s stoppage at UFC 309, and in March 2025 he became **the first man to beat unbeaten Brit Mick Parkin** on a London card.

## Three in a row, and the strangest night of the lot

A decade after the leg break, Delija got his rematch at UFC Paris in September 2025 and knocked him out inside two minutes.

Six months later in Seattle, [Tyrell Fortune](https://fightomic.com/tyrell-fortune-profile/) took a short-notice fight and took a decision. What people remember is what happened afterwards. Bruce Buffer read the scorecards, announced Tybura, and Fortune walked out of the cage toward the tunnel believing he had lost his UFC debut. Officials caught it. ESPN reported that [Fortune was called back into the Octagon](https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/48334914/ufc-fortune-called-back-cage-wrong-winner-declared) to be announced the actual winner, with Buffer apologising for the mix-up on the microphone.

Tybura had his hand raised for about ninety seconds. Then he did not.

At UFC Belgrade on 1 August 2026 he met Rakić, who was moving up from Light Heavyweight and riding four straight defeats. Tybura fought from inside the pocket all night while the Serbian picked at his legs and head from range and cut angles. All three judges scored it 30-27. Three losses on the bounce.

## The numbers that outlast the results

Strip away the last two years and look at what he has accumulated. **Second most decision wins in UFC Heavyweight history.** Second most control time. Second most top position time. Second most total strikes landed, behind only Arlovski. Third most total fight time in the division’s history, more than four hours of it. Tied third for most bouts. His 14 UFC wins are level with Stipe Miocic and Curtis Blaydes.

He has been in there with a future undisputed champion, two interim titleholders, a former champion and most of the division’s top end across ten years. He is one of the most-fought men in the history of the weight class and he never got a title shot.

“The small successes are a big thing for me,” he said in that UFC interview. “I’ve learned to live in the present as much as possible.”

At Ankos he now works alongside the next wave of Polish heavyweights, including [Iwo Baraniewski](https://fightomic.com/iwo-baraniewski-profile/), which is the standard arc for a fighter who has been in the division long enough to become the measuring stick rather than the one doing the measuring.

Daniel Cormier, a relatively short Heavyweight, has met success against bigger opponents in freestyle wrestling and later in Mixed Martial Arts. Cormier was raised in Lafayette, Louisiana where he was raised by his mother and stepfather. Cormier became a pro wrestling fan by age 10, which he watched on TV often. When he was 11, a coach introduced him to wrestling after breaking up a parking lot fight with him and a friend. He attended Louisiana High School where he won his first medals, thrice winning a Division I All-American and State championships. Cormier also played the linebacker position in football, and was offered a scholarship to play at Louisiana State University. He chose wrestling instead, and in 1997 he went to Colby Junior College in Kansas where he attended for two years, then transferred to Oklahoma State University (OSU). It was at OSU that he became a roommate and friend of [King Mo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3799707/?ls). In 2001 he was a runner-up in the NCAA Division I Collegiate Championship and NCAA Big 12 Conference. Cormier won a gold medal at the 2002 at the Pan American Games, and another in 2003 during the Pan American Games. In 2007, he won bronze medals at the FILA Wrestling World Championships, and the FILA Wrestling World Championships.  
  
While preparing to audition for the Olympics team, Cormier's 3 1/2 month daughter,Kaedyn Imri Cormier , died in a car accident on June 14, 2003 in Austin, Texas. The car she was in was hit by a 18 wheeler truck. Severely afflicted by the loss, Cormier stopped wrestling. After some time off, he made the 2004 US Olympics team in Athens, where he finished 4th. Cormier declined an offer from World Wrestling Entertaiment, and to try for the Olympics again. Due to a kidney failure he sustained from cutting weight to 211.5 pounds, Cormier withdrew from the US Olympic wrestling team in 2008, a day before he was to compete in the Beijing Olympics. Cormier could not train for a year, which ended his wrestling career.  
  
In 2009, Cormier started to train in Mixed Martial Arts out of San Jose's American Kickboxing Academy (AKA) , training with [King Mo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3799707/?ls), [Cain Velasquez](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2991500/?ls), and [Luke Rockhold](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4005312/?ls). Injuring his ribs a week before, Cormier fought fellow OSU alumni, [Gary Frazier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4054619/?ls), in his first bout at [Strikeforce Challengers 3 (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1713361/?ls). Cormier kept the fight standing by defending a takedown, landing a knee and taking control of Frazier's back and dominating him on the ground for a portion of the round. After exchanging punches in the second round, Cormier failed to get the takedown after numerous attempts when Frazier held the fence. Cormier gets the better of the stand-up by landing right punches and uppercuts. Frazier missed a knee strike and slipped, which Cormier took advantage of and gets top to land multiple punches to the head and won by TKO. Cormier got his first knockout at [Strikeforce Challengers 7 (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1713365/?ls), defeating [John Devine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4148097/?ls) in the first round.  
  
Cormier remained active outside of [Strikeforce (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1615388/?ls) in July 2010, initiating the busiest weeks of his MMA career by taking a fight against Lucas Browne in the Australian promotion Xtreme MMA, replacing injuring teammate [Mike Kyle](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1851449/?ls) with two days notice. In a bout for the XMMA Heavyweight Championship, Cormier took Brown e to the ground early, and won with devastating striking in four and a half minutes, resulting in Browne receiving up to one hundred stitches. Cormier returned to the United States two weeks later to challenge [Tony Johnson Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4985410/?ls) for the King of the Cage Heavyweight Championship, instead of competing at [Strikeforce Challengers 10 (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1713359/?ls) as planned. Johnson attacked with punches which put Cormier on the defensive. To stop Johnson's offense, Cormier clinches with him and held him against the cage. Johnson gets a double-leg takedown and is reversed with Cormier on top. Cormier controls Johnson on the ground, controlling his back and going for his neck. Johnson struggled to get Cormier off his back until the rear-naked choke is completely secured for the submission win. It was Cormier's second championship win in two weeks. Eight days after winning the King of the Cage title, Cormier fought [Jason Riley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4317829/?ls) at [Strikeforce: Houston (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1841850/?ls). Riley defended a single-leg take-down by Cormier then clinched with him against the fence. Cormier went for another take-down which Riley evaded. A right hand from Cormier stuns Riley and he was easily taken to the ground via double-leg. Further strikes forced Riley to submit by tapping the mat with his right hand. Cormier won the bout in just over a minute, making it his quickest fight.  
  
Cormier returned to Sydney, Australia to defend the Xtremme MMA Heavyweight Championship against [Soa Palelei](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2882816/?ls) at XMMA 3 in November 2010. It was a successful title defense for Cormier, who submitted Palelei by way of punches. Cormier took on [Devin Cole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3972366/?ls) at [Strikeforce Challengers 13 (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1814449/?ls). He tossed Cole to the ground in round one, and landed an assortment of kicks, including a powerful overhand right, more kicks and a take-down trip to the ground. Cormier hit Cole with a leg kick in the second round, then a hip toss which Cole quickly stood up from. Cormier quickly defended against his grounded opponent and got full mount. Cole briefly stood up before he was taken down by Cormier again, who attempted a rear-naked choke. Cole attacked from his back with an attempted kimura on Cormier's left arm until the round ended. Cormier landed a leg kick, then battled for position against the cage while on the feet. The fighters were separated and Cormier defended a takedown try by Cole. Cormier controlled his grounded opponent who stood up at they fought against the fence again. Cormier took Cole to the ground with a body lock and landed punches until the round expired, and won by unanimous decision.  
  
Cormier was to have fought [Shane Del Rosario](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4036817/?ls) in an alternate bout for the Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix tournament, but injuries from a car accident took Del Rosario from the fight. [Jeff Monson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2190183/?ls) replaced him at [Strikeforce: Overeem vs. Werdum (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2200390/?ls). Cormier and Monson engaged with punches in round one, and Cormier connected with kicks and more punches. Cormier landed more kicks in round two, and did not follow Monson--known for his submission abilities--to the ground. Cormier reversed against the cage, landed more strikes and tossed his opponent to the ground and backed away. In the final round, a determined Monson tried taking down Cormier, whom instead struck with punches, knees, and a leg trip. Cormier won by unanimous decision. In August 2011, with his recent win over Monson, Cormier was promoted from alternate to compete in Strikeforce's Heavyweight Grand Prix Tournament by replacing [Alistair Overeem](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4041248/?ls). Cormier proceeded to [Strikeforce: Barnett vs. Kharitonov (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2200438/?ls) where he met [Antonio Silva](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3308622/?ls) in a semi-final Strikeforce Heavyweight Grand Prix fight.  
  
Silva hit his body with a right kick and Cormier reacted with a right leg kick. Silva threw a barrage of punches, some of which connected on Cormier. Cormier hit Silva with a overhand right, allowed him to stand and defended against a takedown attempt which lead to Silva on his back again. The fight was stood up and Cormier connected with a left jab and "Bigfoot" Silva hit him with punches. Silva is put down for a second time when Cormier caught a right leg kick from him, then kicks away his left leg. Cormier backs away for the second time to allow Silva up, hit him with left jabs and a right uppercut which stunned him. Cormier finishes with a right hammer-fist then a left hammer-fist to win by knockout in the first round. Cormier advanced to the tournament finals with [Josh Barnett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2038245/?ls), who submitted [Sergei Kharitonov](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4317952/?ls) in the main event of the same card. Cormier re-injured his right hand fighting Silva in September 2011--then hurt it again in December 2012--postponing the final Grand Prix from March to May 2012.  
  
Cormier fought Barnett for the Strikeforce World Grand Prix Championship at [Strikeforce: Heavyweight Grand Prix Final (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2199068/?ls). He evaded Barnett's jabs and countered with kicks. Barnett struck him with a knee. Cormier him with a barrage of punches. Barnett lands left knee to side of Cormier's face to end the round. In round two Barnett hit Cormier with a left low kick, Cormier punches him in the face. Barnett pushes forward and Cormier hits him with a right uppercut. He gets a single-leg takedown on Barnett who tries a triangle choke and Cormier easily avoids it then an arm-bar. Cormier walks out of a leg-lock submission then landed more punches and elbows from the top. Barnett pushes Cormier against the fence after round three started. Cormier defends the takedown attempts, then grabs Barnett's left leg and picks him up and slams him to the ground on his back. Cormier gets side control but Barnett manages to get up. Cormier lands more punches, then later hit Barnett with a right head kick after a failed takedown. He hit Barnett with knees to end the round. Barnett started of championship round four by hitting Cormier with a left knee, who retaliates with a left hook. Cormier connects with left and right head kicks then get a takedown by holding a leg and tripping Barnett's other one. Barnett attempts submissions on Cormier's right leg/foot. Cormier escapes and control the action from top. In the fifth and final round, an aggressive Barnett hits a right body kick and continued with knees and punches on Cormier against the fence. Barnett lands another knee and a punch when the fight is resumed off the fence. Barnett lands a left hook, body kick and more punches. Cormier connects with two punches and Barnett misses a spinning back fist. Cormier takes him to the ground, and Barnett fought his way to the feet and prevented being slammed by Cormier. Cormier won unanimously on all the judge's score cards to be crowned the Strikeforce World Grand Prix Heavyweight Tournament Champion.  
  
As the tournament champion, Cormier was obligated by [Strikeforce (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1615388/?ls) 's TV partner, Showtime Networks, to have one more bout in the promotion. UFC fighter [Frank Mir](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1845641/?ls) agreed to fight Cormier until a knee injury a month before forced him out of the scheduled November 2012 card. The entire card was cancelled after an injury prevented Strikeforce Middleweight World Champion [Luke Rockhold](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4005312/?ls) from defending the title against [Lorenz Larkin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5095561/?ls). Cormier was later matched against Dutch fighter [Dion Staring](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5492234/?ls) at the promotion's final event, [Strikeforce: Marquardt vs. Saffiedine (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2660180/?ls). Cormier controlled Staring for much of the first round after tripping him twice and landing strikes from the full mounted position to end the round. Staring went after Cormier with punches in the second round and both fought for control against the fence. Cormier resumed his dominance when he tripped Staring with his left leg and controlled him on the ground and attacked from various angles with punches until a technical knockout stoppage with under a minute left in the round. Ronda Rousey burst onto the women's MMA scene in August of 2010. Born in Riverside County, California on February 1, 1987 to parents Ron Rousey and [AnnMaria DeMars](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3310662/?ls), little Ronda was born with an umbilical cord wrapped around her neck that damaged her vocal cords. She didn't speak coherently until the age of six. Ronda was a self-professed tomboy and swam from the ages of 6 to 10. She competed on the Jr. Olympic swim team where she placed in the state level.  
  
Because of her mother, a 7th degree black belt and 1984 World Judo Champion, Ronda took up the sport. She had a hard time socializing with other kids and found that Judo gave her confidence. She holds a 4th degree black belt in the martial art.  
  
Ronda's Judo career is a storied one. At 17 she became the youngest judoka in the 2004 Olympic Games in Athens. That same year she won a gold medal at the World Junior Judo Championships in Budapest, and in 2006 she became the first U.S. female in almost 10 years to win an A-Level tournament going 5-0 to clench the gold at the World Cup in Great Britain. At 19 she won the bronze medal at the Junior World Championships. She is the first U.S. athlete to win two Junior World Medals. In 2007 she added a silver at the World Judo Championships and a gold at the Pan American Games. The pinnacle of her Judo career was a bronze at the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing. Rousey became the first American to win an Olympic medal in women's Judo since it became an Olympic sport in 1992.  
  
After medaling in the Olympics, Ronda's career hit a dead end. She did some bartending to make ends meet and tried to find a better paying job, but it was tough finding anyone that needed her particular skill set. Throwing people down and putting them in armbars aren't really something you can put on a resume. By chance Ronda caught the [Gina Carano](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2442289/?ls) vs. [Julie Kedzie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3110309/?ls) fight on television and things changed.  
  
She made her mixed martial arts debut as an amateur in 2010. Since then she has never lost a fight, winning the majority in the first round by armbar submission. Ronda took it upon herself to chase after and demand attention so that the UFC could no longer ignore women fighters. UFC President [Dana White](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1831502/?ls) had publicly stated that women would never be allowed to fight in the UFC, but on February 23, 2013, Ronda did just that. She won the fight against [Liz Carmouche](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4188548/?ls) in the first round with her signature armbar and became the first UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion.  
  
In 2014, Ronda appeared in her first motion picture - [The Expendables 3 (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2333784/?ls). Other projects are [Furious 7 (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2820852/?ls) and [The Athena Project](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1777617/?ls) as well as [Entourage (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1674771/?ls).

 #### [32. Cris Cyborg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3186415/?ref_=ls_t_39)
