**Angela Patrice Hill**[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-4) (born January 12, 1985) is an American [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") who competes in the women's [Strawweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strawweight_(MMA) "Strawweight (MMA)") division of the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC). She was formerly signed with the [Invicta Fighting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_Fighting_Championships "Invicta Fighting Championships"), where she was the strawweight champion. She is also a former [World Kickboxing Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Kickboxing_Association "World Kickboxing Association") champion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-:0-5)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hill received a [Bachelor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts") degree at the [Cooper Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooper_Union "Cooper Union") School of Art.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-6) Before becoming a professional fighter, she worked as an animator in animation studios and as a bartender.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Kotaku_13_December_2016-7)

Hill is also a video gamer and [cosplayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosplayer "Cosplayer"), and several times appeared in costume before fights at Invicta. She has cosplayed as [Dhalsim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhalsim "Dhalsim"), [Afro Samurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro_Samurai "Afro Samurai"), a _[Fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout\_(franchise) "Fallout (franchise)")_ Vault Dweller, and as one of _[The Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Warriors\_(film) "The Warriors (film)")_, among others.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Kotaku_13_December_2016-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-8)

Hill's paternal grandparents were [Barney and Betty Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barney_and_Betty_Hill_incident "Barney and Betty Hill incident"), who made one of the most notable [alien abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_abduction "Alien abduction") claims in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"). Hill has said of this, "It was a really big deal that you could Wikipedia my grandfather."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-9)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Hill began her professional MMA career in 2014 with a win over future _Invicta_ fighter Stephanie Skinner.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-10)

### The Ultimate Fighter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Ultimate Fighter")]

In June 2014, it was announced that Hill was one of the fighters selected by the UFC to appear on [The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_A_Champion_Will_Be_Crowned "The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned"). She faced [Carla Esparza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Esparza "Carla Esparza") in the preliminary round and lost via submission in the first round.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-11)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship")]

Hill's first fight after The Ultimate Fighter was against [Emily Kagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Kagan "Emily Kagan") at [The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_A_Champion_Will_Be_Crowned_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned Finale") on December 12, 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-12)[Tecia Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecia_Torres "Tecia Torres") fought at [UFC 188](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_188 "UFC 188") and defeated Hill.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-13)

Hill faced [Rose Namajunas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Namajunas "Rose Namajunas") at [UFC 192](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_192 "UFC 192") on October 3, 2015. She lost the fight by submission in the first round. She was subsequently released from the promotion.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-14)

### Invicta FC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Invicta FC")]

On November 17, 2015, Hill announced on her official Facebook page that she signed with Invicta FC.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-15) She made her debut for the promotion at [Invicta FC 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_FC_events "Invicta FC events") on January 16, 2016, and successfully notched a first round [TKO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_knockout "Technical knockout") victory over [Alida Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alida_Gray "Alida Gray").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-16) Hill returned less than two months later on March 11, 2016, and knocked out former strawweight title challenger [Stephanie Eggink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephanie_Eggink "Stephanie Eggink") in the second round, earning her first Performance of the Night bonus as a result of the finish.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-17)

Hill made another quick turnaround to face undefeated strawweight champion [Lívia Renata Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livia_Renata_Souza "Livia Renata Souza") for the title at [Invicta FC 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_FC_events "Invicta FC events") on May 7, 2016.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-18) She won the fight via split decision to become the new Invicta FC Strawweight champion.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-19)

### UFC return

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: UFC return")]

Hill and [Jéssica Andrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9ssica_Andrade "Jéssica Andrade") were briefly linked to a bout at [UFC 207](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_207 "UFC 207").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-20) However, the fight never materialized for that event because of a rule in the UFC's anti-doping policy with USADA.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-21) Subsequently, Andrade was removed from that card with the pairing left intact and rescheduled to take place at [UFC Fight Night 104](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_104 "UFC Fight Night 104") on February 4, 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-AndradeHill-22) Andrade won the fight by unanimous decision. In addition, both participants were awarded _Fight of the Night_ honors.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFC207-23)

Hill faced [Ashley Yoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Yoder "Ashley Yoder") on July 7, 2017, at [The Ultimate Fighter 25 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Redemption#The_Ultimate_Fighter_25_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: Redemption").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-24) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-25)

Hill faced [Nina Ansaroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Ansaroff "Nina Ansaroff") at [UFC Fight Night 120](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_120 "UFC Fight Night 120") on November 11, 2017, in [Norfolk, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk,_Virginia "Norfolk, Virginia").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-26) She lost the fight via unanimous decision.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-27)

Hill faced [Maryna Moroz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryna_Moroz "Maryna Moroz") at [UFC on Fox 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_28 "UFC on Fox 28") on February 24, 2018, at Amway Center in Orlando, Florida.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-28) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-29)

Hill was scheduled to face [Alexa Grasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexa_Grasso "Alexa Grasso") on August 25, 2018, at [UFC Fight Night 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_135 "UFC Fight Night 135").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-30) However, Grasso was pulled out from the bout on July 19, 2018, due to knee injury and she was replaced by [Cortney Casey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortney_Casey "Cortney Casey").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-31) She lost the fight via split decision.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-32) 11 out of 17 media outlets scored the bout for Hill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-33)

Hill faced [Randa Markos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randa_Markos "Randa Markos") on March 23, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 148](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_148 "UFC Fight Night 148").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-34) She lost the fight via a submission in round one.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-35)

Hill replaced an injured [Jessica Penne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Penne "Jessica Penne") against [Jodie Esquibel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Esquibel "Jodie Esquibel") on April 27, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 150](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_150 "UFC Fight Night 150").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-AngelaHill-36) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-37)

Hill faced [Yan Xiaonan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yan_Xiaonan "Yan Xiaonan"), replacing injured [Felice Herrig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felice_Herrig "Felice Herrig"), on June 8, 2019, at [UFC 238](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_238 "UFC 238").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-38) She lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-39)

Hill was scheduled to face Istela Nunes on September 21, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 159](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_159 "UFC Fight Night 159").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-40) However, on August 12, 2019, it was reported that Nunes was removed from the card due to a failed drug test,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-41) and she was replaced by [Ariane Carnelossi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariane_Carnelossi "Ariane Carnelossi").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-42) Hill won the fight via TKO due to a doctor's stoppage in the third round after an elbow she threw cut Carnelossi over the left eye and rendered her unable to continue.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-43)

Hill faced [Hannah Cifers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Cifers "Hannah Cifers"), replacing [Brianna Van Buren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brianna_Van_Buren "Brianna Van Buren") on January 25, 2020, at [UFC Fight Night 166](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_166 "UFC Fight Night 166").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-44) She won the fight via technical knockout in round two.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-45)

Hill accepted a short notice fight once again, replacing [Hannah Goldy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Goldy "Hannah Goldy") to fight [Loma Lookboonmee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loma_Lookboonmee "Loma Lookboonmee") at [UFC Fight Night 168](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_168 "UFC Fight Night 168") on February 23, 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-46) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-47)

Hill faced [Cláudia Gadelha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1udia_Gadelha "Cláudia Gadelha") on May 16, 2020, at [UFC on ESPN 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_8 "UFC on ESPN 8").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-48) She lost the bout via split decision. 13 of 17 media outlets scored the fight in favor of Hill.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-50)

Hill was scheduled to meet [Michelle Waterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Waterson "Michelle Waterson") on August 22, 2020, at [UFC on ESPN 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_15 "UFC on ESPN 15").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-51) However, due to some personal reasons on Waterson's side, the bout was moved three weeks later to the 5 rounds main event at [UFC Fight Night 177](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_177 "UFC Fight Night 177").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-52) Hill lost the fight via split decision.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-53) This fight earned her the _[Fight of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_UFC\_bonus\_award\_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients")_ award.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFN_177-54) 11 out of 21 media outlets scored the bout for Hill.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-55)

A rematch with Tecia Torres was expected to take place on December 12, 2020, at [UFC 256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_256 "UFC 256").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-56) However, Hill was forced to pull out from the event due to testing positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-57)

Hill was scheduled to face [Ashley Yoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Yoder "Ashley Yoder") in a rematch of their 2017 bout on February 27, 2021, at [UFC Fight Night 186](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_186 "UFC Fight Night 186").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-58) However, day of the event it was announced that the bout was scrapped from the card after one of Yoder's cornermen tested positive [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19"). The bout was rescheduled and took place at [UFC Fight Night 187](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_187 "UFC Fight Night 187") on March 13.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-59) Hill won the fight via unanimous decision.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-60)

Hill was scheduled to meet [Amanda Ribas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Ribas "Amanda Ribas") on May 8, 2021, at [UFC on ESPN 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_24 "UFC on ESPN 24").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-61) However, the day of the event Ribas was removed from the bout due to [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") protocols and the bout was cancelled.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-62) The bout was rescheduled for [UFC Fight Night 189](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_189 "UFC Fight Night 189") on June 5, 2021.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-63) Two weeks later, the pairing was scrapped once again as Ribas was still suffering from lingering [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") symptoms.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-FightsOff-64)

The rematch with Tecia Torres was rescheduled and took place on August 7, 2021, at [UFC 265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_265 "UFC 265").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-WSWagain-65) Hill lost the fight via unanimous decision.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Anderson-66)

Hill faced [Virna Jandiroba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virna_Jandiroba "Virna Jandiroba") on May 14, 2022, at [UFC on ESPN 36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_36 "UFC on ESPN 36").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-71) She lost the bout via unanimous decision.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-72)

Hill faced promotional newcomer [Xiong Jingnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiong_Jingnan "Xiong Jingnan") on May 30, 2026 at [UFC Fight Night 277](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_277 "UFC Fight Night 277").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-94) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-95)

**Angela Patrice Hill**[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-4) (born January 12, 1985) is an American [mixed martial artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") who competes in the women's [Strawweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strawweight_(MMA) "Strawweight (MMA)") division of the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC). She was formerly signed with the [Invicta Fighting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_Fighting_Championships "Invicta Fighting Championships"), where she was the strawweight champion. She is also a former [World Kickboxing Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Kickboxing_Association "World Kickboxing Association") champion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-:0-5)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hill received a [Bachelor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts") degree at the [Cooper Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooper_Union "Cooper Union") School of Art.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-6) Before becoming a professional fighter, she worked as an animator in animation studios and as a bartender.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Kotaku_13_December_2016-7)

Hill is also a video gamer and [cosplayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosplayer "Cosplayer"), and several times appeared in costume before fights at Invicta. She has cosplayed as [Dhalsim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhalsim "Dhalsim"), [Afro Samurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro_Samurai "Afro Samurai"), a _[Fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout\_(franchise) "Fallout (franchise)")_ Vault Dweller, and as one of _[The Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Warriors\_(film) "The Warriors (film)")_, among others.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Kotaku_13_December_2016-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-8)

Hill's paternal grandparents were [Barney and Betty Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barney_and_Betty_Hill_incident "Barney and Betty Hill incident"), who made one of the most notable [alien abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_abduction "Alien abduction") claims in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"). Hill has said of this, "It was a really big deal that you could Wikipedia my grandfather."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-9)

## Mixed martial arts career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mixed martial arts career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Hill began her professional MMA career in 2014 with a win over future _Invicta_ fighter Stephanie Skinner.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-10)

### The Ultimate Fighter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Ultimate Fighter")]

In June 2014, it was announced that Hill was one of the fighters selected by the UFC to appear on [The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_A_Champion_Will_Be_Crowned "The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned"). She faced [Carla Esparza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Esparza "Carla Esparza") in the preliminary round and lost via submission in the first round.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-11)

### Ultimate Fighting Championship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship")]

Hill's first fight after The Ultimate Fighter was against [Emily Kagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Kagan "Emily Kagan") at [The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_A_Champion_Will_Be_Crowned_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: A Champion Will Be Crowned Finale") on December 12, 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-12)[Tecia Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecia_Torres "Tecia Torres") fought at [UFC 188](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_188 "UFC 188") and defeated Hill.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-13)

Hill faced [Rose Namajunas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Namajunas "Rose Namajunas") at [UFC 192](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_192 "UFC 192") on October 3, 2015. She lost the fight by submission in the first round. She was subsequently released from the promotion.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-14)

### Invicta FC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Invicta FC")]

On November 17, 2015, Hill announced on her official Facebook page that she signed with Invicta FC.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-15) She made her debut for the promotion at [Invicta FC 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_FC_events "Invicta FC events") on January 16, 2016, and successfully notched a first round [TKO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_knockout "Technical knockout") victory over [Alida Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alida_Gray "Alida Gray").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-16) Hill returned less than two months later on March 11, 2016, and knocked out former strawweight title challenger [Stephanie Eggink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephanie_Eggink "Stephanie Eggink") in the second round, earning her first Performance of the Night bonus as a result of the finish.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-17)

Hill made another quick turnaround to face undefeated strawweight champion [Lívia Renata Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livia_Renata_Souza "Livia Renata Souza") for the title at [Invicta FC 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invicta_FC_events "Invicta FC events") on May 7, 2016.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-18) She won the fight via split decision to become the new Invicta FC Strawweight champion.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-19)

### UFC return

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angela_Hill&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: UFC return")]

Hill and [Jéssica Andrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9ssica_Andrade "Jéssica Andrade") were briefly linked to a bout at [UFC 207](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_207 "UFC 207").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-20) However, the fight never materialized for that event because of a rule in the UFC's anti-doping policy with USADA.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-21) Subsequently, Andrade was removed from that card with the pairing left intact and rescheduled to take place at [UFC Fight Night 104](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_104 "UFC Fight Night 104") on February 4, 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-AndradeHill-22) Andrade won the fight by unanimous decision. In addition, both participants were awarded _Fight of the Night_ honors.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFC207-23)

Hill faced [Ashley Yoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Yoder "Ashley Yoder") on July 7, 2017, at [The Ultimate Fighter 25 Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Fighter:_Redemption#The_Ultimate_Fighter_25_Finale "The Ultimate Fighter: Redemption").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-24) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-25)

Hill faced [Nina Ansaroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Ansaroff "Nina Ansaroff") at [UFC Fight Night 120](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_120 "UFC Fight Night 120") on November 11, 2017, in [Norfolk, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk,_Virginia "Norfolk, Virginia").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-26) She lost the fight via unanimous decision.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-27)

Hill faced [Maryna Moroz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryna_Moroz "Maryna Moroz") at [UFC on Fox 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_Fox_28 "UFC on Fox 28") on February 24, 2018, at Amway Center in Orlando, Florida.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-28) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-29)

Hill was scheduled to face [Alexa Grasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexa_Grasso "Alexa Grasso") on August 25, 2018, at [UFC Fight Night 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_135 "UFC Fight Night 135").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-30) However, Grasso was pulled out from the bout on July 19, 2018, due to knee injury and she was replaced by [Cortney Casey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortney_Casey "Cortney Casey").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-31) She lost the fight via split decision.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-32) 11 out of 17 media outlets scored the bout for Hill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-33)

Hill faced [Randa Markos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randa_Markos "Randa Markos") on March 23, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 148](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_148 "UFC Fight Night 148").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-34) She lost the fight via a submission in round one.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-35)

Hill replaced an injured [Jessica Penne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Penne "Jessica Penne") against [Jodie Esquibel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Esquibel "Jodie Esquibel") on April 27, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 150](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_150 "UFC Fight Night 150").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-AngelaHill-36) She won the fight by unanimous decision.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-37)

Hill faced [Yan Xiaonan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yan_Xiaonan "Yan Xiaonan"), replacing injured [Felice Herrig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felice_Herrig "Felice Herrig"), on June 8, 2019, at [UFC 238](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_238 "UFC 238").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-38) She lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-39)

Hill was scheduled to face Istela Nunes on September 21, 2019, at [UFC Fight Night 159](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_159 "UFC Fight Night 159").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-40) However, on August 12, 2019, it was reported that Nunes was removed from the card due to a failed drug test,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-41) and she was replaced by [Ariane Carnelossi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariane_Carnelossi "Ariane Carnelossi").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-42) Hill won the fight via TKO due to a doctor's stoppage in the third round after an elbow she threw cut Carnelossi over the left eye and rendered her unable to continue.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-43)

Hill faced [Hannah Cifers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Cifers "Hannah Cifers"), replacing [Brianna Van Buren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brianna_Van_Buren "Brianna Van Buren") on January 25, 2020, at [UFC Fight Night 166](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_166 "UFC Fight Night 166").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-44) She won the fight via technical knockout in round two.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-45)

Hill accepted a short notice fight once again, replacing [Hannah Goldy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Goldy "Hannah Goldy") to fight [Loma Lookboonmee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loma_Lookboonmee "Loma Lookboonmee") at [UFC Fight Night 168](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_168 "UFC Fight Night 168") on February 23, 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-46) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-47)

Hill faced [Cláudia Gadelha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1udia_Gadelha "Cláudia Gadelha") on May 16, 2020, at [UFC on ESPN 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_8 "UFC on ESPN 8").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-48) She lost the bout via split decision. 13 of 17 media outlets scored the fight in favor of Hill.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-50)

Hill was scheduled to meet [Michelle Waterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Waterson "Michelle Waterson") on August 22, 2020, at [UFC on ESPN 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_15 "UFC on ESPN 15").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-51) However, due to some personal reasons on Waterson's side, the bout was moved three weeks later to the 5 rounds main event at [UFC Fight Night 177](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_177 "UFC Fight Night 177").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-52) Hill lost the fight via split decision.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-53) This fight earned her the _[Fight of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_UFC\_bonus\_award\_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients")_ award.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFN_177-54) 11 out of 21 media outlets scored the bout for Hill.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-55)

A rematch with Tecia Torres was expected to take place on December 12, 2020, at [UFC 256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_256 "UFC 256").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-56) However, Hill was forced to pull out from the event due to testing positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-57)

Hill was scheduled to face [Ashley Yoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Yoder "Ashley Yoder") in a rematch of their 2017 bout on February 27, 2021, at [UFC Fight Night 186](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_186 "UFC Fight Night 186").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-58) However, day of the event it was announced that the bout was scrapped from the card after one of Yoder's cornermen tested positive [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19"). The bout was rescheduled and took place at [UFC Fight Night 187](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_187 "UFC Fight Night 187") on March 13.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-59) Hill won the fight via unanimous decision.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-60)

Hill was scheduled to meet [Amanda Ribas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Ribas "Amanda Ribas") on May 8, 2021, at [UFC on ESPN 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_24 "UFC on ESPN 24").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-61) However, the day of the event Ribas was removed from the bout due to [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") protocols and the bout was cancelled.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-62) The bout was rescheduled for [UFC Fight Night 189](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_189 "UFC Fight Night 189") on June 5, 2021.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-63) Two weeks later, the pairing was scrapped once again as Ribas was still suffering from lingering [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") symptoms.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-FightsOff-64)

The rematch with Tecia Torres was rescheduled and took place on August 7, 2021, at [UFC 265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_265 "UFC 265").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-WSWagain-65) Hill lost the fight via unanimous decision.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-Anderson-66)

Hill faced [Amanda Lemos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Lemos "Amanda Lemos"), replacing [Nina Nunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Nunes "Nina Nunes"), on December 18, 2021, at [UFC Fight Night 199](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_199 "UFC Fight Night 199").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-67) Hill lost the bout via split decision.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-68) 10 out of 11 media scores gave it to Hill.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-69) This bout earned the _[Fight of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_UFC\_bonus\_award\_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients")_ bonus award.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFN199-70)

Hill faced [Virna Jandiroba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virna_Jandiroba "Virna Jandiroba") on May 14, 2022, at [UFC on ESPN 36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_36 "UFC on ESPN 36").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-71) She lost the bout via unanimous decision.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-72)

Hill faced [Lupita Godinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupita_Godinez "Lupita Godinez") on August 13, 2022, at [UFC on ESPN 41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_41 "UFC on ESPN 41").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-73) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-74)

Hill faced [Emily Ducote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Ducote "Emily Ducote") on December 3, 2022, at [UFC on ESPN 42](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_42 "UFC on ESPN 42").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-75) She won the bout via unanimous decision.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-76)

Hill faced [Denise Gomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denise_Gomes "Denise Gomes") at [UFC Fight Night 231](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_231 "UFC Fight Night 231") on November 4, 2023.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-81) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-82)

Hill faced [Luana Pinheiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luana_Pinheiro "Luana Pinheiro") on May 18, 2024, at [UFC Fight Night 241](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_241 "UFC Fight Night 241").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-83) She won the bout by a guillotine choke submission in the second round.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-:0-5) This fight earned her her first _[Performance of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_UFC\_bonus\_award\_recipients "List of UFC bonus award recipients")_ award.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-UFN_241-84)

Hill faced [Tabatha Ricci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabatha_Ricci "Tabatha Ricci") on August 24, 2024 at [UFC on ESPN 62](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_62 "UFC on ESPN 62").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-85) She lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-86)

Hill faced [Ketlen Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ketlen_Souza "Ketlen Souza") on February 15, 2025 at [UFC Fight Night 251](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_251 "UFC Fight Night 251").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-87) She won the fight by split decision.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-88) 8 out of 10 media outlets scored the bout for Souza.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-89)

Hill faced Iasmin Lucindo on August 9, 2025 at [UFC on ESPN 72](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_72 "UFC on ESPN 72").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-90) She lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-91)

Hill faced Fatima Kline on November 15, 2025 at [UFC 322](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_322 "UFC 322").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-92) She lost the fight by unanimous decision.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-93)

Hill faced promotional newcomer [Xiong Jingnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiong_Jingnan "Xiong Jingnan") on May 30, 2026 at [UFC Fight Night 277](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_277 "UFC Fight Night 277").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-94) She won the fight via unanimous decision.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Hill#cite_note-95)

**John Michael McCarthy** (born October 12, 1962) is a retired American [mixed martial arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") (MMA) [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee "Referee") best known for officiating numerous bouts promoted by the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC), dating back to [UFC 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_2 "UFC 2").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-tapology-1) He is credited as being one of the greatest and most recognizable referees in combat sports history and an important figure in the mixed martial arts world, helping create the [Unified Rules of MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts_rules#Unified_Rules_of_Mixed_Martial_Arts "Mixed martial arts rules") after initially creating the original rule book of the UFC. He currently is a commentator for the [Professional Fighters League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Fighters_League "Professional Fighters League") (PFL) and co-hosts the combat sports-based podcast "Weighing In" with former fighter [Josh Thomson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Thomson "Josh Thomson").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

McCarthy spent some time as an officer of the [Los Angeles Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department "Los Angeles Police Department"), retiring around 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-:0-4)

In 1993, he became involved with the newly created [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC) fighting tournament. He was the referee for [UFC 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_2 "UFC 2"), launching a career as a UFC referee. The UFC initially started with very few rules, but McCarthy gave feedback that it was too dangerous and suggested additional rules, many of which were adopted. Saying the catch phrase originally coined by boxing referee Mills Lane, McCarthy would often start matches by saying "let's get it on" to the fighters, which became an iconic catchphrase that is associated with him and his refereeing.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-:0-4)

The nickname of "Big John" came about because of his size and stature. He stands 6 ft 3 in (1.91 m) and weighs 265 lb (120 kg); making him larger than the majority of the athletes over whom he presides. According to a UFC interview, the nickname was given to him by UFC co-founder and promoter [Art Davie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Davie "Art Davie"). McCarthy recalls that the nickname began when he forcibly lifted Davie off the ground and held him in the air.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-5)

In 2018, McCarthy retired from UFC refereeing, and moved to [Bellator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellator_MMA "Bellator MMA") as a commentator.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-6) He currently serves as a judging and rules analyst for the [Professional Fighters League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Fighters_League "Professional Fighters League") (PFL), who acquired Bellator in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-7)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

McCarthy has two sons and a daughter, one of whom has been an MMA judge since 2013.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-13) McCarthy currently resides in [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-14)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Published work")]

On September 1, 2011, McCarthy's [autobiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiography "Autobiography"), _Let's Get It On - The Making of MMA and its Ultimate Referee_, was published.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-19)

## Film and television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film and television")]

McCarthy had a cameo appearance in the _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_ episode, "[The One with the Ultimate Fighting Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_One_with_the_Ultimate_Fighting_Champion "The One with the Ultimate Fighting Champion")".

McCarthy also served as the referee on the MTV2 series _[Bully Beatdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully\_Beatdown "Bully Beatdown")_, along with professional mixed martial artist [Jason "Mayhem" Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_%22Mayhem%22_Miller "Jason \"Mayhem\" Miller").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-mtv-20)

McCarthy is featured in the award-winning mixed martial arts documentary _[Fight Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight\_Life "Fight Life")_, the film is directed by James Z. Feng and released in 2013.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-fightlife-21)

McCarthy appeared in Season 3b, Episode 5 of [Entourage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entourage_(American_TV_series) "Entourage (American TV series)").

McCarthy appeared at the end of the film [Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Back_Down_2:_The_Beatdown "Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown").

**John Michael McCarthy** (born October 12, 1962) is a retired American [mixed martial arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts "Mixed martial arts") (MMA) [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee "Referee") best known for officiating numerous bouts promoted by the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC), dating back to [UFC 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_2 "UFC 2").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-tapology-1) He is credited as being one of the greatest and most recognizable referees in combat sports history and an important figure in the mixed martial arts world, helping create the [Unified Rules of MMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts_rules#Unified_Rules_of_Mixed_Martial_Arts "Mixed martial arts rules") after initially creating the original rule book of the UFC. He currently is a commentator for the [Professional Fighters League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Fighters_League "Professional Fighters League") (PFL) and co-hosts the combat sports-based podcast "Weighing In" with former fighter [Josh Thomson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Thomson "Josh Thomson").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

McCarthy spent some time as an officer of the [Los Angeles Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department "Los Angeles Police Department"), retiring around 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-:0-4)

In 1993, he became involved with the newly created [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC) fighting tournament. He was the referee for [UFC 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFC_2 "UFC 2"), launching a career as a UFC referee. The UFC initially started with very few rules, but McCarthy gave feedback that it was too dangerous and suggested additional rules, many of which were adopted. Saying the catch phrase originally coined by boxing referee Mills Lane, McCarthy would often start matches by saying "let's get it on" to the fighters, which became an iconic catchphrase that is associated with him and his refereeing.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-:0-4)

The nickname of "Big John" came about because of his size and stature. He stands 6 ft 3 in (1.91 m) and weighs 265 lb (120 kg); making him larger than the majority of the athletes over whom he presides. According to a UFC interview, the nickname was given to him by UFC co-founder and promoter [Art Davie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Davie "Art Davie"). McCarthy recalls that the nickname began when he forcibly lifted Davie off the ground and held him in the air.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-5)

In 2018, McCarthy retired from UFC refereeing, and moved to [Bellator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellator_MMA "Bellator MMA") as a commentator.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-6) He currently serves as a judging and rules analyst for the [Professional Fighters League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Fighters_League "Professional Fighters League") (PFL), who acquired Bellator in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-7)

## Awards and honors

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

McCarthy has two sons and a daughter, one of whom has been an MMA judge since 2013.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-13) McCarthy currently resides in [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-14)

## Published work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Published work")]

On September 1, 2011, McCarthy's [autobiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiography "Autobiography"), _Let's Get It On - The Making of MMA and its Ultimate Referee_, was published.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-19)

## Film and television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_McCarthy_(referee)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film and television")]

McCarthy had a cameo appearance in the _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_ episode, "[The One with the Ultimate Fighting Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_One_with_the_Ultimate_Fighting_Champion "The One with the Ultimate Fighting Champion")".

McCarthy also served as the referee on the MTV2 series _[Bully Beatdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully\_Beatdown "Bully Beatdown")_, along with professional mixed martial artist [Jason "Mayhem" Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_%22Mayhem%22_Miller "Jason \"Mayhem\" Miller").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-mtv-20)

McCarthy is featured in the award-winning mixed martial arts documentary _[Fight Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight\_Life "Fight Life")_, the film is directed by James Z. Feng and released in 2013.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(referee)#cite_note-fightlife-21)

McCarthy appeared in Season 3b, Episode 5 of [Entourage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entourage_(American_TV_series) "Entourage (American TV series)").

McCarthy appeared at the end of the film [Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Back_Down_2:_The_Beatdown "Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown").

# 6 frequently used UFC referees who competed as MMA fighters

Nolan King

USA TODAY Sports

May 23, 2023, 2:00 a.m. ET

[](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fmma%2F2023%2F05%2F23%2Fufc-referees-who-fought-mma-dean-goddard-peterson-grice-trigg%2F81207296007%2F&text=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters&via=MMAJunkie)[](mailto:?subject=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters%20-%20from%20MMA%20Junkie&body=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters%0A%0AThe%20third%20man%20in%20the%20cage%20isn't%20why%20the%20masses%20tune%20in%20to%20watch%20fights.%20However%2C%20officials%20used%20by%20major%20promotions%20on%20a%20frequent%20basis%20often%20rack%20up%20more%20cage-time%20on%20international%20airwaves%20than%20the%20athletes%20they%20oversee.%20Week%20after%20week%2C%20the%20officials%20grace%20the%20streams%20of%E2%80%A6%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20mmajunkie.usatoday.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fmma%2F2023%2F05%2F23%2Fufc-referees-who-fought-mma-dean-goddard-peterson-grice-trigg%2F81207296007%2F)

![Image 1](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/03/03/SMMA/81207264007-91-2575422.png?width=660&height=440&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)
The third man in the cage isn't why the masses tune in to watch fights.

However, officials used by major promotions on a frequent basis often rack up more cage-time on international airwaves than the athletes they oversee.

Week after week, the officials grace the streams of MMA fans around the world. With that, a sense of familiarity is built. They become household names among viewers.

While they may have gained fame through officiating fights, many referees got started as competitors themselves – just check the tape.

Buried in the bowels of YouTube are some of the most popular referees in MMA today throwing punches, kicks, and elbows. Scroll below to watch six referees frequently used by the UFC, Bellator, and PFL compete in MMA bouts.

## Frank Trigg

![Image 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hwa__ZAtTVA)
**Pro record**: 21-9

**Years active**: 1997-2011

OK, so this is perhaps the most obvious of the bunch. Out of all the MMA referees who populate the realm of major promotional regularity, Frank Trigg has the most impressive competitor resume. He competed seven times in the UFC and challenged for the promotion's welterweight championship twice. He retired from competition in 2011 and debuted as a referee in 2014.

## Marc Goddard

![Image 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wYhj5KIPxSM)
**Pro record**: 7-6-1

**Years active**: 2002-2008

The most familiar face in European MMA refereeing is now one of the most universally used officials in the game today. Though his rise to notoriety came on the officiating side, Marc Goddard competed 14 times as a professional MMA fighter from his debut in 2002 up until his competitive retirement in 2008. He competed for Cage Warriors and Cage Rage, among other promotions.

## Blake Grice

![Image 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xJObrHLRfgE)
**Amateur record**: 3-1

**Years active**: 2001-2003

Over the past few years, Blake Grice has established himself in the "big leagues" of MMA officiating. A respected referee, judge, and instructor, Grice has been the overseer of his fair share of major promotional bouts. While he never competed professionally, Grice compiled a 3-1 record as an amateur prior to his officiating days.

## Herb Dean

![Image 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ok-wEIiQEb0)
**Pro record**: 2-3

**Years active**: 2001-2007

Arguably the most recognizable MMA referee of all time, Herb Dean competed five times as a professional MMA fighter. Dean competed all over the map including bouts in the United States, United Kingdom, and South Korea. The most notable name on his record is Joe Riggs, who Dean fought 19 months prior to Riggs' UFC debut.

## Jerin Valel

![Image 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4tlhjI6374M)
**Pro record**: 2-1

**Years active**: 2003-2006

Canada-based official Jerin Valel has partaken in many UFC events as both a referee and an official – but he also competed three times as a professional MMA fighter. While no tape exists of these bouts, a grappling match against a youngster incorrectly called "Rory McDonell" in a decade-old YouTube video.

## Keith Peterson

![Image 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eapSn68cs4w)
**Amateur record**: 4-3

**Years active**: 2007-2008

Before Keith Peterson was "no nonsense" he was throwing punches on the New Jersey regional scene. In the span of 20 months, Peterson competed seven times. He won four and finished two. His career ended after a trilogy with a fighter named Jose Villanueva, who won the series 2-1. Villanueva went on to go 1-2-1 as a professional, as Peterson grinded his way to become one of the most used high-level officials in recent years.

# 6 frequently used UFC referees who competed as MMA fighters

Nolan King

USA TODAY Sports

May 23, 2023, 2:00 a.m. ET

[](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fmma%2F2023%2F05%2F23%2Fufc-referees-who-fought-mma-dean-goddard-peterson-grice-trigg%2F81207296007%2F&text=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters&via=MMAJunkie)[](mailto:?subject=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters%20-%20from%20MMA%20Junkie&body=6%20frequently%20used%20UFC%20referees%20who%20competed%20as%20MMA%20fighters%0A%0AThe%20third%20man%20in%20the%20cage%20isn't%20why%20the%20masses%20tune%20in%20to%20watch%20fights.%20However%2C%20officials%20used%20by%20major%20promotions%20on%20a%20frequent%20basis%20often%20rack%20up%20more%20cage-time%20on%20international%20airwaves%20than%20the%20athletes%20they%20oversee.%20Week%20after%20week%2C%20the%20officials%20grace%20the%20streams%20of%E2%80%A6%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20mmajunkie.usatoday.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fmma%2F2023%2F05%2F23%2Fufc-referees-who-fought-mma-dean-goddard-peterson-grice-trigg%2F81207296007%2F)

![Image 1](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/03/03/SMMA/81207264007-91-2575422.png?width=660&height=440&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)
The third man in the cage isn't why the masses tune in to watch fights.

However, officials used by major promotions on a frequent basis often rack up more cage-time on international airwaves than the athletes they oversee.

Week after week, the officials grace the streams of MMA fans around the world. With that, a sense of familiarity is built. They become household names among viewers.

While they may have gained fame through officiating fights, many referees got started as competitors themselves – just check the tape.

Buried in the bowels of YouTube are some of the most popular referees in MMA today throwing punches, kicks, and elbows. Scroll below to watch six referees frequently used by the UFC, Bellator, and PFL compete in MMA bouts.

## Frank Trigg

![Image 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hwa__ZAtTVA)
**Pro record**: 21-9

**Years active**: 1997-2011

OK, so this is perhaps the most obvious of the bunch. Out of all the MMA referees who populate the realm of major promotional regularity, Frank Trigg has the most impressive competitor resume. He competed seven times in the UFC and challenged for the promotion's welterweight championship twice. He retired from competition in 2011 and debuted as a referee in 2014.

## Marc Goddard

![Image 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wYhj5KIPxSM)
**Pro record**: 7-6-1

**Years active**: 2002-2008

The most familiar face in European MMA refereeing is now one of the most universally used officials in the game today. Though his rise to notoriety came on the officiating side, Marc Goddard competed 14 times as a professional MMA fighter from his debut in 2002 up until his competitive retirement in 2008. He competed for Cage Warriors and Cage Rage, among other promotions.

## Blake Grice

![Image 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xJObrHLRfgE)
**Amateur record**: 3-1

**Years active**: 2001-2003

Over the past few years, Blake Grice has established himself in the "big leagues" of MMA officiating. A respected referee, judge, and instructor, Grice has been the overseer of his fair share of major promotional bouts. While he never competed professionally, Grice compiled a 3-1 record as an amateur prior to his officiating days.

## Herb Dean

![Image 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ok-wEIiQEb0)
**Pro record**: 2-3

**Years active**: 2001-2007

Arguably the most recognizable MMA referee of all time, Herb Dean competed five times as a professional MMA fighter. Dean competed all over the map including bouts in the United States, United Kingdom, and South Korea. The most notable name on his record is Joe Riggs, who Dean fought 19 months prior to Riggs' UFC debut.

## Jerin Valel

![Image 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4tlhjI6374M)
**Pro record**: 2-1

**Years active**: 2003-2006

Canada-based official Jerin Valel has partaken in many UFC events as both a referee and an official – but he also competed three times as a professional MMA fighter. While no tape exists of these bouts, a grappling match against a youngster incorrectly called "Rory McDonell" in a decade-old YouTube video.

## Keith Peterson

![Image 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eapSn68cs4w)
**Amateur record**: 4-3

**Years active**: 2007-2008

Before Keith Peterson was "no nonsense" he was throwing punches on the New Jersey regional scene. In the span of 20 months, Peterson competed seven times. He won four and finished two. His career ended after a trilogy with a fighter named Jose Villanueva, who won the series 2-1. Villanueva went on to go 1-2-1 as a professional, as Peterson grinded his way to become one of the most used high-level officials in recent years.

### “Big” John McCarthy

Mixed Martial Arts (MMA)

*   Refereed thousands of bouts worldwide, including hundreds of Bellator and UFC bouts.

*   Refereed for various global organizations, including K-1, Strikeforce, Affliction, Bellator, King of the Cage, RIZIN, and others.

*   Over the past 30 years, has been a licensed Referee throughout the United States, Canada, and countries worldwide.

*   A key figure in drafting MMA's Unified Rules, recognized by ABC and Athletic Commissions nationwide in America.

*   Certified MMA Referee & Judging Instructor for the Association of Boxing Commissions (ABC).

*   Former Color commentator and member of the broadcast team for Bellator and PFL

Recognitions

*   Awarded Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt in 2006.

*   Inducted into the Master's Hall of Fame in 2006 for “Outstanding Achievements in the Martial Arts.”

*   The first recipient of the 2008 World MMA Awards “Lifetime Achievement” accolade, voted on by the sport's top journalists, and the only person to win the award twice, winning the award again in 2018.

*   Awarded 2007 commendation by Senator James Battin for “Career Accomplishments” in MMA, “for the work done to increase the safety, visibility, and importance of Mixed Martial Arts.”

*   Awarded 2007 proclamation by the California State Athletic Commission for “Dedication and commitment to other officials in helping develop their skills and concern for athletes.”

*   Awarded"Best Referee"award at the World MMA Awards three times; in 2015, 2016 and, 2017.

*   Author of “Let’s Get It On - Making of MMA and its Ultimate Referee.”

### Mike Beltran

*   Retired veteran with 32 years of law enforcement experience with the Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department (LASD) and 6 years with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)

*   Referee and Judge experience since 2004

*   Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt

*   Refereed numerous major MMA world title fights, with the UFC and other organizations

*   ABC certified Referee and Judge

*   Helped teach at the ABC conference

*   Trained by Big John McCarthy since the beginning of his officiating career

*   Testified at the State of California Capitol Building as a subject matter expert to pass legislation for fighters with regard to pension plans and self-defense assembly bills

*   Helped teach Command Courses and taught courses in Spanish in Mexico

*   Fluent Spanish speaker

### Ron McCarthy

*   Professional MMA Judge since 2011.

*   One of the world's top 10 most active Judges, judging Championship and main event bouts for the UFC,

Bellator, PFL, and other high-level organizations.

*   Judge for professional kickboxing and Muay Thai.

*   Passed the COMMAND Judging Course in 2009 and worked amateur fights with the California Amateur MMA Organization (CAMO) throughout the state.

*   Lifelong immersion in the world of MMA.

*   BJJ blue belt.

*   ABC-certified as an MMA Judge.

*   Instructor for judging courses for C.O.M.M.A.N.D. since 2024.

Mixed Martial Arts (MMA)

# Decade in Review – 2017

A look back at the best Octagon moments from 2017

 By Thomas Gerbasi, on Twitter: @TGerbasi • Dec. 30, 2019 

Big news from inside and outside the Octagon filled headlines in 2016, setting a high bar for 2017 to follow, but the UFC was not intimidated in the slightest by such expectations. In fact, it came out firing after a pair of January shows with its first visit to Brooklyn, New York in February.

On that UFC 208 card in Barclays Center, the promotion’s newest division crowned its first champion, as Germaine de Randamie outpointed Holly Holm to win the women’s featherweight crown. Also on the card, it was a good night for Brazil, as Anderson Silva, Glover Teixeira, “Jacare” Souza and Wilson Reis all notched wins for the South American MMA hotbed.

In March, Las Vegas hosted its first event of the year, with Tyron Woodley retaining his welterweight title via decision in his UFC 209 rematch against Stephen Thompson.

Following international stops in Fortaleza and London, the Octagon arrived in Buffalo in April, where upstate New York fans saw Daniel Cormier return to submit Anthony Johnson and retain his light heavyweight title. A week later, the Mighty Mouse train kept on rollin’ as flyweight champ Demetrious Johnson added another successful title defense to his record by submitting Wilson Reis.

May saw two more champs keep their belts intact, as Stipe Miocic defeated Junior Dos Santos and Joanna Jedrzejczyk beat Jessica Andrade, and in June, Max Holloway made it official as he stopped Jose Aldo in Rio to become the undisputed featherweight champion of the world.

![Image 2: Max Holloway punches Jose Aldo of Brazil in their UFC featherweight championship bout during the UFC 212 event at Jeunesse Arena on June 3, 2017 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)](https://ufc.com/images/styles/inline/s3/2019-12/GettyImages-692067200.jpg?VersionId=y3YeXlTHemUbCDGMAxi_ZEdEbAMw2OI4&itok=2Jy70LH3)

 Max Holloway punches Jose Aldo of Brazil in their UFC featherweight championship bout during the UFC 212 event at Jeunesse Arena on June 3, 2017 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images) 

* * *

It had been a fairly quiet first half of the year in the Octagon, but business picked up considerably on International Fight Week, as Justin Gaethje made his long-awaited UFC debut with a Fight of the Year stoppage of Michael Johnson on July 7. That same night, Jesse Taylor won The Ultimate Fighter: Redemption Finale by submitting Dhiego Lima.

The day after that event, Robert Whittaker won the interim middleweight title with a Fight of the Night victory over Yoel Romero in the main event of UFC 213, a bout elevated to that spot when Amanda Nunes was forced out of her bout with Valentina Shevchenko due to illness.

On the Tuesday after UFC 213, it was the premiere of Dana White’s Tuesday Night Contender Series, a show designed to showcase the best up and coming talent from around the world, with memorable performances often earning the winners a UFC contract. Emerging from season one of the DWCS with UFC contracts were the likes of Sean O’Malley, Karl Roberson, Geoff Neal, Grant Dawson and Matt Frevola.

But the July action wasn’t finished yet, as the long-awaited rematch between Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier headlined UFC 214 on July 29 in Anaheim. Again, it was Jones emerging victorious, but he would see the win and his title disappear after a failed drug test.

Also on the card, Cris Cyborg won the women’s featherweight title stripped from Germaine de Ramdamie when she stopped Tonya Evinger, and Woodley retained his 170-pound title with a decision win over Demian Maia.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5NBTDn_8VZc)

Following visits to Mexico City and Rotterdam, Nunes and Shevchenko finally got their rematch in Edmonton on September 9, and in the main event of UFC 215, it was “The Lioness” eking out a split decision win over Shevchenko. And though the loss was disappointing for “Bullet,” she would soon have a new title to chase, as The Ultimate Fighter: A New World Champion introduced the women’s flyweight division with a tournament that would crown a UFC champion.

If you’re wondering where Conor McGregor was at this point in the year, don’t worry, he was around, just not in the Octagon, as “The Notorious” one faced off with future boxing hall of famer Floyd Mayweather Jr. in an August 26 boxing match that captivated the world. McGregor would get stopped by Mayweather in the tenth round, but he impressed observers with his showing in his first professional boxing match.

Back in the Octagon, Tony Ferguson submitted Kevin Lee to win the interim lightweight title, while Johnson set the record for most successful title defenses in UFC history with the Submission of the Year over Ray Borg at UFC 216 on October 7.

![Image 3: Tony Ferguson celebrates after his submission victory over Kevin Lee in their interim UFC lightweight championship bout during the UFC 216 event inside T-Mobile Arena on October 7, 2017 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)](https://ufc.com/images/styles/inline/s3/2019-12/GettyImages-858851306.jpg?VersionId=TbuxlYMl5wJQuiEzeSOcmbLPVBnrJD2e&itok=aaoZpkVE)

 Tony Ferguson celebrates after his submission victory over Kevin Lee in their interim UFC lightweight championship bout during the UFC 216 event inside T-Mobile Arena on October 7, 2017 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC via Getty Imag 

* * *

In November, the UFC returned to Madison Square Garden with another stacked card, and three titles changed hands, as Georges St-Pierre returned from nearly four years away to take the middleweight belt from Michael Bisping, TJ Dillashaw knocked out former teammate Cody Garbrandt for the bantamweight crown, and Rose Namajunas upset Jedrzejczyk for the strawweight title.

It was a wild month for sure, but December got off to a wild beginning as well, as unheralded Nicco Montano completed her run through the TUF 26 field with a win over Roxanne Modafferi that earned her the UFC women’s flyweight title. The next night, Holloway bested Aldo a second time while Francis Ngannou scored a stunning knockout of Alistair Overeem.

The final card of 2017 was in Las Vegas, and in the main event of UFC 219, Cyborg cemented her place as the best female fighter in the game with a decision victory over Holm to retain her women’s featherweight title.

Bring on 2018.

# Decade in Review – 2017

A look back at the best Octagon moments from 2017

 By Thomas Gerbasi, on Twitter: @TGerbasi • Dec. 30, 2019 

Big news from inside and outside the Octagon filled headlines in 2016, setting a high bar for 2017 to follow, but the UFC was not intimidated in the slightest by such expectations. In fact, it came out firing after a pair of January shows with its first visit to Brooklyn, New York in February.

On that UFC 208 card in Barclays Center, the promotion’s newest division crowned its first champion, as Germaine de Randamie outpointed Holly Holm to win the women’s featherweight crown. Also on the card, it was a good night for Brazil, as Anderson Silva, Glover Teixeira, “Jacare” Souza and Wilson Reis all notched wins for the South American MMA hotbed.

In March, Las Vegas hosted its first event of the year, with Tyron Woodley retaining his welterweight title via decision in his UFC 209 rematch against Stephen Thompson.

Following international stops in Fortaleza and London, the Octagon arrived in Buffalo in April, where upstate New York fans saw Daniel Cormier return to submit Anthony Johnson and retain his light heavyweight title. A week later, the Mighty Mouse train kept on rollin’ as flyweight champ Demetrious Johnson added another successful title defense to his record by submitting Wilson Reis.

May saw two more champs keep their belts intact, as Stipe Miocic defeated Junior Dos Santos and Joanna Jedrzejczyk beat Jessica Andrade, and in June, Max Holloway made it official as he stopped Jose Aldo in Rio to become the undisputed featherweight champion of the world.

![Image 2: Max Holloway punches Jose Aldo of Brazil in their UFC featherweight championship bout during the UFC 212 event at Jeunesse Arena on June 3, 2017 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)](https://ufc.com/images/styles/inline/s3/2019-12/GettyImages-692067200.jpg?VersionId=y3YeXlTHemUbCDGMAxi_ZEdEbAMw2OI4&itok=2Jy70LH3)

 Max Holloway punches Jose Aldo of Brazil in their UFC featherweight championship bout during the UFC 212 event at Jeunesse Arena on June 3, 2017 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images) 

* * *

It had been a fairly quiet first half of the year in the Octagon, but business picked up considerably on International Fight Week, as Justin Gaethje made his long-awaited UFC debut with a Fight of the Year stoppage of Michael Johnson on July 7. That same night, Jesse Taylor won The Ultimate Fighter: Redemption Finale by submitting Dhiego Lima.

The day after that event, Robert Whittaker won the interim middleweight title with a Fight of the Night victory over Yoel Romero in the main event of UFC 213, a bout elevated to that spot when Amanda Nunes was forced out of her bout with Valentina Shevchenko due to illness.

On the Tuesday after UFC 213, it was the premiere of Dana White’s Tuesday Night Contender Series, a show designed to showcase the best up and coming talent from around the world, with memorable performances often earning the winners a UFC contract. Emerging from season one of the DWCS with UFC contracts were the likes of Sean O’Malley, Karl Roberson, Geoff Neal, Grant Dawson and Matt Frevola.

But the July action wasn’t finished yet, as the long-awaited rematch between Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier headlined UFC 214 on July 29 in Anaheim. Again, it was Jones emerging victorious, but he would see the win and his title disappear after a failed drug test.

Also on the card, Cris Cyborg won the women’s featherweight title stripped from Germaine de Ramdamie when she stopped Tonya Evinger, and Woodley retained his 170-pound title with a decision win over Demian Maia.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5NBTDn_8VZc)

Following visits to Mexico City and Rotterdam, Nunes and Shevchenko finally got their rematch in Edmonton on September 9, and in the main event of UFC 215, it was “The Lioness” eking out a split decision win over Shevchenko. And though the loss was disappointing for “Bullet,” she would soon have a new title to chase, as The Ultimate Fighter: A New World Champion introduced the women’s flyweight division with a tournament that would crown a UFC champion.

If you’re wondering where Conor McGregor was at this point in the year, don’t worry, he was around, just not in the Octagon, as “The Notorious” one faced off with future boxing hall of famer Floyd Mayweather Jr. in an August 26 boxing match that captivated the world. McGregor would get stopped by Mayweather in the tenth round, but he impressed observers with his showing in his first professional boxing match.

Back in the Octagon, Tony Ferguson submitted Kevin Lee to win the interim lightweight title, while Johnson set the record for most successful title defenses in UFC history with the Submission of the Year over Ray Borg at UFC 216 on October 7.

![Image 3: Tony Ferguson celebrates after his submission victory over Kevin Lee in their interim UFC lightweight championship bout during the UFC 216 event inside T-Mobile Arena on October 7, 2017 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)](https://ufc.com/images/styles/inline/s3/2019-12/GettyImages-858851306.jpg?VersionId=TbuxlYMl5wJQuiEzeSOcmbLPVBnrJD2e&itok=aaoZpkVE)

 Tony Ferguson celebrates after his submission victory over Kevin Lee in their interim UFC lightweight championship bout during the UFC 216 event inside T-Mobile Arena on October 7, 2017 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC via Getty Imag 

* * *

In November, the UFC returned to Madison Square Garden with another stacked card, and three titles changed hands, as Georges St-Pierre returned from nearly four years away to take the middleweight belt from Michael Bisping, TJ Dillashaw knocked out former teammate Cody Garbrandt for the bantamweight crown, and Rose Namajunas upset Jedrzejczyk for the strawweight title.

It was a wild month for sure, but December got off to a wild beginning as well, as unheralded Nicco Montano completed her run through the TUF 26 field with a win over Roxanne Modafferi that earned her the UFC women’s flyweight title. The next night, Holloway bested Aldo a second time while Francis Ngannou scored a stunning knockout of Alistair Overeem.

The final card of 2017 was in Las Vegas, and in the main event of UFC 219, Cyborg cemented her place as the best female fighter in the game with a decision victory over Holm to retain her women’s featherweight title.

Bring on 2018.
